title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯秋八月天下當論
士于鄉御史敖鯤奉
上命按福建得監臨簾內外事簾
以內以所禮聘棕暨敎諭丘
龍雲司考試張榆熊汝諧陳
時進蔣自亮張邦燮周相成
===
張承禮訓導李遠蘇良輔經
仁謙同試事簾以外則左布
政使沈人种右布政使吳文
佳司提調按察使蔡汝賢副
使姚體信司監試它百職事
咸慎簡以充屆期御史齋祓
祗禔
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯秋八月，天下當論士于鄉。御史敖鯤奉上命按福建，得監臨簾內外事。簾以內，以所禮聘棕暨敎諭丘龍雲司考試，張榆、熊汝諧、陳時進、蔣自亮、張邦燮、周相成、張承禮，訓導李遠、蘇良輔、經仁謙同試事；簾以外，則左布政使沈人种、右布政使吳文佳司提調，按察使蔡汝賢、副使姚體信司監試，它百職事咸慎簡以充。屆期，御史齋祓，祗禔
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the jimao year of the Wanli era (1579), the empire was due to evaluate scholars in the provinces. Investigating Censor Ao Kun 敖鯤, having received the Emperor's command to inspect Fujian as Regional Inspector, was authorized to act as Supervising Official for affairs both inside and outside the curtain. Inside the curtain, I, Zong [? 棕], who had been courteously invited, together with Instructor Qiu Longyun 丘龍雲, took charge as Examiners; while Zhang Yu 張榆, Xiong Ruxie 熊汝諧, Chen Shijin 陳時進, Jiang Ziliang 蔣自亮, Zhang Bangxie 張邦燮, Zhou Xiangcheng 周相成, and Zhang Chengli 張承禮, along with Assistant Instructors Li Yuan 李遠, Su Liangfu 蘇良輔, and Jing Renqian 經仁謙, served jointly as Associate Examiners. Outside the curtain, Left Administration Commissioner Shen Renzhong 沈人种 and Right Administration Commissioner Wu Wenjia 吳文佳 took charge as Proctors; Surveillance Commissioner Cai Ruxian 蔡汝賢 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Yao Tixin 姚體信 took charge as Monitoring Officials; and all the various other functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. When the appointed time arrived, the Investigating Censor fasted and purified himself, reverently upholding [? 祗禔]…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
明命而昭告之儼焉若臨百職事
歔然肅慮就列已乃進提學
僉事趙參魯及署提學事僉
事鄭宗學先後所遴士二千
七百有奇三試抜雋者九十
籍
奏之棕以故事宜序首簡棕竊
===
聞諸搢紳學士譚者僉曰閩
海濱鄒魯云夫鄒魯帶甲之
雄不敵齊楚阨塞之險不踰
秦晉譚者率稱鄒魯鄒魯則
以孔孟之故矣廼閩故南徼
之裔疆也周職方列諸荒服
而玆得與鄒魯齒何昉也粤
punctuated:
明命，而昭告之，儼焉若臨。百職事歔然肅慮就列。已，乃進提學僉事趙參魯及署提學事僉事鄭宗學先後所遴士二千七百有奇，三試，抜雋者九十，籍奏之。棕以故事宜序首簡。

棕竊聞諸搢紳學士譚者，僉曰：「閩，海濱鄒魯」云。夫鄒、魯帶甲之雄不敵齊、楚，阨塞之險不踰秦、晉，譚者率稱「鄒魯、鄒魯」，則以孔、孟之故矣。廼閩故南徼之裔疆也，周職方列諸荒服，而玆得與鄒、魯齒，何昉也？粤
translation_en:
… the illustrious mandate, and made a solemn declaration of it, awe-inspiring as though the throne were present in person. The various functionaries, reverent and solemn in thought, took their places in the ranks. Thereafter, the more than two thousand seven hundred scholars who had been successively selected by Zhao Canlu 趙參魯, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education, and Zheng Zongxue 鄭宗學, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Acting in Charge of Education, were admitted. Through three examination sessions, ninety outstanding candidates were chosen, and their names were registered and memorialized to the throne. In accordance with precedent, I, [Gao] Zong 高棕, ought to write a preface for the opening pages.

I have humbly heard what the gentry and scholarly gentlemen say in their discussions; they all declare that "Min [Fujian] is the Zou and Lu of the seashore." Now, in the might of its armored soldiers, Zou and Lu could not match Qi and Chu, and in the strategic impregnability of its mountain passes, they did not surpass Qin and Jin; yet when discussants speak of them, they invariably praise "Zou and Lu, Zou and Lu"—this is solely because of Confucius and Mencius. Yet Min was originally a remote borderland on the southern frontier, which the职方 (Zhifang, Directorate of Dependencies) of the Zhou dynasty ranked among the wild domains (huangfu); how did it begin that it is now able to be ranked alongside Zou and Lu? Looking back…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
自楊中立氏北學洛下與聞
孔孟之道載之以南嗣是仲
素愿中承傳以及考亭益闡
而恢張之於是建溪鐔浦之
間述孔業者雲蒸嚮臻宛然
斷斷之遺風矣然諸儒資不
逢世維時譚者即欲躋閩於
===
鄒魯世不盡然也惟我
明興稽古定制一以經術論士罷
詘百家言學庸語孟易詩顓
主朱氏說尚書主蔡氏說春
秋主胡氏說著為
功令敷天之下治博士業者不
得異學
punctuated: 自楊中立氏北學洛下，與聞孔孟之道，載之以南。嗣是仲素、愿中承傳，以及考亭，益闡而恢張之。於是建溪、鐔浦之間，述孔業者雲蒸嚮臻，宛然斷斷之遺風矣。然諸儒資不逢世，維時譚者即欲躋閩於鄒、魯，世不盡然也。惟我明興，稽古定制，一以經術論士，罷詘百家言。《學》、《庸》、《語》、《孟》、《易》、《詩》顓主朱氏說，《尚書》主蔡氏說，《春秋》主胡氏說，著為功令，敷天之下，治博士業者不得異學。
translation_en: …since Yang Shi 楊時 (courtesy name Zhongli 中立) traveled north to study in Luoyang, heard the Way of Confucius and Mencius, and carried it back south. Thereafter, Luo Congyan 羅從彥 (courtesy name Zhongsu 仲素) and Li Tong 李侗 (courtesy name Yuanzhong 愿中) carried on the transmission down to Zhu Xi 朱熹 of Kaoting 考亭, who further elucidated and expanded it. Thereupon, in the region between Jianxi 建溪 and Tanpu 鐔浦 (Nanping), those who transmitted the teachings of Confucius rose up like gathering clouds and converged in response, truly evoking the ancient ethos of earnest devotion and debate. Yet these Confucian scholars did not meet with favorable times; even if commentators of that era wished to elevate Min (Fujian) to the rank of Zou and Lu, the world did not entirely agree. Only with the rise of our Ming dynasty, which examined antiquity to establish its institutions, were scholars evaluated solely on the basis of mastery of the Classics, while the doctrines of the Hundred Schools were dismissed and rejected. For the Great Learning (Daxue), the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), the Analects (Lunyu), the Mencius (Mengzi), the Book of Changes (Yijing), and the Book of Odes (Shijing), the commentaries of Master Zhu (Zhu Xi) were made the sole authority; for the Book of Documents (Shangshu), the commentary of Master Cai (Cai Shen 蔡沈) was made the authority; and for the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), the commentary of Master Hu (Hu Anguo 胡安國) was made the authority. This was codified into the official examination regulations, so that throughout the entire realm, those pursuing the curriculum of the Erudites were not permitted to follow heterodox teachings. …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承迪之爲憲卽
上黼座之前儒臣之所陳啓下寓
縣之内章縫之所呫嗶壹閩
産儒先所述也由斯以譚閩
學之盛第之鄒魯不虛哉夫
濱産者善沒巖棲者易險習
故也諸人士生長玆邦承服
===
師說而漸靡之者習矣玆締
觀其文率根理要中繩幅蔚
然不詭於訓故有以也雖然
諸儒之學雖不偶於時而顧
大顯于
熈朝章章若斯者非獨其博綜之
勤著述之富已也夷考其履
punctuated: 列聖相承，迪之爲憲。卽上黼座之前，儒臣之所陳啓；下寓縣之内，章縫之所呫嗶，壹閩産儒先所述也。由斯以譚，閩學之盛，第之鄒、魯，不虛哉！夫濱産者善沒，巖棲者易險，習故也。諸人士生長玆邦，承服師說而漸靡之者習矣。玆締觀其文，率根理要，中繩幅，蔚然不詭於訓故，有以也。雖然，諸儒之學，雖不偶於時，而顧大顯于熈朝，章章若斯者，非獨其博綜之勤、著述之富已也。夷考其履，
translation_en: The successive sacred emperors have inherited this tradition, following it as their standard. Thus, above, before the imperial throne, what the Confucian officials expound and present; and below, throughout the empire, what the robed scholars chant and study, are all without exception the transmissions of the former Confucian masters born in Min [Fujian]. Discussed in this light, to rank the flourishing of Min learning alongside that of Zou and Lu is surely no empty claim! Now, those born by the water's edge excel at diving, and those who dwell among the crags treat precipices lightly; this is because of habituation. The scholars and gentlemen born and raised in this region have received and submitted to the teachings of their masters, becoming thoroughly steeped in them through long familiarity. Now, closely examining their essays, we find that they generally take the essential principles as their root, conform to the standards and rules, and are richly refined without deviating from the established glosses—there is indeed a reason for this. Nevertheless, although the learning of those Confucian masters did not meet with favor in their own time, the reason it has instead become so greatly illustrious in our glorious dynasty, shining forth as brilliantly as this, is not merely because of their diligence in broad synthesis or the richness of their writings. If we calmly examine their conduct…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
實亦志孔孟之道矣夫孔孟
之道具在六籍其要指歸於
求仁仁者人之所以人而天
下民物所爲同體者也漢唐
以降臻玆理者蓋尠洛下倡
明斯旨惟中立獨契其微承
傳者諸所詣不知奚若大都
===
闇然禔脩處則刻厲堅苦出
則忠誠勤恤所謂力行近仁
者非耶木難沉淵雖閟終媚
聘瑂韞谷輝卒末掩諸儒之
學大顯于
今日理有固然惜往矣未獲躬
逢之也而多士束髮受書第
punctuated: 實，亦志孔孟之道矣。夫孔孟之道，具在六籍，其要指歸於求仁。仁者，人之所以人，而天下民物所爲同體者也。漢、唐以降，臻玆理者蓋尠。洛下倡明斯旨，惟中立獨契其微。承傳者諸所詣，不知奚若，大都闇然禔脩，處則刻厲堅苦，出則忠誠勤恤，所謂「力行近仁」者非耶？木難沉淵，雖閟終媚；聘瑂韞谷，輝卒末掩。諸儒之學，大顯于今日，理有固然。惜往矣，未獲躬逢之也。而多士束髮受書，第
translation_en: … actual practice, they also set their minds on the Way of Confucius and Mencius. Now, the Way of Confucius and Mencius is fully contained in the Six Classics, and its essential purport comes down to seeking humaneness (ren). Humaneness is that by which a human being is human, and that whereby the people and creatures of the world form a single body. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, those who attained this principle were few indeed. When the scholars of Luoyang championed and elucidated this meaning, Yang Shi 楊時 (courtesy name Zhongli 中立) alone grasped its subtleties. As for the various levels of attainment among those who carried on his transmission, while one may not know exactly how they compared, in general they quietly cultivated themselves in peace: when living in retirement, they were rigorous, steadfast, and enduring of hardship; when serving in office, they were loyal, sincere, diligent, and compassionate. Is this not what is meant by "strenuous practice comes close to humaneness"? Though the munan gem sinks into the abyss and lies hidden, it retains its charm in the end; though prized jade [?] is concealed in the valley, its radiance can ultimately never be obscured. That the learning of these scholars has become illustriously manifest in the present day is only in the natural order of things. Alas, they have passed away and were not able to witness it in person! Yet the many scholars today, from the time they bound up their hair to receive instruction in the books, need only…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
通其緒論無失卽得登等籍
名太常行駸駸嚮用焉視諸
儒當時所遇何如哉夫諸儒
躬其道未躬其遇多士躬其
遇矣如不躬其道而徒勦其
緒餘以梯榮進是閩以諸儒
重而多士不能以閩重恥也
===
而多士承
澤仰流孔孟之道玆益大顯明何
論諸儒由今以往且有民物
之寄矣誠卽國故所述上遡
鄒魯之源反求而得其本心
則不爲不欲推之猶饑猶溺
若撻若溝亦自不容已已是
punctuated: 通其緒論無失，卽得登等，籍名太常，行駸駸嚮用焉。視諸儒當時所遇，何如哉？夫諸儒躬其道，未躬其遇；多士躬其遇矣，如不躬其道，而徒勦其緒餘以梯榮進，是閩以諸儒重，而多士不能以閩重，恥也。而多士承澤仰流，孔孟之道玆益大顯明，何論諸儒？由今以往，且有民物之寄矣。誠卽國故所述，上遡鄒魯之源，反求而得其本心，則不爲不欲，推之猶饑猶溺、若撻若溝，亦自不容已已。是
translation_en: …mastering their transmitted discourses without error, can immediately ascend the ranks, have their names registered in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and move swiftly toward official employment. How does this compare with the circumstances those Confucians encountered in their own times? Now, those Confucians practiced the Way in person, yet did not personally experience such favorable circumstances; you many scholars have personally experienced these favorable circumstances, yet if you do not practice their Way in person, and merely plagiarize their residual teachings as a ladder to栄誉 and advancement, then Fujian is held in esteem because of those Confucians, whereas you scholars cannot bring esteem to Fujian—what a disgrace! Moreover, as you scholars receive the imperial grace and look up to the intellectual current, the Way of Confucius and Mencius is now ever more greatly manifested and illuminated—what need is there even to speak of those earlier Confucians? From this day forward, you will furthermore be entrusted with the welfare of the people and all living things. If you truly take what is recounted in our dynastic traditions, trace it back up to its origins in Zou and Lu [the homelands of Mencius and Confucius], turn inward to seek and recover your original mind, then from what you refuse to do and refuse to desire, extending it until you feel others' hunger and drowning as your own, or feel as if you yourself had beaten them or pushed them into a ditch [if a single person is out of place], it too will naturally become something you cannot stop yourselves from doing. This…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
心也命之曰仁六經載籍雖
博總之敎人求是耳士誠志
是則躬且不有它何知焉斯
之謂一德不貳否則卑卑者
亡論卽矯然崇論閎議玄致
峻標爲名高耳謂民物何故
術不可不愼也
===
國家掄士爲民物計其
制一以經術意蓋如此子多士重
念哉重念哉毋曰此吾鄕耳
熟語也語曰非苟知之實允
蹈之棕謹執是爲久要云是
役也提督右僉都御史耿定
向飭武敷文章縫爲憲提督
punctuated:
心也，命之曰仁。六經載籍雖博，總之敎人求是耳。士誠志是，則躬且不有，它何知焉？斯之謂一德不貳。否則，卑卑者亡論，卽矯然崇論閎議、玄致峻標，爲名高耳，謂民物何？故術不可不愼也。國家掄士，爲民物計，其制一以經術，意蓋如此。子多士重念哉！重念哉！毋曰：「此吾鄕耳熟語也。」語曰：「非苟知之，實允蹈之。」棕謹執是爲久要云。
是役也，提督右僉都御史耿定向飭武敷文，章縫爲憲；提督
translation_en:
…mind, which is called benevolence (ren). Although the Six Classics and other texts are vast, in sum they simply teach people to seek this. If a scholar truly sets his will upon this, he does not even hold his own person dear—what else would he care to know? This is what is meant by "pure virtue without duplicity." Otherwise, setting aside those who are base and lowly, even those who ostentatiously engage in lofty discourses and grand arguments, or affect abstruse profundity and towering standards, are merely pursuing high reputation—what do they do for the people and all things? Therefore, one cannot but be cautious in one's art of learning. When the state selects scholars, it plans for the sake of the people and all things; that its system relies uniformly on mastery of the Classics is likely for this very reason. May you many scholars ponder this deeply! Ponder this deeply! Do not say, "These are just words we have heard all too often in our home region." As the saying goes, "It is not merely knowing it, but truly putting it into practice." I, [Gao] Zong 高棕, respectfully hold fast to this as an enduring pledge.

In this undertaking, Superintendent and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Geng Dingxiang 耿定向 regulated military affairs and spread civil culture, serving as a model for scholars in ceremonial dress; Superintendent…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
南贛右僉都御史蒙詔風教
夙孚紆猷遐漸鎮守總兵官
呼良朋綏疆重士而左給事
中蕭崇業行人謝杰弭節右
文以協賛則右叅政佘立左
叅議鄭汝璧右叅議聶廷璧
副使喬懋敬吳孔性僉事李
===
樂彭應時張對以防衛則副
總兵官侯繼高郭堅署都指
揮同知梅應魁署都指揮僉
事劉大勛吳憲秦經國方伯
以入
賀則左叅政王元敬副使歐希
稷署都指揮僉事萬達甫王
punctuated: 南贛右僉都御史蒙詔，風教夙孚，紆猷遐漸；鎮守總兵官呼良朋，綏疆重士；而左給事中蕭崇業、行人謝杰，弭節右文；以協賛則右叅政佘立、左叅議鄭汝璧、右叅議聶廷璧、副使喬懋敬、吳孔性、僉事李樂、彭應時、張對；以防衛則副總兵官侯繼高、郭堅、署都指揮同知梅應魁、署都指揮僉事劉大勛、吳憲、秦經國、方伯；以入賀則左叅政王元敬、副使歐希稷、署都指揮僉事萬達甫、王
translation_en: …of Nan-Gan, Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right Meng Zhao 蒙詔, whose moral teaching has long inspired trust and whose far-reaching counsels have gradually spread; Grand Defender and Regional Commander Hu Liangpeng 呼良朋, who pacifies the frontiers and values scholars; and Supervising Secretary of the Left Xiao Chongye 蕭崇業 and Messenger Xie Jie 謝杰, who halted their carriages here and esteemed culture. Those who assisted in the administration were Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right She Li 佘立, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Left Zheng Rubi 鄭汝璧, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right Nie Tingbi 聶廷璧, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Qiao Maojing 喬懋敬 and Wu Kongxing 吳孔性, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Li Le 李樂, Peng Yingshi 彭應時, and Zhang Dui 張對; those who handled security and defense were Vice Regional Commanders Hou Jigao 侯繼高 and Guo Jian 郭堅, Acting Vice Commander Mai Yingkui 梅應魁, and Acting Assistant Commanders Liu Daxun 劉大勛, Wu Xian 吳憲, Qin Jingguo 秦經國, and Fang Bo 方伯; and those who went to the court to offer congratulations were Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Wang Yuanjing 王元敬, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ou Xiji 歐希稷, and Acting Assistant Commanders Wan Dafu 萬達甫 and Wang…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
有麟先事揆度均有勞焉例
得竝書
湖廣黃州府麻城縣儒學敎
諭姚棕謹序
punctuated:
有麟，先事揆度，均有勞焉，例得竝書。
湖廣黃州府麻城縣儒學敎諭姚棕謹序。
translation_en:
…Youlin, who planned and deliberated in advance of the affair, all contributed their efforts, and by precedent their names may be recorded together.
Respectfully prefaced by Yao Zong 姚棕, Instructor of the Confucian School of Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
萬曆七年福建鄉試
監臨官

Kong Wenren 孔聞仁, Unclassified Magistrate (dianshi) of Sha County in Yanping Prefecture (courtesy name Zhiren 知任, a native of Linchuan County, Jiangxi, who entered service as a lesser functionary [liyuan]).
Lu Yingji 盧應機, Postal Relay Station Master (yicheng) of Sanshan Postal Relay Station in Fuzhou Prefecture (courtesy name Fengbo 逢伯, a native of Dongguan County, Guangdong, who entered service as a courier [chengchai]).

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
素以為絢兮何謂也子曰繪事後素曰禮
後乎子曰起予者商也始可與言詩已
矣
浩浩其天
孟子曰雞鳴而起孳孳為善者舜之徒也
易
知至至之可與幾也
===
六四井甃无咎象曰井甃无咎脩井也九
五井洌寒泉食象曰寒泉之食中正也
上六井收勿幕有孚元吉象曰元吉在
上大成也
安土敦乎仁故能愛
兌正秋也
書
禹曰都帝慎乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止
惟幾惟康其弼直
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「『素以為絢兮』，何謂也？」子曰：「繪事後素。」曰：「禮後乎？」子曰：「起予者商也，始可與言《詩》已矣。」

浩浩其天。

孟子曰：「雞鳴而起，孳孳為善者，舜之徒也。」

易

知至至之，可與幾也。

六四：井甃，无咎。《象》曰：「井甃无咎」，脩井也。九五：井洌，寒泉食。《象》曰：「寒泉之食」，中正也。上六：井收勿幕，有孚元吉。《象》曰：「元吉在上」，大成也。

安土敦乎仁，故能愛。

兌，正秋也。

書

禹曰：「都！帝，慎乃在位。」帝曰：「俞！」禹曰：「安汝止，惟幾惟康，其弼直。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"'Plain silk to make the pattern bright'—what does this mean?" The Master said, "The business of painting comes after the plain groundwork." Zi Xia said, "Then ritual comes afterward?" The Master said, "It is Shang who brings out my meaning! Now I can begin to speak of the Odes with him indeed." [Analects 3.8]

Vast and boundless is his Heaven! [Doctrine of the Mean 32]

Mencius said, "He who rises at cockcrow and diligently seeks to do good is a follower of Shun." [Mencius 7A.25]

Classic of Changes (Yijing)

Knowing what is to be reached and reaching it, one can deal with the subtle incipient tendencies. [Hexagram 1, Qian, Wenyan Commentary]

Six in the fourth place: The well is being lined with tile; no blame. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'The well is being lined with tile; no blame'—this means repairing the well." Nine in the fifth place: In the well is a clear, cold spring from which one can drink. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Drinking from the cold spring'—this is because it is central and correct." Six at the top: The well is drawn from without being covered; there is sincerity and supreme good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Supreme good fortune at the top'—this is the great completion." [Hexagram 48, Jing]

Abiding in peace on the earth and earnest in benevolence, he is therefore able to love. [Great Treatise (Xici) I.4]

Dui (The Joyous) is mid-autumn. [Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua) 5]

Classic of Documents (Shujing)

Yu said, "Oh! Emperor, be cautious regarding the throne you occupy." The Emperor said, "Yes!" Yu said, "Rest calmly in the point where you should abide; attend to the subtle springs of things and to peaceful stability, and let your assistants be upright." [Yi and Ji (Yi Ji)]

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
若網在綱有條而不紊
曰王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日歲月日
時無易百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家
用平康
世篤忠貞服勞王家
詩
三之日于耜四之日舉趾同我婦子饁彼
南畝田畯至喜七月流火九月授衣春
日載陽有鳴倉庚女執懿筐遵彼微行
===
爰求柔桑春日遲遲采蘩祁祁
樂只君子天子葵之
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
至于海邦淮夷蠻貊及彼南夷莫不率從
莫敢不諾
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕秋
公會宋人齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕
punctuated:
若網在綱，有條而不紊。
曰：「王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。歲月日時無易，百穀用成，乂用明，俊民用章，家用平康。」
世篤忠貞，服勞王家。
詩
三之日于耜，四之日舉趾。同我婦子，饁彼南畝，田畯至喜。七月流火，九月授衣。春日載陽，有鳴倉庚。女執懿筐，遵彼微行，爰求柔桑。春日遲遲，采蘩祁祁。
樂只君子，天子葵之。
思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。
至于海邦，淮夷蠻貊，及彼南夷，莫不率從，莫敢不諾。
春秋
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕；秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕；
translation_en:
"When a net is attached to its head-rope, every strand is in order and there is no confusion."
"It is said: 'What the king scrutinizes is the year; the ministers and officers, the month; the heads of the lower officials, the day. When in the year, the month, and the day, the seasonable conditions do not change, the hundred grains mature, administration becomes enlightened, men of outstanding ability are distinguished, and the royal house enjoys peace and tranquility.'"
"From generation to generation your family has been steadfast in loyalty and integrity, toiling in the service of the royal house."
Classic of Odes (Shi)
"In the days of the third month they repair the plowshares; in the days of the fourth month they step out to the fields. Together with my wife and children, I carry food to those southern acres; the surveyor of the fields comes and is pleased. In the seventh month the Fire Star declines; in the ninth month clothes are given out. In the spring days the warmth begins, and the orioles sing. The young women take their deep baskets and follow those small paths to seek the tender mulberry leaves. The spring days lengthen out; they gather the white southernwood in crowds."
"Happy be the lord! The Son of Heaven measures his merits."
"Reverent and dignified was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving was she toward Zhou Jiang, a wife in the capital house. Tai Si inherited her fair renown, and so bore a hundred sons."
"Even unto the states along the sea, the tribes of the Huai, the Man and the Mo, and those southern Yi—none fail to follow and obey, none dare not answer to his call."
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In autumn, men of Song, men of Qi, and men of Zhu attacked Ni" [fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang]; "In autumn, the Duke met with men of Song and men of Qi to attack Xu" [twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang]; …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
公會齊人宋人救鄭莊公二十有八年
齊人救邢閔公元年
春晉侯侵曹晉侯伐衛僖公二十有八年
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒成公九年秋楚公
子壬夫帥師侵宋襄公元年
齊人歸讙及闡哀公八年
禮記
禹湯文武成王周公由此其選也
灌以圭璋用玉氣也
===
故商者五帝之遺聲也商人識之故謂之
商齊者三代之遺聲也齊人識之故謂
之齊
天子修男敎父道也
第貳場
論
養心莫善於寡欲
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔後元年
punctuated:
公會齊人、宋人救鄭，莊公二十有八年。
「齊人救邢」，閔公元年。
「春，晉侯侵曹，晉侯伐衛」，僖公二十有八年。
「楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒」，成公九年；「秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋」，襄公元年。
「齊人歸讙及闡」，哀公八年。

《禮記》
「禹、湯、文、武、成王、周公，由此其選也。」
「灌以圭璋，用玉氣也。」
「故商者，五帝之遺聲也，商人識之，故謂之商；齊者，三代之遺聲也，齊人識之，故謂之齊。」
「天子修男敎，父道也。」

第貳場
論
「養心莫善於寡欲」
詔、誥、表內科一道
擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔，後元年。
translation_en:
… the Duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to rescue Zheng" (twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang).
"Men of Qi rescued Xing" (first year of Duke Min).
"In spring, the Marquis of Jin invaded Cao; the Marquis of Jin attacked Wei" (twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi).
"Prince Yingqi of Chu led an army to attack Ju" (ninth year of Duke Cheng); "In autumn, Prince Renfu of Chu led an army to invade Song" (first year of Duke Xiang).
"Men of Qi returned Huan and Chan" (eighth year of Duke Ai).

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, King Cheng, and the Duke of Zhou were because of this the outstanding ones among them."
"In pouring the libation, one uses the gui and zhang jade tablets, making use of the vital essence of jade."
"Therefore, the Shang airs are the surviving sounds of the Five Emperors; the people of Shang remembered them, and so they are called Shang. The Qi airs are the surviving sounds of the Three Dynasties; the people of Qi remembered them, and so they are called Qi."
"The Son of Heaven cultivates the teachings for men, which is the way of the father."

Second Session
Discourse
"For nourishing the mind, nothing is better than making desires few."

Imperial Edict (zhao), Imperial Mandate (gao), or Memorial (biao) (choose one):
Compose an imperial edict in imitation of the Han dynasty deliberating on measures that might assist the common people (first year of the Houyuan era [163 BCE]).

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以房玄齡爲太傅誥〔貞觀十七年〕
擬輔臣奉
旨撰
進
雝肅殿箴
命書
御屏賀表
判語〔五條〕
漏用鈔印
===
收支留難
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
冒破物料
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問仲尼述文武之政不啻備矣乃其明要
在修身取人故志古所以自鏡也顯賢
所以自輔也至如陳鑑書屏義則何居
punctuated:
擬唐以房玄齡爲太傅誥〔貞觀十七年〕。
擬輔臣奉旨撰進《雝肅殿箴》，命書御屏賀表。

判語〔五條〕：
漏用鈔印。
收支留難。
禁止迎送。
優恤軍屬。
冒破物料。

第叁場

策〔五道〕

問：仲尼述文、武之政，不啻備矣，乃其明要在修身、取人。故志古所以自鏡也，顯賢所以自輔也。至如陳鑑書屏，義則何居？
translation_en:
Draft of a Tang-dynasty mandate appointing Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 as Grand Mentor (643, the seventeenth year of the Zhenguan 貞觀 era).
Draft of a congratulatory memorial from the Grand Secretaries, who, having received an imperial command to compose and present the Admonitions for the Hall of Harmonious Reverence (Yongsu dian zhen 雝肅殿箴), were ordered to have them inscribed on the imperial screen.

Legal judgments (five items):
Omitting to affix the paper-money seal.
Obstructing the receipt and disbursement of funds or grain.
Prohibiting ceremonial welcoming and seeing off of officials.
Showing compassionate relief to military dependents.
Fraudulently wasting government materials.

Third Session

Policy Questions (five items)

Question: Confucius's account of the governance of Kings Wen and Wu was more than comprehensive, yet its clear essentials lay in cultivating the person and selecting men of talent. Thus, recording antiquity is the means to hold up a mirror to oneself, and exalting the worthy is the means to secure assistance for oneself. As for setting forth "mirrors" of history and inscribing names upon screens, what is the meaning behind such practices? …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
蒼姬氏以前尚矣願治之主不世出而
忠謀嘉猷之士亦堇堇有聞或千秋金
鑑或龜鑑精義或兵鑑或內治聖鑑或
藝祖憲鑑均之書以鑑名者或疏刺史
或記吉州守或識潁州理或書從臣所
舉監司或揭監司帥臣郡守均之官以
屏紀者此與修身取人之道果得其要
領否歟我
皇上天縱神聖
===
倚任耆碩相與孜孜治理
帝鑑有圖官名有屏薄海內外亦既能纚纚揚
其盛矣爾多士試即今故證嚮之何如
夫禔身有實而儀監為文官人有經而
辨名為跡伏覩
皇上謹天戒數語暨
面諭廉能顥乎肫肫燁然赫矣爾多士信能闚
仲尼之指敶文武之道可以有補於
聖明是所願轉
punctuated: 蒼姬氏以前，尚矣！願治之主不世出，而忠謀嘉猷之士亦堇堇有聞。或《千秋金鑑》，或《龜鑑精義》，或《兵鑑》，或《內治聖鑑》，或《藝祖憲鑑》，均之書以鑑名者；或疏刺史，或記吉州守，或識潁州理，或書從臣所舉監司，或揭監司、帥臣、郡守，均之官以屏紀者。此與修身取人之道，果得其要領否歟？我皇上天縱神聖，倚任耆碩，相與孜孜治理。《帝鑑》有圖，官名有屏，薄海內外，亦既能纚纚揚其盛矣。爾多士試即今故，證嚮之何如？夫禔身有實，而儀監為文；官人有經，而辨名為跡。伏覩皇上謹天戒數語，暨面諭廉能，顥乎肫肫，燁然赫矣！爾多士信能闚仲尼之指，敶文武之道，可以有補於聖明，是所願轉…
translation_en:
Prior to the house of Zhou, times are remote in antiquity! Thereafter, rulers who earnestly desired good governance did not appear in every generation, and gentlemen offering loyal counsels and fine plans were likewise rarely heard of. In some cases there was the Golden Mirror for a Thousand Autumns (Qianqiu jinjian 千秋金鑑), in others the Essential Meanings of the Tortoise and Mirror (Guijian jingyi 龜鑑精義), or the Military Mirror (Bingjian 兵鑑), or the Sage Mirror for Inner Governance (Neizhi shengjian 內治聖鑑), or the Constitutional Mirror of the Founding Ancestor (Yizu xianjian 藝祖憲鑑)—all alike being books titled "Mirror." In some cases a ruler listed the Regional Inspectors (cishi 刺史), in others he recorded the Prefect of Jizhou, or noted the governance of Yingzhou, or wrote down the Surveillance Officials (jiansi 監司) recommended by attendant ministers, or posted the names of Surveillance Officials, Military Commanders (shuaichen 帥臣), and Commandery Governors (junshou 郡守)—all alike being officials recorded on folding screens. Compared with the Way of cultivating the person and selecting men, did these practices truly grasp its essential points or not?

Our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine sagacity, relies upon and employs venerable and great ministers, working together with them in tireless diligence for the ordering of the state. There is the Illustrated Mirror for Emperors (Dijian tushuo 帝鑑圖說), and there is the screen bearing the names of officials; within and beyond the four seas, people are already able to extol their magnificence at length. Let you many scholars try to examine present affairs and verify how those past examples compare with them.

Now, regulating oneself has its reality, whereas taking models and mirrors is merely outward form; appointing men to office has its constant standard, whereas distinguishing names is merely an external trace. We humbly behold the several words spoken by His Majesty in reverent heed of Heaven's warnings, together with his personal injunctions delivered face-to-face to the incorrupt and capable—how luminous in their earnestness, how brilliantly resplendent! If you many scholars are truly able to peer into the intent of Confucius and set forth the Way of Kings Wen and Wu so as to be of some aid to our sacred and enlightened Sovereign, this is what I wish to transmit so that it may be…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
聞者也
問孔孟設教曷甞不諄諄於求仁哉孔子
多說體孟子多說用儒先有是言矣濂
溪氏衍絶緒以授二程其所論仁果於
孔孟之㫖合乎程門英才林立顧寔能
識仁者未易多得或以惻隱自然言仁
或以生意言仁或以公言仁庶幾哉識
仁者乎乃道南之許獨有所屬豈其契
悟爲獨深與遡厥流派若羅若李咸有
===
發越至紫陽氏出作仁說圖以明其意
而訓仁六字眞氏謂前人所未發者也
多士亦能詳榷否自宋以來稱學曰濂
洛關閩由斯以譚閩尤章灼長遠矣夫
道在天下苟無與立則無與明故意閩
學其涵養操脩自有𨔝異者與不然何
師友淵源所漸獨能延孔孟之統垂訓
至今也多士居恒誦法聖賢稱引仁義
况爾鄉先喆其必有得於尚論之素者
punctuated:
聞者也。
問：孔、孟設教，曷甞不諄諄於求仁哉？孔子多說體，孟子多說用，儒先有是言矣。濂溪氏衍絶緒以授二程，其所論仁，果於孔、孟之㫖合乎？程門英才林立，顧寔能識仁者未易多得。或以「惻隱自然」言仁，或以「生意」言仁，或以「公」言仁，庶幾哉識仁者乎？乃「道南」之許，獨有所屬，豈其契悟爲獨深與？遡厥流派，若羅、若李，咸有發越。至紫陽氏出，作《仁說圖》以明其意，而訓仁六字，眞氏謂前人所未發者也。多士亦能詳榷否？自宋以來，稱學曰「濂、洛、關、閩」。由斯以譚，閩尤章灼長遠矣。夫道在天下，苟無與立，則無與明。故意閩學其涵養操脩，自有𨔝異者與？不然，何師友淵源所漸，獨能延孔、孟之統，垂訓至今也？多士居恒誦法聖賢，稱引仁義，况爾鄉先喆，其必有得於尚論之素者，
translation_en:
… to pass on to the Emperor’s hearing.

Question: When Confucius and Mencius established their teachings, when did they ever cease to earnestly emphasize the pursuit of humaneness (ren)? Earlier Confucians have remarked that Confucius mostly spoke of its substance (ti), whereas Mencius mostly spoke of its function (yong). Master Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] carried forward the broken thread of transmission and passed it to the two Cheng brothers [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤]; did what he discussed regarding humaneness truly accord with the purport of Confucius and Mencius? Among the disciples of the Cheng brothers, brilliant talents stood like a forest, yet those who were genuinely able to grasp the nature of humaneness were not easily found in large numbers. Some spoke of humaneness in terms of "the spontaneity of commiseration," some spoke of humaneness in terms of "vitality" (shengyi), and some spoke of humaneness in terms of "impartiality" (gong)—came these close to grasping humaneness? Yet the commendation of "the Way traveling south" (Daonan) was bestowed upon one person alone [Yang Shi 楊時]; was his personal realization uniquely profound? Tracing this stream of transmission, masters such as Luo [Luo Congyan 羅從彥] and Li [Li Tong 李侗] all further developed and illuminated it. When Master Ziyang [Zhu Xi 朱熹] appeared, he composed the Diagram of the Treatise on Humaneness (Renshuo tu) to clarify its meaning, and as for his six-character gloss on humaneness ["the character of the mind and the principle of love" 心之德愛之理], Master Zhen [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] said it was something no predecessor had ever articulated. Can you gentlemen also deliberate upon this in detail? Since the Song dynasty, the schools of learning have been referred to as "Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min." Speaking from this perspective, the learning of Min [Fujian] has been especially illustrious and enduring. Now, as for the Way in the world, if there is no one to establish it, there is no one to illuminate it. Might we surmise, then, that the self-cultivation and moral practice of the Min school possessed something extraordinarily distinctive? Otherwise, why is it that the gradual influence of its lineage of teachers and friends was uniquely able to perpetuate the orthodoxy of Confucius and Mencius and hand down its teachings to the present day? In ordinary times, you gentlemen recite and model yourselves on the sages and worthies, citing humaneness and righteousness; how much more so since these are the former worthies of your own native province! Surely you have gained insights from your habitual study and evaluation of the past; …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
試著於篇吾將以觀志焉
問諭書名以同俗定音律以和聲王者所
以考文而正樂也書契作而天粟零律
呂制而祥鳳鳴制作關造化宜乎世爲
天下法矣慨自坑焚恣害挾偶煩刑古
法蕩滅是可歎也考諸周官四史掌記
時事典同掌辨度數法固詳且備也故
仲尼因魯史以脩春秋筆削加焉歸魯
正樂雅頌各得其所蓋有明徵矣世疑
===
彤管非筆謂黃鐘最清者何所考據與
筆說筆經作於何人新書全書詳於誰
氏果得其源委否歟篆隸變於斯邈分
隸勒於磾典晉帖唐碑遂多譌謬四聲
拘於江左輕重異于南北秦隴梁益取
韻尤遠點畫聲音久矣其失辨也茲欲
正楷隸之譌以復古法諧律呂之音以
定元聲抑何取裁焉洪惟我
聖祖命儒臣製洪武正韻頒示中外
punctuated:
試著於篇，吾將以觀志焉。
問：諭書名以同俗，定音律以和聲，王者所以考文而正樂也。書契作而天粟零，律呂制而祥鳳鳴，制作關造化，宜乎世爲天下法矣！慨自坑焚恣害，挾偶煩刑，古法蕩滅，是可歎也。考諸《周官》，四史掌記時事，典同掌辨度數，法固詳且備也。故仲尼因魯史以脩《春秋》，筆削加焉；歸魯正樂，《雅》、《頌》各得其所，蓋有明徵矣。世疑彤管非筆，謂黃鐘最清者，何所考據與？《筆說》、《筆經》作於何人？《新書》、《全書》詳於誰氏？果得其源委否歟？篆、隸變於斯、邈，分、隸勒於磾、典，晉帖、唐碑遂多譌謬；四聲拘於江左，輕重異于南北，秦、隴、梁、益取韻尤遠，點畫、聲音久矣其失辨也。茲欲正楷、隸之譌以復古法，諧律呂之音以定元聲，抑何取裁焉？洪惟我聖祖命儒臣製《洪武正韻》，頒示中外，
translation_en:
… Set them forth in your essays, through which I shall observe your aspirations.

Question: Instructing in the names of written characters so as to unify customs, and determining the musical pitches so as to harmonize sounds—these are the means by which a true king examines writing and rectifies music. When written contracts were created, heaven rained down millet; when the Yang and Yin pitch-pipes (lülü) were fashioned, auspicious phoenixes sang. Such creations are bound up with the transformative power of nature; how fitting that for generations they have served as models for all under heaven! Alas, ever since the wanton destruction of the burying of scholars and burning of books, and the onerous punishments against harbouring books and gathering to discuss them, the ancient methods have been swept away—this is truly lamentable. Examining the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the four Scribes (shi) were in charge of recording contemporary affairs, and the Pitch-pipe Master (Diantong) was in charge of distinguishing measures and numbers; the regulations were indeed detailed and complete. Thus Confucius drew upon the historical records of Lu to compile the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), applying his brush to write and delete; and when he returned to Lu to rectify music, the "Odes" (Ya) and "Hymns" (Song) each found their proper place—of this there is clear evidence. Yet the world doubts whether the red tube (tongguan) was a writing brush, and claims that the Yellow Bell (Huangzhong) pitch is the highest and clearest; on what evidence are such views based? By whom were the Discourse on the Brush (Bishuo) and the Classic of the Brush (Bijing) written? Which scholars elaborated the New Book (Xinshu) and the Complete Book (Quanshu)? Did they truly grasp their origins and developments? Since seal script (zhuan) and clerical script (li) were altered by Li Si 李斯 and Cheng Miao 程邈, and bafen and clerical scripts were engraved by師宜官 [?] / Jin Midi 金日磾 [?] and Handan Chun 邯鄲淳 /韋誕 [?] (Di and Dian), the model calligraphies of the Jin and the stone inscriptions of the Tang consequently came to contain many errors. Since the four tones were constrained by the practice of the lower Yangtze region (Jiangzuo), with light and heavy pronunciations differing between north and south, and the rhymes adopted in Qin, Long, Liang, and Yi diverging even further, the strokes of characters and the sounds of speech have long lost their proper distinctions. If we now wish to correct the errors in standard (kai) and clerical scripts in order to restore the ancient methods, and to harmonize the notes of the pitch-pipes in order to fix the fundamental sound, upon what standards should we rely? Humbly reflecting on how our Sacred Ancestor (Emperor Taizu) commanded Confucian officials to compile the Orthodox Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun) and promulgate it throughout the court and provinces, …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
諭禮部製
宴饗樂章被之管絃
列聖相承悉遵用之可謂書同文矣律和聲矣
廼議者或謂樂經殘缺而雅律未盡諧
俗隸舛謬而書名未盡諭則同文正樂
之化實有待于
今日諸士必有精于字學明於音律者矣幸
詳言之毋曰以俟君子
問書曰政貴有恒辭尚體要又曰世祿之
===
家鮮克由禮此古今語好尚論風化者
必稽焉閩自唐常衮設鄉校使學者爲
文章習俗一變迨宋休明齒爲上國等
于鄒魯我
國家二百年來賢哲奮庸斌斌濟濟迄今逾
盛或謂文盛于前士習則不逮往昔然
與否與歷攷志傳所載自楊文敏而下
以功業文章顯者不暇具論如蔡清周
瑛之理學黃鞏黃仲昭之氣節陳茂烈
punctuated:
諭禮部製宴饗樂章，被之管絃，列聖相承，悉遵用之，可謂書同文矣，律和聲矣。廼議者或謂《樂經》殘缺而雅律未盡諧，俗隸舛謬而書名未盡諭，則同文正樂之化，實有待于今日。諸士必有精于字學、明於音律者矣，幸詳言之，毋曰「以俟君子」。

問：《書》曰：「政貴有恒，辭尚體要。」又曰：「世祿之家，鮮克由禮。」此古今語好尚、論風化者必稽焉。閩自唐常衮設鄉校，使學者爲文章，習俗一變；迨宋休明，齒爲上國，等于鄒魯。我國家二百年來，賢哲奮庸，斌斌濟濟，迄今逾盛。或謂文盛于前，士習則不逮往昔，然與？否與？歷攷志傳所載，自楊文敏而下，以功業文章顯者，不暇具論；如蔡清、周瑛之理學，黃鞏、黃仲昭之氣節，陳茂烈
translation_en:
…and instructed the Ministry of Rites to compose musical pieces for court banquets and set them to pipes and strings. Successive sacred emperors have inherited and followed them in every respect; truly it may be said that writing has been unified into the same script and the pitch-pipes have harmonized the sounds! Yet some commentators argue that because the Classic of Music (Yuejing) is fragmentary, the elegant pitches are not yet completely harmonized, and because vulgar clerical script is full of errors, the written characters are not yet completely understood; thus the transformative work of unifying script and rectifying music truly awaits the present day. Among you scholars there must certainly be those who are well-versed in philology and discerning in musical temperament. Please set forth your views in detail, and do not say, "Wait for a superior man."

Question: The Book of Documents (Shu) says, "In governance, value consistency; in words, prize substance and essentials." It also says, "Families of hereditary emolument rarely abide by ritual propriety." Those past and present who speak of prevailing tastes and discuss moral transformation invariably examine these words. In Fujian (Min), ever since Chang Gun of the Tang established local schools and had students compose literary essays, customs were utterly transformed; by the flourishing era of the Song, it ranked among the foremost regions, equal to Zou and Lu. Over the two hundred years of our dynasty, worthies and sages have risen to active service in refined and abundant numbers, flourishing ever more down to the present. Yet some say that while literary culture is more flourishing than before, the scholarly ethos does not measure up to bygone days—is this so, or is it not? Examining successively what is recorded in gazetteers and biographies, from Yang Rong (Yang Wenmin) onward, we have no leisure to discuss in full all those who distinguished themselves through meritorious deeds and literary writings; but consider the Neo-Confucian learning of principle (lixue) of Cai Qing and Zhou Ying, the moral integrity of Huang Gong and Huang Zhongzhao, the earnest conduct of Chen Maolie…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之篤行陳真晟之恬退之數公者巋然
多士之表也邇來習尚得無有鑿于前
哲者乎說者謂崇儉素釐文體脩實行
正心術為閩士所宜先抑果然乎我
皇上銳意復古期得真材屢廑
詔旨夫謹好尚以作士一道德以同俗正今日
所亟圖也轉移興起之機安在多士試
究言之以觀所尚
問閩往被海患比來稍攝然矣第閩廣舳
===
艫相接廣寇未靖閩未可安枕也夫廣
海島嶼延袤逋寇蕩平非易乃閩不過
南澳彭湖湄洲海壇爾當事者猶獨慮
彭湖之難處何以故也或議攻或議守
或議塞斯亦有足采否大抵海防所患
莫大於勾引接濟故番舶雖開而日本
之禁猶嚴焉頃
朝議下兩省申禁蓋其慮遠矣論者猶患事
權之難一何歟夫為弭盜計非勦即撫
punctuated:
之篤行、陳真晟之恬退，之數公者，巋然多士之表也。邇來習尚，得無有鑿于前哲者乎？說者謂崇儉素、釐文體、脩實行、正心術，為閩士所宜先，抑果然乎？我皇上銳意復古，期得真材，屢廑詔旨。夫謹好尚以作士，一道德以同俗，正今日所亟圖也。轉移興起之機安在？多士試究言之，以觀所尚。
問：閩往被海患，比來稍攝然矣。第閩、廣舳艫相接，廣寇未靖，閩未可安枕也。夫廣海島嶼延袤，逋寇蕩平非易；乃閩不過南澳、彭湖、湄洲、海壇爾，當事者猶獨慮彭湖之難處，何以故也？或議攻，或議守，或議塞，斯亦有足采否？大抵海防所患，莫大於勾引、接濟，故番舶雖開，而日本之禁猶嚴焉。頃朝議下兩省申禁，蓋其慮遠矣，論者猶患事權之難一，何歟？夫為弭盜計，非勦即撫，
translation_en:
… earnest conduct, and the tranquil retirement of Chen Zhensheng 陳真晟—these several gentlemen stand tower-like as models for the multitude of scholars. Could it be that recent customs and fashions are at variance with those former worthies? Commentators say that esteeming frugality and simplicity, rectifying literary style, cultivating substantive conduct, and correcting the inclinations of the mind are what the scholars of Fujian ought to prioritize; is this indeed so? Our August Emperor is keenly intent on restoring antiquity, hoping to obtain true talent, and has repeatedly shown concern in His imperial edicts. Being careful about preferences and fashions so as to rouse the scholars, and unifying morality so as to harmonize customs, are precisely what must be urgently planned for today. Wherein lies the pivot for transforming and inspiring them? Let you scholars examine and speak of this thoroughly, so that we may observe what you esteem.

Question: In the past, Fujian suffered from maritime troubles, though lately things have quieted down somewhat. Yet the ships of Fujian and Guangdong follow one another bow to stern; while the Guangdong pirates are not yet pacified, Fujian cannot rest easy on its pillow. Now, the islands of the Guangdong sea stretch out extensively, and sweeping away fugitive pirates there is not easy. In Fujian, however, there are no more than Nan'ao 南澳, Penghu 彭湖, Meizhou 湄洲, and Haitan 海壇; why is it that those in charge of affairs still uniquely worry that Penghu is difficult to manage? Some propose attacking, some propose defending, and some propose blockading—is there anything among these proposals worth adopting? Generally speaking, among the troubles of coastal defense, none is greater than collusion with and provisioning of the pirates; therefore, although foreign merchant ships have been permitted to trade, the prohibition against Japan remains strict. Recently, court deliberations sent orders down to the two provinces to reiterate the prohibitions, which indeed shows far-sighted concern; yet why do commentators still worry about the difficulty of unifying authority over affairs? Now, in devising plans to suppress bandits, if it is not extermination then it is pacification, …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而其要在練兵練土去客則人人能譚
矣然未聞有顯臻厥效者豈練之非其
道抑將之非其人與昔人有言無事而
先憂有事而不懼玆欲爲閩桑土計安
出爾多士嶽嶽懷當世慮矧鄉國乎其
審畫而對毋勦陳說
punctuated: 而其要在練兵。練土去客，則人人能譚矣，然未聞有顯臻厥效者，豈練之非其道，抑將之非其人與？昔人有言：「無事而先憂，有事而不懼。」玆欲爲閩桑土計，安出？爾多士嶽嶽懷當世慮，矧鄉國乎！其審畫而對，毋勦陳說。
translation_en: …and its essential point lies in training troops. Everyone is able to talk about training local troops and dismissing guest troops, yet we have not heard of anyone visibly achieving results from this. Is it because the training does not follow the proper method, or because those in command are not the right men? A person of the past had a saying: "To worry beforehand when there is no trouble, and to be unafraid when trouble arises." Now, if we wish to take preventive measures for Fujian before the rain comes, from where shall our plan emerge? You many scholars proudly harbor concerns for the affairs of the present age—how much more so when it comes to your own native province! Consider your plans carefully and reply, and do not merely plagiarize stale talk.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
素以為絢兮何謂也子曰繪事後素曰禮
後乎子曰起予者商也始可與言詩已
矣
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批刋落鉛華歸于雅馴復
古之文也
同考試官訓導李批首義作者往往以繪事
===
禮後平對殊失輕重此作獨得題意而詞復簡確宜錄以式
考試官教諭丘批峻潔渾成
考試官教諭姚批崇雅黜浮宜冠多士
聖人與賢者論詩因其善悟而與之也夫詩非
善悟者難與言也賢者禮後之悟深於詩矣夫
子與之也固宜且夫詩之為教其詞婉其理該
非以意悟者不能達也故夫子嘗雅言之而可
與之言者鮮矣詩詞有曰素以為絢兮子夏始
疑而問焉亦徒以其詞而未會其意也夫子曉
punctuated:
第壹場。
四書。
「素以為絢兮，何謂也？」子曰：「繪事後素。」曰：「禮後乎？」子曰：「起予者商也！始可與言《詩》已矣。」
陳文選。
同考試官訓導蘇批：刋落鉛華，歸于雅馴，復古之文也。
同考試官訓導李批：首義作者，往往以繪事、禮後平對，殊失輕重。此作獨得題意，而詞復簡確，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭丘批：峻潔渾成。
考試官教諭姚批：崇雅黜浮，宜冠多士。
聖人與賢者論《詩》，因其善悟而與之也。夫《詩》非善悟者，難與言也。賢者「禮後」之悟，深於《詩》矣，夫子與之也固宜。且夫《詩》之為教，其詞婉，其理該，非以意悟者不能達也。故夫子嘗雅言之，而可與之言者鮮矣。《詩》詞有曰「素以為絢兮」，子夏始疑而問焉，亦徒以其詞而未會其意也。夫子曉…
translation_en:
First Session.

The Four Books.

"'The plain silk is used to make the patterned!' What does this mean?" The Master said, "The business of painting comes after the plain silk." He said, "Does ritual then come after?" The Master said, "It is Shang who brings out my meaning! Now I can begin to speak of the Odes with him indeed."

By Chen Wenxuan 陳文選.

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Su 蘇 comments: Stripping away cosmetic ornament and returning to refined elegance, this is prose that restores antiquity.

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Li 李 comments: Writers on this first topic often treat "the business of painting" and "ritual comes after" as parallel counterparts of equal weight, completely losing the relative emphasis. This composition alone grasps the meaning of the theme, and its diction is moreover concise and exact; it should be recorded as a model.

Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: Lofty, pure, and seamlessly complete.

Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: Exalting refinement and rejecting superficiality, it deserves to stand first among the many scholars.

When the Sage discussed the Odes with the worthy, it was because of his capacity for keen comprehension that he commended him. Now, unless one is capable of keen comprehension, it is difficult to speak of the Odes with him. In awakening to the idea that "ritual comes after," the worthy went deep into the Odes; that the Master commended him was certainly fitting.

Moreover, in the teaching of the Odes, the words are subtle and the principles comprehensive; one who does not comprehend through the underlying intent cannot penetrate them. Therefore, although the Master often spoke of them in polished language, those with whom he could truly discuss them were few. There is a line in the Odes that reads, "The plain silk is used to make the patterned!" When Zixia 子夏 first doubted this and asked about it, he too was merely attending to its words without yet grasping its intent. The Master enlightened…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之以爲素非絢也先繪事以立其質繪尚飾也
後素工以昭其文是卽素以爲絢之謂也商於
是有悟而復於夫子曰繪事旣後矣然則禮以
嘉會固天下之至文也而非其所自始也意者
禮不虛行必先有以敦天下之朴也而禮其爲
之後乎不然何繪事之後於素也抑亦詩人之
言有未盡耶夫子從而與之曰予方論詩而商
也悟學斯其爲起予者乎自是而與之言詩精
神心術與詩通焉凡詞近而托意於遠者可與
===
達也性情物理與詩會焉凡詞顯而寓意於微
者可與幾也吾非商之與言而誰與哉吁詩必
善悟如商而後可與言也信乎詩之難言也抑
夫子之與商不獨以詩也周文之敝禮眩本末
而日用不知矣故禮云禮云之嘆欲人緣末以
求本也商也知禮之後則亦知禮之本矣使人
皆知禮如商也先進其可復乎是則夫子與商
之意也
浩浩其天
punctuated:
之，以爲素非絢也，先繪事以立其質；繪尚飾也，後素工以昭其文，是卽「素以爲絢」之謂也。商於是有悟，而復於夫子曰：「繪事旣後矣，然則禮以嘉會，固天下之至文也，而非其所自始也。意者禮不虛行，必先有以敦天下之朴也，而禮其爲之後乎？不然，何繪事之後於素也？抑亦詩人之言有未盡耶？」夫子從而與之曰：「予方論《詩》，而商也悟學，斯其爲起予者乎！自是而與之言《詩》，精神心術與《詩》通焉，凡詞近而托意於遠者，可與達也；性情物理與《詩》會焉，凡詞顯而寓意於微者，可與幾也。吾非商之與言，而誰與哉！」吁！《詩》必善悟如商，而後可與言也，信乎《詩》之難言也！抑夫子之與商，不獨以《詩》也。周文之敝，禮眩本末，而日用不知矣。故「禮云禮云」之嘆，欲人緣末以求本也。商也知禮之後，則亦知禮之本矣。使人皆知禮如商也，先進其可復乎？是則夫子與商之意也。

「浩浩其天。」
translation_en:
…him, explaining that plain white is not itself the colorful pattern; rather, in the business of painting, one first establishes the ground. And since painting values adornment, the painting work comes after the plain white silk in order to display its pattern—this is precisely what is meant by "taking the plain white to make the colorful pattern."

At this, Shang [Bu Shang 卜商, i.e., Zixia 子夏] had an awakening and replied to the Master, saying: "If the business of painting comes afterward, then although ritual, by bringing together what is finest, is indeed the ultimate refinement in the world, it is not where things begin. Could it be that ritual is not practiced in a vacuum, that there must first be that which cultivates the unadorned simplicity of the world, and that ritual then comes after it? Otherwise, why would the business of painting come after the plain white ground? Or is it that the poet's words left something unsaid?"

The Master thereupon approved of him, saying: "I was just discussing the Odes (Shi), and Shang has grasped the principle of learning—surely he is the one who inspires me! From now on, I can speak of the Odes with him. When his spirit and mind commune with the Odes, whatever uses near words to entrust a distant meaning, we can penetrate together; when his nature, feelings, and grasp of the principles of things converge with the Odes, whatever uses manifest words to lodge a subtle meaning, we can fathom together. If I do not speak of them with Shang, with whom shall I speak?"

Ah! Only when someone is as good at awakening to meaning as Shang can one speak with him of the Odes—truly, how difficult it is to speak of the Odes! Yet the Master's approval of Shang was not solely on account of the Odes. In the decline of Zhou refinement, ritual had become confused as to root and branch, and people used it daily without understanding. Thus the Master's lament, "'Ritual, ritual,' they say," was a desire that people trace the branches back to seek the root. Since Shang knew that ritual comes after, he also knew the root of ritual. If all men understood ritual as Shang did, could not the ways of the men of former times be restored? This, then, was the Master's intention in approving of Shang.

"Vast and boundless is his Heaven!"

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批形容至誠心體浩浩處極
透徹非淺學可到
同考試官教諭張批造理精奧攑詞渾融蓋體
認而有得者
考試官教諭丘批深湛之思昌大之詞
考試官教諭姚批典實可正文體
中庸於至誠極賛其知化之盛焉夫知化者聖
心之天也知惟自然而其天無外矣中庸賛之
===
也宜哉今夫化育之理運於天地會於吾心本
至大也一誠所貫也至誠無倚而知化焉則其
天也豈曰有外之天哉吾見心涵太虛而渾淪
磅礴廓之莫知其極誠通造化而包含徧覆究
之不見其窮二氣五行之運皆其默會則皆其
統括也而昭曠之原何所不有四時百物之機
皆其潛通則皆其範圍也而虛靈之內何所不
容靜而存神造化之專翕者在聖心焉寂然之
天浩浩乎不可以方所拘也動而達化造化之
punctuated:
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批：「形容至誠心體浩浩處，極透徹，非淺學可到。」
同考試官教諭張批：「造理精奧，攑詞渾融，蓋體認而有得者。」
考試官教諭丘批：「深湛之思，昌大之詞。」
考試官教諭姚批：「典實，可正文體。」
《中庸》於至誠，極賛其知化之盛焉。夫知化者，聖心之天也。知惟自然，而其天無外矣，《中庸》賛之也宜哉！今夫化育之理，運於天地，會於吾心，本至大也，一誠所貫也。至誠無倚而知化焉，則其天也，豈曰有外之天哉？吾見心涵太虛，而渾淪磅礴，廓之莫知其極；誠通造化，而包含徧覆，究之不見其窮。二氣五行之運，皆其默會，則皆其統括也，而昭曠之原，何所不有？四時百物之機，皆其潛通，則皆其範圍也，而虛靈之內，何所不容？靜而存神，造化之專翕者在聖心焉，寂然之天，浩浩乎不可以方所拘也；動而達化，造化之
translation_en:
Gong Tingbin 龔廷賓.
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Xiong 熊: "In depicting how the substance of the mind of utmost sincerity is vast and boundless, it is extremely penetrating—not something shallow learning could reach."
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Zhang 張: "Its grasp of principle is refined and profound, and its phrasing is harmonious and well-integrated; this comes from one who has personally experienced and realized the truth."
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Qiu 丘: "Profound and deep thought; grand and flourishing diction."
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Yao 姚: "Canonical and substantive; fit to rectify literary style."
With regard to the person of utmost sincerity, the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸) praises to the utmost the magnificence of his knowing the transformations. Now, that which knows the transformations is the Heaven of the sage's mind. Because this knowing is purely natural, its Heaven has nothing outside itself; how fitting it is that the Doctrine of the Mean praises it! Now, the principle of transforming and nourishing operates throughout heaven and earth and converges within our mind; it is originally supreme in greatness, and is penetrated by a single sincerity. When one of utmost sincerity, leaning on nothing, knows the transformations, then can his Heaven be called a Heaven that lies outside? I see a mind that encompasses the Great Vacuity, undifferentiated and vast—expand it, and none can know its limit; a sincerity that penetrates creation and transformation, all-embracing and universally covering—investigate it to the end, and one sees no exhaustion. The operations of the two vital energies and the five phases are all tacitly understood by him, and thus are all encompassed by him; within that bright and spacious source, what is not present? The springs of action of the four seasons and the hundred things are all silently penetrated by him, and thus are all circumscribed by him; within that vacuous and numinous spiritual intelligence, what is not contained? When tranquil, he preserves the spirit, and the concentrated contraction of creation and transformation resides within the sage's mind—a quiescent Heaven, vast and boundless, that cannot be confined by direction or place. When active, he comprehends the transformations, and the…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
直闢者在聖心焉擴然之天浩浩乎不可以形
體囿也是何也造化一誠也聖心之誠一造化
也故運之兩間者非大斂之一心者非小矣化
育無心者也聖心亦無思者也故本之一誠若
微而涵乎萬化則大矣至誠知化功用其盛矣
哉噫聖人天道之極致子思獨契其深矣雖然
聖人不惟知化已也天地至大人猶有憾則裁
成輔相之道且於聖人賴之然聖非絕德也吾
心之初一誠也一天也欲以蔽之則誠者僞大
===
者隘與天地不相似矣至聖不失其初焉耳學
者善反之則性存故曰誠者聖功之本
孟子曰雞鳴而起孳孳爲善者舜之徒也
宋獻瑞
同考試官訓導經 批 發孟子啓迪人心意于
起結處親切有味
同考試官敎諭陳 批 不刻意爲工而醇正昌
達可爲時義準繩矣
考試官敎諭丘 批 意見不凡
punctuated:
直闢者在聖心焉，擴然之天，浩浩乎不可以形體囿也。是何也？造化一誠也，聖心之誠一造化也，故運之兩間者非大，斂之一心者非小矣。化育無心者也，聖心亦無思者也，故本之一誠若微，而涵乎萬化則大矣。至誠知化，功用其盛矣哉！噫！聖人天道之極致，子思獨契其深矣。雖然，聖人不惟知化已也，天地至大，人猶有憾，則裁成輔相之道，且於聖人賴之。然聖非絕德也，吾心之初，一誠也，一天也；欲以蔽之，則誠者僞，大者隘，與天地不相似矣。至聖不失其初焉耳，學者善反之則性存，故曰：誠者，聖功之本。

「孟子曰：雞鳴而起，孳孳爲善者，舜之徒也。」
宋獻瑞
同考試官訓導經批：發孟子啓迪人心意，于起結處親切有味。
同考試官敎諭陳批：不刻意爲工，而醇正昌達，可爲時義準繩矣。
考試官敎諭丘批：意見不凡。
translation_en:
… expansive opening of creation and transformation resides within the mind of the sage, and this vast Heaven is so boundless that it cannot be confined by physical form. Why is this so? Creation and transformation are nothing other than sincerity, and the sincerity of the sage's mind is one with creation and transformation; therefore, as it operates between Heaven and Earth it is not disproportionately vast, and as it is gathered into a single mind it is not disproportionately small. Transforming and nourishing processes are without deliberate intent, and the sage's mind is likewise without anxious thought; therefore, while rooted in a single sincerity that seems subtle, in encompassing the myriad transformations it is vast. For utmost sincerity to know transformation—how magnificent is its function! Alas! In the ultimate perfection of the sage and the Way of Heaven, Zisi 子思 alone grasped its profundity. Even so, the sage does not merely know transformation and stop there. Though Heaven and Earth are supremely great, human beings still find things to regret in them, and thus the Way of regulating and assisting nature relies upon the sage. Yet sagehood is not an unattainable virtue. In the original state of our mind, it is wholly sincere and wholly one with Heaven. When selfish desires obscure it, what was sincere becomes false, what was great becomes narrow, and it no longer resembles Heaven and Earth. The supreme sage merely does not lose this original state. If learners skillfully return to it, their innate nature will be preserved. Therefore it is said: Sincerity is the foundation of the work of becoming a sage.

"Mencius said: 'He who rises at cockcrow and diligently does good is a follower of Shun.'"
Song Xianrui 宋獻瑞
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jing 經 comments: He brings out Mencius's intention of inspiring the human mind, and at the opening and closing sections it is intimate and full of flavor.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: Without straining for artificial craft, it is pure, upright, and fluent, and can serve as a standard for contemporary examination essays.
Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: The insight is extraordinary.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭姚批有渾厚氣象
大賢於人心而示以作聖之機焉夫聖人善之
至也一念爲善亦足以作聖而夫人可不勉哉
孟子迪人心者如此蓋曰人品係于立心之微
而學術由于趨向之正舜大聖人也後世無及
焉與舜爲徒似若未易能者然舜非絕德善斯
成性者也人性皆善亦可爲舜者也人患弗爲
耳誠能雞鳴而起方天機之有覺孳孳爲善遂
時敏之不遑良心生于夜氣而欲擴其好惡之
===
眞由是旦晝弗忘者此善也此心也善端動於
幾微而思充其仁義之量由是惟日不足者亦
此善也此心也茲人也不爲舜之徒乎蓋聖人
能盡其性而全體至善本不外於吾心夫人强
于爲善而一念惟勤亦可入於聖域以法天下
未必如舜而善之外無他法也善同則其趨同
舜固先得夫同然斯亦後舜而效法矣以傳後
世未必如舜而善之外無他傳也趨同則其歸
同舜固與人而爲善斯亦由善以希舜矣于是
punctuated:
考試官敎諭姚批：有渾厚氣象。

大賢於人心，而示以作聖之機焉。夫聖人，善之至也；一念爲善，亦足以作聖，而夫人可不勉哉？孟子迪人心者如此。蓋曰：人品係于立心之微，而學術由于趨向之正。舜，大聖人也，後世無及焉，與舜爲徒，似若未易能者。然舜非絕德，善斯成性者也；人性皆善，亦可爲舜者也，人患弗爲耳。誠能雞鳴而起，方天機之有覺；孳孳爲善，遂時敏之不遑。良心生于夜氣，而欲擴其好惡之眞，由是旦晝弗忘者，此善也，此心也；善端動於幾微，而思充其仁義之量，由是惟日不足者，亦此善也，此心也。茲人也，不爲舜之徒乎？蓋聖人能盡其性，而全體至善，本不外於吾心；夫人强于爲善，而一念惟勤，亦可入於聖域。以法天下，未必如舜，而善之外無他法也；善同則其趨同，舜固先得夫同然，斯亦後舜而效法矣。以傳後世，未必如舜，而善之外無他傳也；趨同則其歸同，舜固與人而爲善，斯亦由善以希舜矣。于是
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: It possesses a rich and substantial aura.

The great worthy addresses the human mind and reveals to it the pivot for becoming a sage. Now, a sage is the ultimate perfection of goodness; yet a single thought devoted to doing good is also sufficient to make one a sage—so how could anyone fail to exert themselves? Such was the way Mencius guided the human mind. It is as if to say: a person's character depends on the subtle incipient stirrings of how they establish their mind, and their learning derives from the rectitude of their orientation. Shun 舜 was a great sage whom later generations could not equal; to become a follower of Shun would seem no easy thing to achieve. Yet Shun did not possess some unattainable virtue—it was simply through goodness that he brought his nature to completion. Since human nature is good in all people, anyone can also become a Shun; the only worry is that people do not act upon it. If one can truly rise at cockcrow, just when the heavenly mechanism awakens to awareness, and diligently do good without a moment's slackness in timely exertion: when the innate good mind is born of the night breath and one desires to expand the genuineness of its likes and dislikes, so that throughout the morning and day one never forgets it—it is this goodness, and this mind; when the beginnings of goodness stir in the subtlest incipience and one seeks to fill out the full measure of one's benevolence and righteousness, so that the whole day seems insufficient for it—it is likewise this goodness, and this mind. Such a person—are they not a follower of Shun? For the sage is able to exhaust his nature, and the complete substance of supreme goodness is fundamentally not external to our own mind; if an ordinary person strives vigorously at doing good and remains unceasingly diligent in every thought, they too can enter the realm of sagehood. In serving as a model for the world, one may not yet equal Shun, yet outside of goodness there is no other model; when the goodness is the same, the orientation is the same—Shun to be sure was the first to grasp what is common to all minds, and this person follows after Shun in emulating that model. In transmitting to later generations, one may not yet equal Shun, yet outside of goodness there is nothing else to transmit; when the orientation is the same, the ultimate destination is the same—Shun to be sure joined with others in doing good, and this person likewise proceeds through goodness to aspire to Shun. Thereupon…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
知人皆可以爲舜而爲之自一念向善始苟出
乎善則入于利其去舜遠矣可不審哉抑論舜
蹠之分惟在善利之間夫人而知之也然亦有
以善自名卒歸於利者特一念起於自爲有所
溺而不察耳善乎張敬夫曰無所爲而爲者義
也有所爲而爲者利也噫明于此則萬世心學
之原係之矣
易
六四井甃无咎象曰井甃无咎脩井也九
===
五井洌寒泉食象曰寒泉之食中正也
上六井收勿幕有孚元吉象曰元吉在
上大成也
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批體裁整潔詞意渾鬯
是易義之佳者
同考試官教諭張批闡發三爻象語不煩
而意義自見宜錄
考試官教諭丘批氣格雄渾
punctuated:
知人皆可以爲舜，而爲之自一念向善始。苟出乎善，則入于利，其去舜遠矣，可不審哉！抑論舜、蹠之分，惟在善、利之間，夫人而知之也。然亦有以善自名，卒歸於利者，特一念起於自爲，有所溺而不察耳。善乎，張敬夫曰：「無所爲而爲者，義也；有所爲而爲者，利也。」噫！明于此，則萬世心學之原係之矣。

《易》
「六四，井甃，无咎。《象》曰：井甃无咎，脩井也。九五，井洌，寒泉食。《象》曰：寒泉之食，中正也。上六，井收勿幕，有孚元吉。《象》曰：元吉在上，大成也。」
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批：體裁整潔，詞意渾鬯，是《易》義之佳者。
同考試官教諭張批：闡發三爻象，語不煩而意義自見，宜錄。
考試官教諭丘批：氣格雄渾。
translation_en:
… [Thus,] one knows that anyone can become like Shun, and doing so begins with a single thought directed toward goodness. If one departs from goodness, one enters into profit, and is far removed from Shun—how could one not examine this carefully? Moreover, in discussing the distinction between Shun and Robber Zhi, that it lies solely between goodness and profit is something everyone knows. Yet there are also those who claim the name of goodness for themselves, yet ultimately end up in profit; it is merely that a single thought arises from self-interest, and being immersed in something, they fail to examine it. Well said is the remark of Zhang Jingfu (Zhang Shi 張栻): "Doing something without an ulterior motive is righteousness; doing something with an ulterior motive is profit." Ah! If one is clear about this, then the source of the learning of the mind (xinxue) for ten thousand generations depends upon it.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"Six in the fourth place: The well is lined with tiles; no blame. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'The well is lined with tiles, no blame'—this means repairing the well. Nine in the fifth place: The well is clear, a cold spring for drinking. The Commentary on the Images says: 'The drinking of the cold spring'—this is because it is central and correct. Six at the top: The well is drawn from; do not cover it. There is sincerity; supreme good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Supreme good fortune at the top'—this is great completion."
Gong Tingbin 龔廷賓
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Xiong comments: The structure is neat and clean, and the diction and meaning are profound and fluent. It is a fine piece of exposition on the Book of Changes.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang comments: It elucidates the three lines and their Images; the words are not prolix, yet the meaning naturally manifests itself. It ought to be recorded.
Examiner, Instructor Qiu comments: The spirit and style are vigorous and profound.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭姚批醇正有古意
歷觀井爻之義見養道之備焉夫由井甃泉食
而至於大成茲養道所爲備也爻象交著其義
有以夫且井以養爲義是故君子得之以養其
身以養天下夫使天下而各被其養焉王道成
矣惟茲觀于六四陰柔不泉則道足潤身而功

四能自養也非能養人也以言乎成功未也觀
于九五陽剛中正則德裕淵衷而惠洽寰宇故

Examiner and Instructor Yao comments: Pure, orthodox, and possessing the spirit of antiquity.

Surveying the meanings of the lines of the hexagram "The Well" (Jing), one sees the completeness of the Way of Nourishment. Indeed, progressing from "the well is lined with tile" and "the spring is drunk from" to "great completion"—this is how the Way of Nourishment is made complete. That the line statements and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) mutually manifest this meaning is truly with good reason! Moreover, a well takes nourishment as its essential meaning; therefore, the superior man grasps it to nourish his own person and to nourish All under Heaven. When All under Heaven each receive his nourishment, the Kingly Way is accomplished.

Now, observing the Six in the Fourth place: being yin and yielding, it is not yet a spring, so its Way is sufficient to enrich one's own person, yet its merit does not reach to others. Thus the line statement says, "The well is lined with tile; no blame," and the Commentary on the Images explains this as "repairing the well." From this we know that the Fourth line can nourish itself, but is not yet able to nourish others; to speak of accomplished merit, it is not there yet.

Observing the Nine in the Fifth place: being yang, firm, central, and correct, its virtue is abundant within the depths of the heart and its grace saturates the entire realm. Thus the line statement says, "The well is clear; the cold spring is drunk from," and the Commentary on the Images explains this through its being "central and correct." From this we know that the Fifth line both nourishes itself and is able to nourish others; yet to speak of great completion, it is still not there yet.

Coming to the Six at the Top: its outflow has a source, so its virtue is supreme; its nourishment is inexhaustible, so its merit is universal. Thus the line statement says, "The well is drawn from; do not cover it," to display its abundance, and "There is sincerity; supreme good fortune," to trace its fundamental root; and the Commentary on the Images further explains this as "great completion." For by this point, Heavenly virtue and the Kingly Way unite the internal and external to bring capability to completion; lofty, brilliant, broad, and thick, it resembles Heaven and Earth. The "lining with tile" of the Fourth line and the "drinking" of the Fifth line are altogether not worth mentioning; has not the Way of Nourishment reached its ultimate pinnacle!

Alas! "Lining the well with tile" is not the end; it is succeeded by "drinking from the spring." "Drinking from the spring" is not the end; it concludes with "great completion." Such is the difficulty of exhausting the Way of Nourishment; those who preside over governance may observe this! 吉，必先之「有孚」，何哉？蓋王道本於誠意。《中庸》論賛化育，必歸於至誠。至誠者，孚之極也。故堯以允恭致萬邦協和，舜以允塞臻四方風動，二聖爲帝道大成，皆誠爲之本也。此又養天下者所當知也。

… good fortune," why must he precede it with "possessing sincerity"? Because the Kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere. When the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) discusses assisting in the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth, it necessarily attributes this to utmost sincerity. Utmost sincerity is the pinnacle of trustworthiness (fu). Thus Yao, through sincere courtesy, brought about harmony among the myriad states; Shun, through sincere integrity, caused the four quarters to be moved as if by the wind. That the two sages achieved the great completion of the Imperial Way was in both cases rooted in sincerity. This, too, is what those who nourish the world ought to know.

"Content in his situation and earnest in benevolence, therefore he is able to love." [Zhouyi, Xici I.4]
By Huang Guoding 黃國鼎.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiong: On this topic, most writers copy old clichés, which makes for truly tiresome reading. This piece alone trims away superfluity and strips out浮floridness, genuinely and fluently expressing the fundamental purport; it can serve as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang: Balanced, upright, brisk, and vigorous—an essay that values substance. It should be selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qiu: Concise, weighty, and proper in form.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yao: Elucidates the meaning of the topic clearly and exhaustively.

When we observe the sage's utmost embodiment of benevolence, his full realization of human nature becomes manifest. Now, benevolence has love as its governing principle; by being content in one's situation and earnest in benevolence, love is established therein—how supreme is the benevolence of the sage! The meaning of the Great Treatise (Dazhuan) is that the sage fully realizes his nature through the Changes (Yi), and his benevolence is already seen in how his Way brings aid to all without being swept away. Yet how could it be limited to that alone? Why? Benevolence is rooted in the mind; its substance is unceasing, and its love is inexhaustible. title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
遇不以遇戕吾德順逆隨其所值安焉而已也
天理之周流一息匪間蓋無欲而好之者惟仁
矣常變隨其所遭順焉而已也元善之浹洽無
適不然蓋中心安之者惟仁矣夫心以仁爲體
渾然立愛之原則愛因心而施擴然仁覆之度
仁無我者也視天下人皆我也立人達人舉一
世康濟之聖人民胞之心固其獨至矣仁無物
者也視萬物皆一體也因物付物舉天下阜成
之聖人物與之懷固其恒切矣此所謂道濟之
===
仁仁之至也一地之博厚載物也然非易何以
哉甞觀之夫子在陳無慍在匡無懼爲司寇而
魯大治何者非安何者非仁老安少懷其愛之
在於萬物可見者故其言曰仁者安仁噫安仁
未易能也其利仁乎程子曰一命之士苟存心
於愛物於人必有所濟此立愛之端學易者勗
之
書
禹曰都帝愼乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止
punctuated:
遇，不以遇戕吾德。順逆隨其所值，安焉而已也。天理之周流，一息匪間，蓋無欲而好之者，惟仁矣。常變隨其所遭，順焉而已也。元善之浹洽，無適不然，蓋中心安之者，惟仁矣。夫心以仁爲體，渾然立愛之原；則愛因心而施，擴然仁覆之度。仁無我者也，視天下人皆我也。立人達人，舉一世康濟之，聖人民胞之心，固其獨至矣。仁無物者也，視萬物皆一體也。因物付物，舉天下阜成之，聖人物與之懷，固其恒切矣。此所謂道濟之仁，仁之至也，一地之博厚載物也。然非《易》何以哉？甞觀之夫子，在陳無慍，在匡無懼，爲司寇而魯大治，何者非安？何者非仁？老安少懷，其愛之在於萬物可見者。故其言曰：「仁者安仁。」噫！安仁未易能也，其利仁乎！程子曰：「一命之士，苟存心於愛物，於人必有所濟。」此立愛之端，學《易》者勗之。
《書》
禹曰：「都！帝，愼乃在位。」帝曰：「俞！」禹曰：「安汝止，
translation_en:
… circumstances, and does not allow circumstances to harm his virtue. Whether meeting with thuận (favorable) or逆 (adverse) fortune, he simply rests content with whatever he encounters. The circulation of Heavenly Principle does not cease for a single breath; indeed, having no desires, what he delights in is benevolence alone. Whether encountering constancy or change, he simply accords with whatever befalls him. The pervasive nourishment of primal goodness is present everywhere; indeed, what the core of his mind rests content in is benevolence alone. Now, since the mind takes benevolence as its substance, it is the undifferentiated source that establishes love; and as love is dispensed in accordance with the mind, it has the expansive measure of all-sheltering benevolence. Benevolence has no self: it regards all people in the world as oneself. Establishing others and helping others succeed, bringing peace and relief to the entire age—the sage's mind of regarding all people as his compatriots is assuredly supreme in him alone. Benevolence sets no barrier between self and things: it regards the myriad things as one body. Responding to each thing according to its own nature, bringing abundance and completion to all under heaven—the sage's sentiment of regarding all things as his companions is assuredly ever-earnest in him. This is what is meant by the benevolence that brings salvation through the Way; it is the ultimate of benevolence, just like the breadth and thickness of the earth supporting all things. Yet without the Book of Changes (Yi), how could this be achieved? Consider the Master: in Chen he felt no resentment, in Kuang he felt no fear, and when he served as Minister of Justice, Lu was brought to great order. Which of these was not resting content? Which of these was not benevolence? "To bring comfort to the aged and to cherish the young"—in this, his love abiding in the myriad things can be seen. Thus his words say: "The benevolent person rests content in benevolence." Alas! Resting content in benevolence is not easily achieved; perhaps one should seek to benefit from benevolence! Master Cheng said: "If a scholar of the lowest official rank truly keeps his mind set on loving living things, he is sure to be of some aid to others." This is the beginning of establishing love; let those who study the Book of Changes exert themselves in it.

無餘蘊矣且有虞之世舜爲之君而禹弼之位

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jing 經 comments: The way of governance of the house of Yu [Shun] uniquely flourished in antiquity simply because ruler and minister were cautious regarding the throne. This essay elucidates the theme as though the author had witnessed it in person; it ought to be selected for inclusion.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: Broad, grand, and leisurely in pace, it deeply grasps the stylistic substance of the "Canons" and "Counsels" (Dian Mo) [of the Book of Documents].

Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: Warm, pure, classical, and substantial.

Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: Lustrous and limpid.

The great minister instructs the sage ruler on the need to be cautious on the throne, and thereby sets forth in detail the way of such caution.

Extreme indeed is the difficulty of the ruler's position! Only when cultivation is mutually pursued both inwardly and outwardly is the way of being cautious on the throne exhausted without remainder. Now, in the age of the house of Yu, with Shun 舜 as ruler and Yu 禹 assisting him, there was assuredly no lack of caution regarding the throne. Yet Yu's concern was still unending; sighing in admiration, he set forth before the Emperor: "The position of ruler is of the utmost weight—how could it be a place for self-indulgence? If for a single day one is not heedful, boundless anxieties take root therein; though the age be brought to order, how can one who cautiously cultivates himself forget this? If a single thought becomes lax, the sorrows of the Four Seas are portended therein; though the people now have grain to eat, how can one who is cautious in his actions neglect this?" Such was Yu's untiring mind, and the Emperor assuredly felt a deep accord with it.

Taking advantage of the Emperor's assent, Yu then advanced further, saying: "The way of being cautious on the throne is nothing other than mutually cultivating both the inward and the outward. title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
微者著而心焉一安於善其制事也省其發省
其安而事焉一從乎心如是而脩之於内矣輔
此位者臣也君心未安則格君之心而啟沃皆
直辭君事未當則正君之事而匡捄皆直道又
如是而脩之於外焉斯則心事並醇其功已至
而君臣交警其道益完由是而天人且莫之違
矣慎位之道其至已哉噫此固盛世君臣授受
心法也故禹之告舜曰慎乃在位而舜之命禹
亦曰慎乃有位其心一也相契之深有以夫然
===
考文王之爲政又曰罔知罔兼若居已於逸者
何哉保治功者不可無舜禹之慎識治體者不
可無文王之逸兩者並觀始得
世篤忠貞服勞王家
余雲標
同考試官訓導經 批 世臣忠貞濟美發揮殆盡
而詞婉誼正尤得周王感動君牙之意
同考試官敎諭陳 批 形容大臣以心勤國處令
人躍然起思
punctuated:
微者著，而心焉一安於善；其制事也，省其發、省其安，而事焉一從乎心。如是而脩之於内矣。輔此位者，臣也。君心未安，則格君之心，而啟沃皆直辭；君事未當，則正君之事，而匡捄皆直道。又如是而脩之於外焉。斯則心事並醇，其功已至；而君臣交警，其道益完。由是而天人且莫之違矣，慎位之道其至已哉！噫，此固盛世君臣授受心法也。故禹之告舜曰：「慎乃在位。」而舜之命禹亦曰：「慎乃有位。」其心一也，相契之深，有以夫！然考文王之爲政，又曰「罔知罔兼」，若居已於逸者，何哉？保治功者，不可無舜、禹之慎；識治體者，不可無文王之逸。兩者並觀始得。

世篤忠貞，服勞王家。
余雲標
同考試官訓導經批：世臣忠貞濟美，發揮殆盡，而詞婉誼正，尤得周王感動君牙之意。

translation_en:
… and what is subtle is made manifest, so that the mind abides wholly in goodness; in regulating affairs, he examines their inception and examines their restful completion, so that affairs wholly follow the mind. In this manner, cultivation is achieved within. Those who assist in this position are the ministers. When the sovereign's mind is not yet at rest in goodness, they rectify the sovereign's mind, and their enlightening counsels are all forthright words; when the sovereign's affairs are not yet proper, they correct the sovereign's affairs, and their rectifying aid follows the straight path. In this manner, too, cultivation is achieved from without. Thus, mind and affairs are both pure, their achievement having reached the utmost; sovereign and minister mutually admonish one another, their Way becoming ever more complete. From this, neither Heaven nor man will oppose them—how consummate indeed is the Way of being cautious in one's position! Alas, this was truly the mental discipline transmitted between sovereign and minister in a flourishing age. Therefore, when Yu counselled Shun, he said, "Be cautious in the position you occupy," and when Shun charged Yu, he likewise said, "Be cautious in the position you hold." Their minds were one; how profound were the grounds of their mutual accord! Yet when we examine the governance of King Wen, it is also said that he "neither took personal cognizance nor combined duties," as though placing himself in ease—why is this? Those who preserve the achievements of governance cannot be without the caution of Shun and Yu; those who understand the essential body of governance cannot be without the ease of King Wen. Only by viewing both together does one grasp it.

"Generation after generation they maintained steadfast loyalty and fidelity, laboring in the service of the royal house."
Yu Yunbiao 
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jing: How hereditary ministers perpetuate the excellence of their loyalty and fidelity is expounded almost exhaustively, while the gentle phrasing and righteous import especially capture the Zhou king's intention in moving Junya.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen: The depiction of great ministers devoting their minds to diligent service for the state makes the reader's thoughts leap with inspiration.

蓋曰國家所以重世臣者非以爵祿私其家也
謂其風之足以啓後而代有作求之嗣也吾嘗
憶爾祖父而重有感矣彼盡心之謂忠純心之
謂貞固服勞之本而王家之幹也世篤之者鮮
===
矣惟爾祖父心存爲國恒誠確之不渝事在勤
王尤夙夜之匪懈爾祖之忠誠固作之孚先矣
而爾父則世守之懷忠以報國將奕世而重光
爾祖之貞一固貽之家法矣而爾父則世求之
含貞以從王歷再傳而不泯王家有敎民之事
也自此心之忠貞者以左右有民啓其思翼其
行後先相望賢勞殆可想矣王家有養民之事
也自此心之忠貞者以宣力四方恤其隱圖其
安述作相承勳勞今未艾矣蓋在我先王也以
punctuated:
考試官敎諭丘批：古健中有欵曲。
考試官敎諭姚批：雅潔可誦。
觀世臣以心勤國，而後人當知所法矣。夫大臣事君以心也，而盡心王家者至世世焉，其垂範於後之人者如是哉！宜周王述之以感君牙也。蓋曰：國家所以重世臣者，非以爵祿私其家也，謂其風之足以啓後，而代有作求之嗣也。吾嘗憶爾祖、父而重有感矣。彼盡心之謂忠，純心之謂貞，固服勞之本而王家之幹也，世篤之者鮮矣。惟爾祖、父，心存爲國，恒誠確之不渝；事在勤王，尤夙夜之匪懈。爾祖之忠誠，固作之孚先矣，而爾父則世守之，懷忠以報國，將奕世而重光；爾祖之貞一，固貽之家法矣，而爾父則世求之，含貞以從王，歷再傳而不泯。王家有敎民之事也，自此心之忠貞者，以左右有民，啓其思，翼其行，後先相望，賢勞殆可想矣；王家有養民之事也，自此心之忠貞者，以宣力四方，恤其隱，圖其安，述作相承，勳勞今未艾矣。蓋在我先王也，以
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: Within its archaic vigor there is nuanced intricacy.
Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: Elegant, clean, and worthy of recitation.
Observing how hereditary ministers toil for the state with their hearts, their descendants ought to know what to take as their model. Now, a great minister serves his ruler with his heart; when devoting one's heart to the royal house extends from generation to generation, how great is the example thus bequeathed to later men! Fitting it is that the King of Zhou recounted this to move Jun Ya 君牙. It is as if he said: The reason the state esteems hereditary ministers is not to show private favor to their families with noble ranks and emoluments; rather, it is because their moral influence suffices to inspire posterity, so that in each generation there are heirs who actively seek to match their predecessors. Whenever I recall your grandfather and father, I am deeply moved. Devoting one's heart entirely is called loyalty; keeping one's heart pure is called constancy. These are truly the root of toiling in service and the mainstay of the royal house, yet few are those who earnestly practice them generation after generation. Only your grandfather and father kept their hearts set on serving the state, ever sincere, steadfast, and unswerving; in the work of toiling for the king, they were especially untiring from morning to night. Your grandfather's loyal sincerity indeed established a trustworthy precedent beforehand [?], and your father preserved it across the generations—cherishing loyalty to repay the state, so that through successive generations its splendor was renewed. Your grandfather's constant singleness of heart indeed bequeathed a family standard, and your father sought to live up to it across the generations—harboring constancy to follow the king, so that through two transmissions it was not extinguished. The royal house has the task of instructing the people; proceeding from the loyalty and constancy of this heart, they assisted and guided the people, awakening their thoughts and supporting their conduct—looking to one another from predecessor to successor, their worthy toils can well be imagined. The royal house has the task of nourishing the people; proceeding from the loyalty and constancy of this heart, they exerted their strength throughout the four quarters, showing compassion for the people's hidden sufferings and planning for their security—inheriting and continuing one another's work, their meritorious toils even now have not ceased. For on the part of our former kings, in…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
求舊之意用人旣不負於其臣在爾祖父也以
承家之心報國自不負於其君今爾世其官而
知法焉則王家益賴而先烈彌光矣可不勉哉
大抵莫爲之前雖美弗彰莫爲之後雖盛弗傳
故必有繼述之人而後忠貞之念可以寄之於
不窮有臣若斯卽與國咸休也固宜豈世官世
祿云乎故伊陟象賢丁公繼美將以世而益重
矣美哉泱泱乎臣道之光哉
詩
===
樂只君子天子葵之
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批葵字發揮最難是作體格莊
重意旨瑩明宛然盛世氣象足占所蘊
同考試官訓導李批發明君臣相得意宏麗典
雅錄之以式
考試官敎諭丘批意融詞鬯
考試官敎諭姚批雋永有味
觀周臣受知於君其必有以感之矣甚矣人臣
punctuated:
求舊之意用人，旣不負於其臣；在爾祖父也，以承家之心報國，自不負於其君。今爾世其官而知法焉，則王家益賴，而先烈彌光矣，可不勉哉！大抵莫爲之前，雖美弗彰；莫爲之後，雖盛弗傳。故必有繼述之人，而後忠貞之念可以寄之於不窮。有臣若斯，卽與國咸休也固宜，豈世官世祿云乎！故伊陟象賢，丁公繼美，將以世而益重矣。美哉泱泱乎，臣道之光哉！

詩
「樂只君子，天子葵之。」
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批：葵字發揮最難。是作體格莊重，意旨瑩明，宛然盛世氣象，足占所蘊。
同考試官訓導李批：發明君臣相得意，宏麗典雅，錄之以式。
考試官敎諭丘批：意融詞鬯。
考試官敎諭姚批：雋永有味。

觀周臣受知於君，其必有以感之矣。甚矣，人臣…
translation_en:
…the intention of seeking out men of old families, they surely did not fail their subjects; and as for your grandfather and father, repaying the state with the heart of carrying on the family tradition, they naturally did not fail their rulers. Now if you inherit their offices and know how to take them as your model, the royal house will rely on you all the more, and the illustrious achievements of your ancestors will shine even brighter. How could you not exert yourself! In general, if there is no one to go before, even beauty will not be made manifest; if there is no one to follow after, even flourishing virtue will not be transmitted. Therefore, there must be someone to inherit and carry on the work before the spirit of loyalty and constancy can be entrusted to endless generations. When there are ministers such as these, it is certainly fitting that they share in the fortunes of the state—how could it merely be a matter of hereditary office and hereditary emolument! Thus Yi Zhi (伊陟) resembled the worthy example of his father, and Duke Ding (丁公) continued the fine virtue of his predecessor; across the generations they became ever more esteemed. How admirable, how grand and expansive—truly the glory of the way of the minister!

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"Happy be the lord, / The Son of Heaven measures his merits."
Chen Wenxuan (陳文選)
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Su (蘇): Elaborating on the word "measures" (kui 葵) is most difficult. This composition has a dignified structure and clear, luminous meaning; it vividly captures the spirit of a flourishing age, sufficient to reveal the author's inner cultivation.
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li (李): It elucidates the idea of mutual rapport between ruler and minister in a grand, splendid, and classically elegant manner. It is recorded here as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Qiu (丘): The ideas are harmonious and the diction fluent.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yao (姚): Richly meaningful and full of flavor.
