title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
知遇之難也可樂如君子而受知于君也非其
必然者乎采菽天子所以答魚藻也若曰君臣
之相臨者分而其相孚者心以心獲上吾於來
朝君子有取焉蓋其欽翼中存而溢于泰交者
藹然溫文之度寅恭外著而形于晉接者怡然
豈弟之風君子洵可樂也而天子之葵與否其
何敢必焉然在國之忠貞旣感通之有素而在
朝之齊遬自孚契之益深天子照臨百官本無
微不察者匪紓如君子必將曰此其爲我周之
藎臣乎而推誠以待之者攣如也天子智臨萬
國亦無隱弗達者殿邦如君子必將曰此其爲
我周之良翰乎而推心以置之者翕如也念切
忠君其自許於生平者則然乃天子則旣諒其
忠焉而帝心簡在喜起其交孚矣所以共成豈
樂之休風者不在是乎心存愛國其自盟於獨
知者則然乃天子亦旣然其信焉而宸衷眷注
明良其合德矣所以共保那居之盛治者其在
茲乎信乎君子以天子之心爲心而赤芾邪幅
punctuated: 知遇之難也。可樂如君子，而受知于君也，非其必然者乎？《采菽》，天子所以答《魚藻》也，若曰：君臣之相臨者，分；而其相孚者，心。以心獲上，吾於來朝君子有取焉。蓋其欽翼中存，而溢于泰交者，藹然溫文之度；寅恭外著，而形于晉接者，怡然豈弟之風。君子洵可樂也，而天子之葵與否，其何敢必焉？然在國之忠貞，旣感通之有素；而在朝之齊遬，自孚契之益深。天子照臨百官，本無微不察者，匪紓如君子，必將曰：「此其爲我周之藎臣乎！」而推誠以待之者，攣如也。天子智臨萬國，亦無隱弗達者，殿邦如君子，必將曰：「此其爲我周之良翰乎！」而推心以置之者，翕如也。念切忠君，其自許於生平者則然，乃天子則旣諒其忠焉，而帝心簡在，喜起其交孚矣，所以共成豈樂之休風者，不在是乎？心存愛國，其自盟於獨知者則然，乃天子亦旣然其信焉，而宸衷眷注，明良其合德矣，所以共保那居之盛治者，其在茲乎？信乎！君子以天子之心爲心，而赤芾邪幅
translation_en: … how difficult it is to gain the appreciative recognition of one's ruler! When a noble man is so worthy of delight and therefore receives the appreciative recognition of his ruler, is that not an inevitable outcome? The ode "Plucking the Beans" (Caishu) was how the Son of Heaven replied to "Fish in the Pondweed" (Yuzao). It is as if to say: What governs the hierarchy between ruler and subject is status, yet what binds them in mutual trust is the heart. In winning the confidence of one's superior through the heart, I find much to commend in these noble men who have come to court. For the reverent caution preserved within them overflows in harmonious communion as a genial, gentle, and refined demeanor; the respectful humility manifested without takes form in court audiences as a cheerful, easy, and fraternal air. The noble men are truly worthy of delight, yet whether the Son of Heaven would gauge their hearts or not—how could they dare take that for granted? Nevertheless, since their loyal integrity in their fiefs had long established a sympathetic resonance, their reverent and circumspect deportment at court naturally deepened that mutual accord all the more. The Son of Heaven shines down upon the hundred officials, and there is inherently nothing so subtle that he does not perceive; seeing the noble men so untiring and unremitting, he will surely say: "Are these not the devoted subjects of our Zhou?" And thus his extending of sincere trust in treating them is closely bound indeed. The Son of Heaven rules the myriad states with wisdom, and there is likewise nothing so hidden that he does not comprehend; seeing the noble men stabilizing the realm, he will surely say: "Are these not the fine bulwarks of our Zhou?" And thus his reposing of heartfelt confidence in them is harmonious indeed. Earnestly devoted to loyalty to their ruler—such was the standard they set for themselves throughout their lives; and now the Son of Heaven has already understood their loyalty. Selected in the sovereign's heart, they rejoice and rise up in mutual trust. Does not the way they jointly achieve the splendid custom of joyous harmony lie precisely in this? Harbouring love for the state in their hearts—such was the vow they swore to themselves in their solitary conscience; and now the Son of Heaven has likewise affirmed their good faith. With the imperial bosomfixing its affectionate regard upon them, the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers unite in virtue. Does not the way they jointly preserve the flourishing governance of tranquil dwelling lie right here? Truly, the noble men take the heart of the Son of Heaven as their own heart, whereas the red knee-covers and slant-wrapped leg-bindings…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之交其餘也故天子以君子之心爲心而車馬
黼衮之予亦其餘也盛時君臣相得而治道益
彰也如是夫雖然此特君之諒臣者然耳而臣
猶不敢恃也卽周公位極人臣勤勞王室至吐
握拮据身任天下之重而不辭成王不啻葵之
矣而赤舄几几公何自有焉噫千載而下守成
業而致盛治者頌成王之德而稱周公之功不
衰故事君若周公者可也
思齊大任文王之母思媚周姜京室之婦
===
===
大姒嗣徽音則百斯男
許文俊
同考試官訓導蘇 批 聖母賢妃文德所由盛是作
透徹渾融詞理精詣眞大雅之文錄之
同考試官訓導李 批 發明題意婉約詳盡佳
士佳士
考試官敎諭丘 批 醇雅蘊藉
考試官敎諭姚 批 明瑩可式
詩人歌聖德而推本於母之聖妃之賢焉夫文
punctuated:
之交其餘也；故天子以君子之心爲心，而車馬、黼衮之予亦其餘也。盛時君臣相得，而治道益彰也如是夫！雖然，此特君之諒臣者然耳，而臣猶不敢恃也。卽周公位極人臣，勤勞王室，至吐握拮据，身任天下之重而不辭；成王不啻葵之矣，而「赤舄几几」，公何自有焉？噫！千載而下，守成業而致盛治者，頌成王之德而稱周公之功不衰。故事君若周公者，可也。

「思齊大任，文王之母，思媚周姜，京室之婦。大姒嗣徽音，則百斯男。」
許文俊
同考試官訓導蘇批：聖母賢妃，文德所由盛。是作透徹渾融，詞理精詣，眞大雅之文。錄之。
同考試官訓導李批：發明題意，婉約詳盡。佳士！佳士！
考試官敎諭丘批：醇雅蘊藉。
考試官敎諭姚批：明瑩可式。

詩人歌聖德，而推本於母之聖、妃之賢焉。夫文
translation_en:
… presentation of red knee-covers and leg-wrappers is merely secondary; therefore the Son of Heaven takes the mind of the noble man as his own mind, and the bestowal of carriages, horses, and embroidered ceremonial robes is likewise secondary. Such was the mutual understanding between ruler and minister in a flourishing age, whereby the way of governance became ever more manifest! Even so, this describes only how the ruler trusts his ministers, whereas the minister still dares not presume upon it. Take the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公): having reached the highest rank attainable by a subject, he toiled for the royal house, spitting out his food and grasping his hair to receive worthy men, laboring strenuously and taking the heavy burden of the world upon himself without shrinking. King Cheng (Chengwang 成王) more than measured and understood him, yet with "his red slippers så composed and dignified," what did the Duke ever claim for himself? Ah! A thousand years later, those who preserve an established patrimony and achieve flourishing governance still extol the virtue of King Cheng and praise the achievements of the Duke of Zhou without cease. Therefore, to serve one's ruler as the Duke of Zhou did is the proper standard.

"Reverent was Tai Ren, the mother of King Wen; loving and compliant was she toward Zhou Jiang, a wife of the capital house. Tai Si succeeded to her admirable renown, and a hundred sons were born."
By Xu Wenjun 許文俊.

Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: Clear and lustrous, worthy to serve as a model.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
王天縱之聖也以母妃而咸有一德所以成之
助之者不有自乎歌文德者推本言之若曰文
王聖德之純雖由於所性而有相之道亦存乎
其人何以言之母而聖也所以成其始文王之
母則大任是已端莊誠一之懿雖不可以易窺
然其持身也以敬思齊之度儼乎中宮之母儀
也其事周姜也以孝思媚之風稱乎京室之婦
順也以是聖母而生我文王則淵源之有自非
止一朝一夕之故矣所以成之者不既遠乎妃
===
而賢也所以代其終文王之妃則大姒是已幽
閒貞靜之蘊雖不可以易測然孝以承先休而
徽音昭世濟之美德之光前者可稱也慈以逮
羣下而斯男衍則百之多德之裕後者可徵也
以是賢妃而配我文王則內治之克相非特一
健一順之常矣所以助之者不既深乎要之天
爲有周而生文王天爲文王而生大任大姒此
固天倫之獨盛而周之德其可謂至德也已矣
抑不特此也父王季子武王文之無憂者夫子
punctuated: 王天縱之聖也，以母妃而咸有一德，所以成之、助之者，不有自乎？歌文德者推本言之，若曰：文王聖德之純，雖由於所性，而有相之道，亦存乎其人。何以言之？母而聖也，所以成其始。文王之母，則大任是已。端莊誠一之懿，雖不可以易窺；然其持身也以敬，「思齊」之度，儼乎中宮之母儀也；其事周姜也以孝，「思媚」之風，稱乎京室之婦順也。以是聖母而生我文王，則淵源之有自，非止一朝一夕之故矣。所以成之者，不既遠乎？妃而賢也，所以代其終。文王之妃，則大姒是已。幽閒貞靜之蘊，雖不可以易測；然孝以承先休，而「徽音」昭世濟之美，德之光前者可稱也；慈以逮羣下，而「斯男」衍「則百」之多，德之裕後者可徵也。以是賢妃而配我文王，則內治之克相，非特一健一順之常矣。所以助之者，不既深乎？要之，天爲有周而生文王，天爲文王而生大任、大姒。此固天倫之獨盛，而周之德其可謂至德也已矣。抑不特此也，父王季，子武王，文之無憂者，夫子…
translation_en:
…King Wen was a sage endowed by Heaven. Yet since his mother and his consort both possessed pure and single-minded virtue, did not that which brought him to completion and assisted him have its source? In singing of King Wen's virtue, the poet traced it back to its root, as if to say: Although the purity of King Wen's sagely virtue came from his innate nature, the way of mutual assistance also depended upon those around him.

How may this be explained? When a mother is sagely, she brings the beginning to completion. The mother of King Wen was none other than Tairen. Although her dignified, reverent, sincere, and undivided excellence cannot easily be fathomed, in conducting herself with reverence, her demeanor in "reverently behavioral" ("Siqi") was truly the maternal model of the central palace; and in serving Taijiang of Zhou with filial piety, her bearing in "loving devotion" ("Simei") matched the wifely obedience expected in the royal house. For such a sagely mother to give birth to our King Wen meant that the fountainhead had its origin, and it was not the work of a single morning or a single evening. Was not that by which she brought him to completion far-reaching indeed?

When a consort is worthy, she carries the work through to its end. The consort of King Wen was none other than Taisi. Although the depth of her secluded, serene, chaste, and quiet character cannot easily be measured, through her filial piety she succeeded to the excellence of her predecessors, so that her "fine reputation" ("huiyin") made manifest the beauty of successive generations, and her virtue in glorifying those before her was worthy of praise; and through her kindness she reached down to all below, so that "these sons" ("sinan") multiplied to "a hundred in number" ("zebai"), and her virtue in enriching posterity could be verified. For such a worthy consort to be matched with our King Wen meant that her capable assistance in governing the inner quarters went beyond the ordinary pairing of firmness and docility. Was not that by which she assisted him profound indeed?

In sum, Heaven gave birth to King Wen for the House of Zhou, and Heaven gave birth to Tairen and Taisi for King Wen. This was indeed a unique flourishing of heavenly human relationships, and the virtue of Zhou may truly be called supreme virtue! And it was not only this: with King Ji as his father and King Wu as his son, that King Wen had no cause for sorrow is what the Master [Confucius]…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
獨賛之而此詩曰大任大姒蓋當時歌其德而
推本言之耳然則文王內外之所值其古今帝
王之僅見者乎雖然小心翼翼望道未見文王
且不自知其聖也噫此文王之所以爲文歟
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕秋
公會宋人齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕
公會齊人宋人救鄭〔莊公二十有八年〕

===
王命衮

歷觀伯國節制之師而知伯臣善用其民矣夫
兵貴有制也齊桓壹以節制之師行之則管氏
之力哉昔桓也圖伯而管子以天下才相之君
臣之間拳拳規畫亡他策也唯以民不可重役
punctuated:
獨賛之，而此詩曰大任、大姒，蓋當時歌其德而推本言之耳。然則文王內外之所值，其古今帝王之僅見者乎！雖然，小心翼翼，望道未見，文王且不自知其聖也。噫，此文王之所以爲文歟！

春秋
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕；秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕；公會齊人、宋人救鄭〔莊公二十有八年〕；齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕。

translation_en:
… uniquely praised it, whereas this ode speaks of Tairen and Taisi because at the time people sang of his virtue and traced it back to its origins. That being so, were not the domestic and external circumstances that King Wen encountered rarely seen among emperors and kings of past and present? Even so, cautiously and reverently, looking toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it, King Wen did not even consider himself a sage. Ah, is this not why King Wen was "Wen" (the Cultured)?

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In autumn, men of Song, men of Qi, and men of Zhu invaded Ni" [fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang]; "in autumn, the Duke met with men of Song and men of Qi to invade Xu" [twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang]; "the Duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to rescue Zheng" [twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang]; "men of Qi rescued Xing" [first year of Duke Min].

Wang Minggun

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
重役則疲賦不可橫斂橫斂則匱財匱力疲將
焉用之於是作內政以寄軍令焉將不大夫兵
不大眾蓋二十餘年于茲矣有如郕之伐徐之
伐討有罪也彼其不恪而吾武威臨之豈不能
悉力以耀中原哉顧國有討貳之制吾勿敢踰
兵莫重乎討貳之二役者則節兵之一驗也又
如鄭之救邢之救恤無辜也彼其孔棘而吾簡
書是畏豈不能大舉以惠親暱哉顧國有恤患
之制吾勿敢踰兵莫重乎恤患之二役者又節
===
兵之一驗也夫以山東之蓋藏臨淄之武悍固
最勝之遺而宇內稱雄者也加以二十年休養
生息而師徒不頓民不罷勞盡章章如是則夫
一舉而用之南無楚西無秦晉又豈待異日見
哉春秋於數役皆以人書蓋紀其素所節制者
然也匪直伐宋為爾矣仲父謀國之功胡可少
耶攷之內政之作大抵倣比閭族黨之遺也顧
周以王而齊僅以伯則以功利之私與關睢麟
趾之意所操者異耳厥後晉也州兵魏也戍卒
punctuated: 重役則疲；賦不可橫斂，橫斂則匱。財匱力疲，將焉用之？於是作內政以寄軍令焉。將不大夫，兵不大眾，蓋二十餘年于茲矣。有如郕之伐、徐之伐，討有罪也。彼其不恪，而吾武威臨之，豈不能悉力以耀中原哉？顧國有討貳之制，吾勿敢踰。兵莫重乎討貳，之二役者，則節兵之一驗也。又如鄭之救、邢之救，恤無辜也。彼其孔棘，而吾簡書是畏，豈不能大舉以惠親暱哉？顧國有恤患之制，吾勿敢踰。兵莫重乎恤患，之二役者，又節兵之一驗也。夫以山東之蓋藏，臨淄之武悍，固最勝之遺而宇內稱雄者也。加以二十年休養生息，而師徒不頓，民不罷勞，盡章章如是。則夫一舉而用之，南無楚，西無秦、晉，又豈待異日見哉？《春秋》於數役皆以「人」書，蓋紀其素所節制者然也，匪直伐宋為爾矣。仲父謀國之功，胡可少耶？攷之內政之作，大抵倣比閭族黨之遺也。顧周以王而齊僅以伯，則以功利之私，與《關睢》、《麟趾》之意所操者異耳。厥後晉也州兵，魏也戍卒，
translation_en: …for if burdened with heavy labor, they become exhausted; and that taxes must not be arbitrarily levied, for if arbitrarily levied, resources become depleted. When wealth is depleted and strength is exhausted, of what use will they be? Thereupon, he instituted domestic administration in which to lodge military commands. The commanders were not Great Officers, and the troops were not massive hosts—it had been thus for over twenty years. For instance, the campaigns against Cheng and against Xu were to punish the guilty. Since they were irreverent and we confronted them with our martial might, could we not have mobilized all our strength to dazzle the Central Plains? Yet the state had regulations for punishing the disloyal, which we dared not transgress. No military action is weightier than punishing the disloyal, and these two campaigns are one proof of his restraint in using troops. Or again, the rescues of Zheng and of Xing were to succor the innocent. Since they were in dire urgency and we stood in awe of the dispatch tablets calling for aid, could we not have launched a grand mobilization to show favor to our close kin and allies? Yet the state had regulations for succoring those in distress, which we dared not transgress. No military action is weightier than succoring those in distress, and these two campaigns are another proof of his restraint in using troops. Now, with the accumulated stores of Shandong and the martial fierceness of Linzi, Qi truly possessed a legacy of supreme superiority and was renowned as a dominant power within the realm. Add to this twenty years of resting and nurturing the people, so that the army was not dulled and the populace was not worn out—all as manifestly clear as this. Thus, when he mobilized and employed them at a single stroke, there was no Chu to the south and no Qin or Jin to the west; why would one need to wait for a later day to see this? In all several of these campaigns, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the actors simply as "men" (ren), which is to document how they were habitually kept under disciplined restraint; it was not only in the campaign against Song that this was so. How could the merit of Uncle Zhong [Guan Zhong] in planning for the state be belittled? If we examine the institution of his domestic administration, in general outline it imitated the legacy of the Zhou local units of bi, lü, zu, and dang. Yet Zhou thereby became true kings while Qi merely became hegemon, simply because the selfishness of utilitarian gain differed in its guiding principle from the spirit of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes. Thereafter, with the district troops (zhoubing) of Jin, the garrison conscripts (shuzu) of Wei,…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
秦也甲士兵制之變日紛紛焉又内政作之俑
也於戲固世變使然哉
齊人歸讙及闡哀公八年
陳焺
同考試官教諭張批是題傳意甚婉作者語多
纏縛子能會傳成文意瑩詞朗可以錄矣
考試官教諭丘批辭理明盡
考試官教諭姚批能發聖人美魯之意
春秋紀歸地者之順所以揚君美也夫讙闡之
===
歸順矣魯實以順召之美不既章乎慨自邾益
為俘齊人震怒一舉而下魯二邑焉讙闡之緼
于齊也有日矣一旦疆域之外有奉輿圖而至
者豈其遽念太師盟府之藏而無愛於魯哉蓋
恒物之情可以逆亦可以順人心之順有所感
必有所應彼魯以逆怒齊齊亦以逆蹙魯幾不
可為國矣幸魯也悔禍而俘君釋於負瑕故齊
也輸心而侵疆歸於東土仇讎息而甥舅如初
孰徴之也齊所以起戎第愛一邾耳邾安而我
punctuated:
秦也甲士，兵制之變日紛紛焉，又内政作之俑也。於戲，固世變使然哉！

齊人歸讙及闡（哀公八年）
陳焺
同考試官教諭張批：是題傳意甚婉，作者語多纏縛，子能會傳成文，意瑩詞朗，可以錄矣。
考試官教諭丘批：辭理明盡。
考試官教諭姚批：能發聖人美魯之意。

《春秋》紀歸地者之順，所以揚君美也。夫讙、闡之歸，順矣，魯實以順召之，美不既章乎？慨自邾益為俘，齊人震怒，一舉而下魯二邑焉，讙、闡之緼于齊也有日矣。一旦疆域之外，有奉輿圖而至者，豈其遽念太師盟府之藏，而無愛於魯哉？蓋恒物之情，可以逆亦可以順，人心之順，有所感必有所應。彼魯以逆怒齊，齊亦以逆蹙魯，幾不可為國矣。幸魯也悔禍，而俘君釋於負瑕；故齊也輸心，而侵疆歸於東土。仇讎息而甥舅如初，孰徴之也？齊所以起戎，第愛一邾耳；邾安而我
translation_en:
… and the armored soldiers of Qin—changes in the military system grew increasingly tumultuous day by day, and it was the "internal administration" (neizheng) that started this bad precedent. Alas! Was this not indeed brought about by the transformations of the age?

"The People of Qi Returned Huan and Chan" (Eighth Year of Duke Ai)
By Chen Sheng

Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang's comment: On this topic, the meaning of the commentary is quite subtle, and writers often get tangled up in their words. You have grasped the commentary to compose your essay; the ideas are lucid and the diction is clear. It is worthy of selection.
Examiner, Instructor Qiu's comment: The diction and reasoning are clear and thorough.
Examiner, Instructor Yao's comment: Able to bring out the Sage's intention in praising Lu.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the tractability of those who returned territory in order to extol the ruler's virtue. Now, the return of Huan and Chan was an act of tractability, and since Lu had in fact invited it through its own tractability, was not its virtue thereby made manifest? Alas, ever since Yi of Zhu was taken captive, the people of Qi were enraged and at one stroke captured two towns of Lu; Huan and Chan had been bound [?] to Qi for some time. When one day from beyond the borders someone came bearing the maps and registers of those lands, could it be that Qi suddenly remembered the archives of the Grand Preceptor's covenant repository and begrudged nothing to Lu? Indeed, the nature of ordinary affairs is such that one may act with defiance or with tractability; and as for tractability in the human heart, where there is a stimulus there is surely a response. Previously, Lu had provoked Qi's anger through defiance, and Qi likewise pressed Lu hard through defiance, to the point where Lu could scarcely survive as a state. Fortunately, Lu regretted the calamity and released the captive ruler from Fuxia; therefore, Qi yielded its heart and returned the invaded territory to the eastern land. Enmity ceased and the marriage-alliance relations of nephew and uncle were restored as before—what brought this to pass? The reason Qi had raised arms was merely out of affection for Zhu alone; once Zhu was secure, our…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之封境舉安蓋勢有必至矣和好通而疆里如
故孰正之也我所以召釁第虐一郕耳郕歸而
我之故宇隨歸蓋理有固然矣夫舉全魯之力
不足以當齊而能以一念之善止其不戢以強
大之齊亦何厭之有而感于一念之善遂與維
新自是而魯得有辭于先公齊可自謝於天下
善之遷也過之改也寔兩國共之矣不然齊怒
未怠魯其有寧日乎春秋直書曰歸紀順也歸
者順則所以致之順者美可知已春秋之不諱
===
以益來也意在斯乎嗟嗟是亦聖人善則稱君
耳郕益之歸豈眞悔悟之萌而甘自戢也無乃
有怵心乎亡何復有于鄡之師卽甚不悛曷以
加玆矣聖人曲爲魯諱有是哉雖然春秋大改
過亦所以訓萬世也
禮記
故商者五帝之遺聲也商人識之故謂之
商齊者三代之遺聲也齊人識之故謂
之齊
punctuated:
之封境舉安，蓋勢有必至矣。和好通而疆里如故，孰正之也？我所以召釁，第虐一郕耳，郕歸而我之故宇隨歸，蓋理有固然矣。夫舉全魯之力，不足以當齊，而能以一念之善止其不戢；以強大之齊，亦何厭之有，而感于一念之善，遂與維新。自是而魯得有辭于先公，齊可自謝於天下。善之遷也，過之改也，寔兩國共之矣。不然，齊怒未怠，魯其有寧日乎？《春秋》直書曰「歸」，紀順也。歸者順，則所以致之順者，美可知已。《春秋》之不諱「以益來」也，意在斯乎！嗟嗟！是亦聖人善則稱君耳。郕益之歸，豈眞悔悟之萌而甘自戢也？無乃有怵心乎！亡何復有于鄡之師，卽甚不悛，曷以加玆矣！聖人曲爲魯諱，有是哉！雖然，《春秋》大改過，亦所以訓萬世也。

《禮記》
故商者，五帝之遺聲也，商人識之，故謂之商。齊者，三代之遺聲也，齊人識之，故謂之齊。
translation_en:
… our borders were all made secure; this was indeed an inevitable outcome of the circumstances. Peaceful relations were restored and the territory returned to how it was before—who set this right? The reason we invited hostility was merely by mistreating that one state of Zhu [here written Cheng 郕, i.e., Viscount Yi of Zhu]; once he was returned, our old lands were promptly returned as well, for such is the natural principle of things. Now, mustering the strength of the entire state of Lu was insufficient to withstand Qi, yet through a single good thought it was able to halt Qi's unchecked aggression; and as for mighty Qi, what limit was there to its greed, yet moved by a single good thought, it granted Lu a fresh start. From this, Lu had words with which to answer to its former dukes, and Qi could excuse itself before the world. Moving toward goodness and reforming past faults were truly shared by both states. Otherwise, with Qi's anger unabated, would Lu have had a single day of peace? The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) directly records it as "returned" (gui), registering compliance with what is right. Since the return was compliant, the beauty of that which brought about this compliance can easily be known. That the Spring and Autumn Annals did not conceal "coming with Yi [of Zhu]"—did its intention not lie in this? Alas! This too is simply the Sage attributing goodness to the ruler. Was the return of Yi from Cheng truly thesprouting of genuine remorse and a willingness to restrain oneself? Or was it rather out of fear in their hearts? Before long there was again the military expedition at Qiao—even the most unrepentant could not have gone further than this! Could it really be that the Sage went to such lengths to conceal Lu's faults? Even so, the Spring and Autumn Annals attaches great importance to reforming faults, which is also meant to instruct ten thousand generations.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore, the Shang [music] is the surviving sound of the Five Emperors; the people of Shang remembered it, and therefore it is called Shang. The Qi [music] is the surviving sound of the Three Dynasties; the people of Qi remembered it, and therefore it is called Qi."

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
黎時中
同考試官教諭蔣批此題類於轉拆處多見
繁擾是作剔盡浮詞冲融典雅必邃養之士也
同考試官教諭張批體格平正筆力俊健
可式
考試官教諭丘批善發帝王遺聲之意錄之
考試官教諭姚批清暢不凡
觀商齊之所由名者而其音足尚矣夫帝王往
矣而遺音存焉商齊人識之故稱斯名耳善歌
===
者可不知所自哉今夫歌之於人大矣極之則
功化甚神而本之則從出有自國風雅頌遠矣
何獨於商齊而疑之彼肆直而慈愛者宜歌商
人知商之音善矣然歌於商而不始於商也大
道為公而五帝興焉不有洩之為天地之元聲
者乎而今之所謂商者即其遺矣第歷數世之
後惟商人識之聲以商而存故名亦以商而起
耳即其音而求之當必有神交於五帝之隆者
豈燕溺之商巳耶溫良而能斷者宜歌齊人知
punctuated:
黎時中
同考試官教諭蔣批：此題類於轉拆處多見繁擾。是作剔盡浮詞，冲融典雅，必邃養之士也。
同考試官教諭張批：體格平正，筆力俊健，可式。
考試官教諭丘批：善發帝王遺聲之意，錄之。
考試官教諭姚批：清暢不凡。
觀商、齊之所由名者，而其音足尚矣。夫帝王往矣，而遺音存焉，商、齊人識之，故稱斯名耳。善歌者可不知所自哉？今夫歌之於人大矣，極之則功化甚神，而本之則從出有自。《國風》、《雅》、《頌》遠矣，何獨於商、齊而疑之？彼肆直而慈愛者，宜歌商。人知商之音善矣，然歌於商而不始於商也。大道為公，而五帝興焉，不有洩之為天地之元聲者乎？而今之所謂商者，即其遺矣。第歷數世之後，惟商人識之，聲以商而存，故名亦以商而起耳。即其音而求之，當必有神交於五帝之隆者，豈燕溺之商巳耶？溫良而能斷者，宜歌齊。人知
translation_en:
Li Shizhong 黎時中

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣: Essays on this topic usually show much clutter and confusion at the transitions. This composition strips away all superficial verbiage; it is harmonious, refined, and classically elegant—surely the work of a scholar of deep cultivation.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張: Its structure is balanced and upright, and its brushwork is vigorous and spirited; it can serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘: It skillfully brings out the meaning of the surviving music of the Five Emperors and Three Kings; record it for publication.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚: Clear, fluent, and extraordinary.

When one observes why the airs of Shang 商 and Qi 齊 were so named, their music is indeed worthy of esteem. Now, the Emperors and Kings have passed on, yet their surviving music remains; because the people of Shang and Qi remembered and preserved it, it was called by these names. How can one who is skilled in singing fail to know its origins?

Now, the significance of song to humankind is great indeed. Taken to its ultimate reach, its transformative power is utterly miraculous; traced to its root, its emergence has a definite source. The Airs of the States (Guofeng 國風), the Odes (Ya 雅), and the Hymns (Song 頌) are already of distant antiquity; why then should one have doubts solely regarding the airs of Shang and Qi?

Those who are forthright and yet compassionate ought to sing the airs of Shang. People know that the music of Shang is good, yet while it is sung in Shang, it did not originate in Shang. When the Great Way prevailed for the common good, the Five Emperors arose; was there not that which they gave vent to as the primordial music of Heaven and Earth? And what is nowadays called "Shang" is none other than their legacy. It is only that after the passage of several ages, the people of Shang alone remembered it; because the music was preserved through Shang, its name likewise arose from Shang. If one seeks it through its music, one will surely enter into spiritual communion with the flourishing age of the Five Emperors—how could it merely be the Shang of indulgent, decadent ease?

Those who are gentle and good and yet capable of decisive judgment ought to sing the airs of Qi. People know…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
齊之音善矣然歌於齊不始於齊也文明迭運
而三代興焉不有播之為天地之中聲者乎而
今之所謂齊者即其遺矣第歷數世之後惟齊
人識之聲自齊而傳故名亦以齊而起耳即其
音而求之當必有心通於三代之英者豈傲僻
之齊巳耶夫五帝三代先天下而彰其美商人
齊人後天下而盛其傳聞音而考其自故于今
稱五帝三王之美而誦商齊之音不衰君子當
知所執矣雖然古樂不可復作矣君子誠能涵
===
養德性以求所謂無聲之樂者則中和位育一
以貫之而三王可四五帝可六矣孟氏所謂今
之樂猶古之樂也不然雖咸英韶濩樂自樂耳
於直巳陳德何有
天子修男教父道也
陳鳴熙
同考試官教諭蔣 批 文有體裁非務繁縟
者
同考試官教諭張 批 發揮男教父道意極精
punctuated:
齊之音善矣，然歌於齊不始於齊也。文明迭運而三代興焉，不有播之為天地之中聲者乎？而今之所謂齊者，即其遺矣。第歷數世之後，惟齊人識之，聲自齊而傳，故名亦以齊而起耳。即其音而求之，當必有心通於三代之英者，豈傲僻之齊巳耶！夫五帝三代先天下而彰其美，商人、齊人後天下而盛其傳。聞音而考其自，故于今稱五帝三王之美，而誦商、齊之音不衰，君子當知所執矣。雖然，古樂不可復作矣。君子誠能涵養德性，以求所謂無聲之樂者，則中和位育一以貫之，而三王可四、五帝可六矣，孟氏所謂「今之樂猶古之樂」也。不然，雖《咸》、《英》、《韶》、《濩》，樂自樂耳，於直巳陳德何有？

天子修男教父道也
陳鳴熙
同考試官教諭蔣批：文有體裁，非務繁縟者。
同考試官教諭張批：發揮男教父道，意極精
translation_en:
… that the airs of Qi are good; yet though sung in Qi, they did not originate in Qi. As civilizing brilliance revolved through successive eras and the Three Dynasties arose, were there not those who diffused it as the central harmony of Heaven and Earth? What is nowadays called "Qi" is simply their surviving legacy. Only, after the passage of several generations, the people of Qi alone preserved the knowledge of it; because the melodies were transmitted from Qi, the name too arose from Qi. If one seeks into them through their musical notes, there must surely be that which brings the mind into communion with the finest spirits of the Three Dynasties—how could it merely be the Qi of arrogance and perversity! Now, the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties preceded the world in manifesting their beauty, while the people of Shang and the people of Qi followed after the world in making their transmission flourish. Listening to the airs and examining their origins, down to the present day people praise the beauty of the Five Emperors and Three Kings and recite the airs of Shang and Qi without decline; the gentleman ought to know what to hold fast to. Even so, ancient music cannot be revived. If the gentleman can truly nurture his moral nature so as to seek what is called "music without sound," then centrality and harmony, the proper ordering of Heaven and Earth and the nourishment of all things, will be threaded together as one—and the Three Kings may become four, and the Five Emperors may become six. This is what Master Meng (Mencius) meant by saying, "The music of today is just like the music of antiquity." Otherwise, even with the Xian, Ying, Shao, and Hu, the music would merely be music for its own sake—what would it have to do with rectifying oneself and setting forth one's virtue?

"The Son of Heaven cultivates the teachings for men; this is the way of a father." [Book of Rites, "Hunyi" 昏義]
By Chen Mingxi 陳鳴熙.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang: The essay has proper form and structure; he is not one who pursues ornate prolixity.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang: In elaborating on the teachings for men and the way of a father, the ideas are extremely precise…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
當而詞采且蔚然佳士也
考試官敎諭丘批整潔疏暢
考試官敎諭姚批明潤結尤得肯
王者以子道覺天下斯有父之尊矣夫天之立
君以子民也男敎之脩非父天下之道乎見於
昏義者若謂君后天下之大倫而陰陽天下之
大義男正位乎外而男敎之脩固君天下者之
責也玆焉出震以綏猷而導天下於軌物之内
乘乾以作則而囿斯世於皇極之中明此以正
===
百官固此敎也天地四方之所有事者靡不昭
揭以示之矣明此以正萬民亦此敎也裁成左
右之所當盡者靡不振舉而脩之矣天子之脩
男敎若此非父道乎蓋維君奉天以子民而倡
率之有方成之者與生之者等維民則君以自
治而作新之有術君我者與父我者同以之儀
刑乎百官而百官仰之敷言之訓非燕翼之謀
乎雖謂卽家之嚴父亦可矣以之表率乎萬民
而萬民尊之忠利之敎非義方之訓乎雖謂卽
punctuated:
當，而詞采且蔚然，佳士也。
考試官敎諭丘批：整潔疏暢。
考試官敎諭姚批：明潤，結尤得肯。
王者以子道覺天下，斯有父之尊矣。夫天之立君，以子民也；男敎之脩，非父天下之道乎？見於《昏義》者，若謂：君后，天下之大倫，而陰陽，天下之大義。男正位乎外，而男敎之脩，固君天下者之責也。玆焉出震以綏猷，而導天下於軌物之内；乘乾以作則，而囿斯世於皇極之中。明此以正百官，固此敎也，天地四方之所有事者，靡不昭揭以示之矣；明此以正萬民，亦此敎也，裁成左右之所當盡者，靡不振舉而脩之矣。天子之脩男敎若此，非父道乎？蓋維君奉天以子民，而倡率之有方，成之者與生之者等；維民則君以自治，而作新之有術，君我者與父我者同。以之儀刑乎百官，而百官仰之，敷言之訓，非燕翼之謀乎？雖謂卽家之嚴父，亦可矣。以之表率乎萬民，而萬民尊之，忠利之敎，非義方之訓乎？雖謂卽
translation_en:
…and apt, while its literary flair is moreover luxuriant—a fine scholar indeed!
Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: Neat, clean, and flowing smoothly.
Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: Clear and lustrous; the conclusion especially hits the mark.
When a true king awakens the world through the way of treating his subjects as children, he thereby possesses the veneration due to a father. Now, Heaven establishes the ruler in order to treat the people as his children; is not the cultivation of masculine instruction the way to be a father to the world? As seen in the "Meaning of Marriage" (Hunyi 昏義), it is as if to say: the ruler and the empress constitute the great human relationship of the world, and yin and yang constitute the great principle of the world. The man occupies his correct position on the outside, and the cultivation of masculine instruction is assuredly the responsibility of the one who rules the world. Here, he emerges in the trigram Zhen 震 to give repose to moral principles, guiding the world within the bounds of rules and standards; he mounts the trigram Qian 乾 to serve as a model, encompassing this age within the August Ultimate. To clarify this in order to rectify the hundred officials is assuredly this very instruction: of all the affairs pertaining to heaven, earth, and the four quarters, there are none that are not brightly held up and displayed to them. To clarify this in order to rectify the myriad people is also this very instruction: of all that ought to be fulfilled in regulating, completing, and assisting, there is nothing that is not roused up and cultivated. When the Son of Heaven cultivates masculine instruction like this, is it not the way of a father? For the ruler serves Heaven in treating the people as his children, and in leading them he has a method, so that the one who brings them to completion is equal to the one who gives them birth; the people take the ruler as their model in governing themselves, and in renewing them he has an art, so that the one who rules over us is the same as the one who fathers us. Taking this to serve as a model for the hundred officials so that the hundred officials look up to him—is not the instruction of his widely promulgated words a plan for providing comfort and protection to posterity? Even to say that he is just like the stern father of a household would be permissible. Taking this to set an example for the myriad people so that the myriad people revere him—is not the teaching of loyalty and benefit an instruction in righteous conduct? Even to say that he is just like…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
民之大父亦可矣何也天子之與后猶日之與
月陰之與陽也男教克脩則聰明睿智有如日
之象焉剛健中正有答陽之義焉日道也陽道
也君道也父道也寧非異位而同象者乎雖然
天地合而後萬物生二南之化始於關雎尚矣
惟君天下者思乾父付托之重而守正無爲以
端教本則刑于化溥而海內之氣清和咸理天
心且默應之矣所係豈其微哉是故天子貴建
中和之極
===
第貳場
論
養心莫善於寡欲
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批是作發寡欲養心之旨甚明
而格高調古辭健意新可以占素養矣允宜高薦
同考試官訓導李批議論正大氣格渾雄而束處
尤見忠讜之意有學有識之士也錄之以式
考試官教諭丘批明徹雅健迥異諸作
punctuated:
民之大父亦可矣。何也？天子之與后，猶日之與月，陰之與陽也。男教克脩，則聰明睿智，有如日之象焉；剛健中正，有答陽之義焉。日道也，陽道也，君道也，父道也，寧非異位而同象者乎？雖然，天地合而後萬物生，二南之化始於《關雎》尚矣。惟君天下者思乾父付托之重，而守正無爲，以端教本，則刑于化溥，而海內之氣清和咸理，天心且默應之矣，所係豈其微哉？是故天子貴建中和之極。

第貳場
論
《養心莫善於寡欲》
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批：是作發寡欲養心之旨甚明，而格高調古，辭健意新，可以占素養矣，允宜高薦。
同考試官訓導李批：議論正大，氣格渾雄，而束處尤見忠讜之意，有學有識之士也，錄之以式。
考試官教諭丘批：明徹雅健，迥異諸作。
translation_en:
… one might even call him the great father of the people. Why is this so? The Son of Heaven and the Empress are like the sun and the moon, or yin and yang. When the teachings for men are capably cultivated, then in intelligence, perspicacity, and wisdom, there is an image like that of the sun; in firm vigor and central uprightness, there is a meaning that responds to yang. The way of the sun, the way of yang, the way of the ruler, and the way of the father—are they not different in position yet identical in image? Even so, only after Heaven and Earth unite are the myriad things born; it has long been esteemed that the transforming influence of the "Two Nan" [sections of the Classic of Poetry] began with the "Guanju" [ode]. Only when he who rules All under Heaven ponders the weighty trust conferred by the Heavenly Father (Qian), and maintains uprightness and non-purposive action to rectify the root of instruction, will the transformation by personal example spread widely, the vital energies within the seas all be governed in clear harmony, and the mind of Heaven moreover silently respond to him. How could what depends on this be slight? Therefore, the Son of Heaven values establishing the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony.

Second Session
Discourse
"For nourishing the mind, nothing is better than making desires few" (Yang xin mo shan yu gua yu)
Chen Wenxuan 
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Su comments: This composition elucidates the purport of making desires few to nourish the mind very clearly, while its formal structure is lofty and its tone antiquity-inspired, its diction vigorous and its ideas fresh. From it one can gauge his habitual cultivation; he truly deserves to be highly recommended.
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li comments: The argument is upright and grand, the spirit and structure浑雄 [vigorous and majestic], and the concluding section especially reveals a loyal and forthright intent. He is a scholar possessing both learning and insight; we record this to serve as a model.
Examiner Instructor Qiu comments: Lucid, penetrating, refined, and vigorous—vastly different from the other compositions.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭姚批博雅閎邃是有得於養心之學者
夫人心之初一天也善事心者惟去其累乎天
者以復吾初而已矣曷言乎人心之初也天之
生人畀之以四肢百骸之體則宰之以虛靈知
覺之心其初本湛然瑩然天也而無有欲也有
欲則人矣人與天恒交相勝者也故人多則勝
天而天寡天多則勝人而人寡多寡之間養之
善不善係焉顧所以察之者何如耳善養心者
不求之物欲交感之後而惟求之吾心無欲之
===
初常使理爲主而物爲役則我常得以操順應
之權而物不得以爲吾湛一之累夫然後此心
之天以完而養之之道斯其至也養心莫善於
寡欲孟氏誠有味乎其言之哉嘗求之天矣夫
夫天輕清上浮惟玄惟默焉耳矣無聲無臭焉
耳矣而環宇宙內刁者調者呌者號者蠉飛而
蠕動者莫不各以其聲色象貌之類而肖形斂
迹以還於大塊而大塊卒澹然無欲斯固天之
心也人受天地之中以生得其虛靈不昧者具
punctuated:
考試官敎諭姚批：博雅閎邃，是有得於養心之學者。

夫人心之初，一天也。善事心者，惟去其累乎天者，以復吾初而已矣。曷言乎人心之初也？天之生人，畀之以四肢百骸之體，則宰之以虛靈知覺之心。其初本湛然瑩然，天也，而無有欲也；有欲，則人矣。人與天，恒交相勝者也。故人多則勝天而天寡，天多則勝人而人寡。多寡之間，養之善不善係焉，顧所以察之者何如耳。善養心者，不求之物欲交感之後，而惟求之吾心無欲之初。常使理爲主而物爲役，則我常得以操順應之權，而物不得以爲吾湛一之累。夫然後此心之天以完，而養之之道斯其至也。「養心莫善於寡欲」，孟氏誠有味乎其言之哉！嘗求之天矣。夫天輕清上浮，惟玄惟默焉耳矣，無聲無臭焉耳矣。而環宇宙內，刁者、調者、呌者、號者、蠉飛而蠕動者，莫不各以其聲色象貌之類，而肖形斂迹以還於大塊，而大塊卒澹然無欲，斯固天之心也。人受天地之中以生，得其虛靈不昧者，具
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Yao's comment: Broadly learned, refined, vast, and profound; this is the work of one who has truly grasped the learning of nourishing the mind.

Now, the original state of the human mind is wholly one with Heaven. One who is good at serving the mind simply cast off whatever encumbers the heavenly within it, so as to return to our original state, and nothing more. What is meant by the original state of the human mind? When Heaven gives birth to man, it endows him with a body of four limbs and a hundred bones, and governs it with a mind of empty, numinous consciousness and perception. In its original state, it is inherently limpid and lustrous—it is Heaven, and has no desires. Once there are desires, it becomes human. The human and the heavenly are constantly locked in mutual conquest. Thus, when the human is abundant, it overcomes Heaven and the heavenly becomes scarce; when the heavenly is abundant, it overcomes the human and the human becomes scarce. Upon the balance of abundance and scarcity hangs whether the nourishment of the mind is good or not; it simply depends on how one examines it. One who is good at nourishing the mind does not seek it after external things and desires have interacted and stirred, but seeks it solely in the original state of our mind when it is free of desires. By always making principle the master and external things the servants, we are always able to wield the authority of responding in accordance with things, while external things cannot become an encumbrance to our limpid unity. Only then is the Heaven within this mind made whole, and the Way of nourishing it reaches its utmost. "For nourishing the mind, nothing is better than making desires few"—how truly rich in meaning are these words of Mencius! I have sought the principle of this in Heaven. Now, [夫] Heaven, light and pure, floats above; it is simply dark and silent, and nothing more; it is simply without sound or odor, and nothing more. Yet throughout the universe, all things that rustle gently, stir harmoniously, cry out, or roar, and all creatures that flit about or wriggle along—none fail, each according to its kind in sound, color, form, and appearance, to take shape and then withdraw its traces to return to the Great Clod; and yet the Great Clod remains ever tranquil and free of desire. This is indeed the mind of Heaven. Man receives the centered harmony of Heaven and Earth to be born, obtaining that which is empty, numinous, and unclouded, and possesses it…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而爲心命之曰天君其精天精也其粹天粹也
其神明天神明也大虛中涵意象俱泯萬物作
類一私不淆斯時也情竇未開何有喜怒哀樂
之偏也物感未交何有聲色臭味之雜也思慮
未起何有克伐怨欲之私也湛然常清瑩然常
明斯則心之所自來也初也而莫非天也無有
所謂欲又安所事養也惟夫人生而靜者感物
而動心動於外欲攻於內即上智所不能無者
故心一馳於喜怒哀樂則七情不承其度而吾
===
之天鑿矣心一溺於聲色臭味則五官不保其
常而吾之天漓矣心一涉於克伐怨欲則一真
不守其宅而吾之天戕矣此一心也斂之幾何
而天下之可訢可羨可誘可嗜者交攻而遞進
吾有所欲物輒投之物有所感心輒繫之卒使
冲默之體直爲形骸昭曠之區莫非斤斧嗟乎
豈人心之初固若是耶夫人心之初自途人以
至於聖人一也聖人者爲能葆其真而不汨於
僞動以天而不間以人未有物先而其來不有
punctuated: 而爲心，命之曰「天君」。其精，天精也；其粹，天粹也；其神明，天神明也。大虛中涵，意象俱泯；萬物作類，一私不淆。斯時也，情竇未開，何有喜怒哀樂之偏也？物感未交，何有聲色臭味之雜也？思慮未起，何有克伐怨欲之私也？湛然常清，瑩然常明，斯則心之所自來也，初也，而莫非天也。無有所謂欲，又安所事養也？惟夫人生而靜者，感物而動，心動於外，欲攻於內，即上智所不能無者。故心一馳於喜怒哀樂，則七情不承其度，而吾之天鑿矣；心一溺於聲色臭味，則五官不保其常，而吾之天漓矣；心一涉於克伐怨欲，則一真不守其宅，而吾之天戕矣。此一心也，斂之幾何，而天下之可訢、可羨、可誘、可嗜者，交攻而遞進。吾有所欲，物輒投之；物有所感，心輒繫之。卒使冲默之體直爲形骸，昭曠之區莫非斤斧。嗟乎！豈人心之初固若是耶？夫人心之初，自途人以至於聖人，一也。聖人者，爲能葆其真而不汨於僞，動以天而不間以人，未有物先而其來不有，
translation_en:
… to form the mind, which is named the "Heavenly Ruler." Its essence is Heaven's essence; its purity is Heaven's purity; its spiritual intelligence is Heaven's spiritual intelligence. Contained within the Great Vacuity, both conceptual intentions and outward images are obliterated; though the myriad things arise in their respective kinds, not a single selfish impulse confuses it. At this time, the aperture of the emotions has not yet opened—how could there be any partiality of joy, anger, sorrow, or pleasure? Sensory impressions from external things have not yet made contact—how could there be any admixture of sounds, colors, odors, or flavors? Deliberate thoughts have not yet arisen—how could there be the selfishness of superiority, boasting, resentment, or covetousness? Limpid and ever pure, lustrous and ever bright: this is whence the mind comes; it is its original state, and none of it is not Heaven. When there is nothing that can be called desire, what need is there to engage in nourishing it?

Only when that which in human life is originally tranquil is stirred into motion by external things—the mind moved from without and desires attacking from within—does there arise that which even those of the highest wisdom cannot be entirely without. Therefore, once the mind gallops off after joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure, the seven emotions fail to observe their proper measure, and the Heaven within us is chiseled away. Once the mind drowns in sounds, colors, odors, and flavors, the five senses fail to preserve their constant norm, and the Heaven within us is diluted. Once the mind wades into superiority, boasting, resentment, and covetousness, the one true nature fails to guard its dwelling, and the Heaven within us is injured. This single mind—how little is it reined in, while all the things in the world that can delight, entice, seduce, or be craved attack it together and advance in turn! Whenever we have a desire, external things immediately cater to it; whenever external things stir an impression, the mind immediately becomes tethered to them. In the end, this causes our tranquil and silent substance to become mere bodily husks, and our bright and spacious realm to be met everywhere with axes and hatchets. Alas! Could the original state of the human mind really be like this?

Now, the original state of the human mind, from the person on the street all the way to the sage, is one and the same. The sage is able to cherish his true nature and not be submerged in falsity, moving by means of Heaven without being interrupted by what is human; before external things are present, their coming is not anticipated…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
既有物後而其去不留故欲不待寡而自盡心
不待養而自存者凡以其初未失也吾人之心
未能如聖人之無欲則養心之道將放而不求
惟聽吾不制之軀以役役於小體之烠與是場
師之舍梧檟而養樲棘者也未善也將離形去
智舉吾有覺之心而游於無何有之鄉與是又
釋氏之虛無寂滅桎梏而槁之者也未善也然
則善養者當何如亦曰心之有欲不能絕之使
無亦不可縱之使多惟寡之而已矣謹之於尸
===
居淵默之際以窒此欲之原防之於旦晝云爲
之頃以遏此欲之流喜怒哀樂之交於前也吾
視之若晦明寒暑之序則七情之欲寡而所以
養吾心之中和者莫善於此矣聲色臭味之誘
於體也吾等之若浮雲太虛之迹則五官之欲
寡而所以養吾心之湛一者莫善於此矣克伐
怨欲之萌於中也吾勝之若大將克敵之勇則
方寸種種之欲寡而所以養吾心之靜正者莫
善於此矣夫是之謂以心制欲而不以欲累心
punctuated: 既有物後，而其去不留。故欲不待寡而自盡，心不待養而自存者，凡以其初未失也。吾人之心，未能如聖人之無欲，則養心之道，將放而不求，惟聽吾不制之軀，以役役於小體之烠與？是場師之舍梧檟而養樲棘者也，未善也。將離形去智，舉吾有覺之心，而游於無何有之鄉與？是又釋氏之虛無寂滅，桎梏而槁之者也，未善也。然則善養者當何如？亦曰：心之有欲，不能絕之使無，亦不可縱之使多，惟寡之而已矣。謹之於尸居淵默之際，以窒此欲之原；防之於旦晝云爲之頃，以遏此欲之流。喜怒哀樂之交於前也，吾視之若晦明寒暑之序，則七情之欲寡，而所以養吾心之中和者，莫善於此矣。聲色臭味之誘於體也，吾等之若浮雲太虛之迹，則五官之欲寡，而所以養吾心之湛一者，莫善於此矣。克伐怨欲之萌於中也，吾勝之若大將克敵之勇，則方寸種種之欲寡，而所以養吾心之靜正者，莫善於此矣。夫是之謂以心制欲，而不以欲累心，
translation_en: …and after external things have passed, their departure leaves no trace behind. Therefore, that their desires are exhausted of themselves without waiting to be made few, and their minds are preserved of themselves without waiting to be nourished, is entirely because their original nature has never been lost. Since our own minds cannot be like the sage's in having no desires, as for the way of nourishing the mind: shall we let it go straying without seeking it back, merely allowing our unrestrained bodily frame to slave away at the pilfering [?] of the lesser parts of our constitution? That would be like the master gardener abandoning the parasol and catalpa trees to cultivate sour jujubes and thorns—it is not the best way. Or shall we cast off bodily form and discard knowledge, taking our conscious mind to roam in the realm of Nothing-at-All? That, again, would be like the Buddhists' emptiness and nirvanic extinction, shackling the mind and making it wither away—it is not the best way either. If so, then what should one who is good at nourishing the mind do? One can only say: when the mind has desires, we cannot cut them off completely to make them nonexistent, nor may we indulge them to let them multiply; we should simply make them few, and nothing more. Be vigilant during moments of corpse-like stillness and abyssal silence, so as to block up the source of these desires; stand on guard during the hours of daytime speech and action, so as to stem the flow of these desires. When joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure alternate before us, if we view them as the natural sequence of darkness and light, cold and heat, then the desires of the seven emotions will be made few, and for nourishing the equilibrium and harmony of our mind, nothing is better than this. When sounds, colors, odors, and flavors entice our bodily frame, if we regard them as mere traces of floating clouds in the Great Vacuity, then the desires of the five senses will be made few, and for nourishing the limpid unity of our mind, nothing is better than this. When contentiousness, boastfulness, resentment, and covetousness sprout within us, if we overcome them with the courage of a great general conquering the enemy, then the various desires in the square inch of our heart will be made few, and for nourishing the tranquil rectitude of our mind, nothing is better than this. Now, this is what is called governing desires with the mind and not encumbering the mind with desires;…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
天理之分數常多人欲之分數常寡外者不入
而何心非欲內者不出而何欲非天靜則虛而
明通焉一天精之涵也動則直而公溥焉一天
粹之著也徵之爲睟面盎背極之爲彌綸參贊
一天神天明之周流而泛應也至是則湛然者
得其體瑩然者不失其常吾之心一天之心而
無欲之初大虛同體聖人之域其優入之矣寡
欲之功謂非養心之至要至要者與雖然君心
尤爲萬化之原而養之尤難蓋其威命靈爽之
===
權本足以羅致百欲而百計以求中者又環相
踵也然則清心寡欲之功豈可已乎故曰君心
惟在所養又曰人主當防未萌之欲此善發孟
氏未盡之意
表
擬輔臣奉
旨撰
進
雝肅殿箴
punctuated:
天理之分數常多，人欲之分數常寡。外者不入，而何心非欲？內者不出，而何欲非天？靜則虛而明通焉，一天精之涵也；動則直而公溥焉，一天粹之著也；徵之爲睟面盎背，極之爲彌綸參贊，一天神天明之周流而泛應也。至是，則湛然者得其體，瑩然者不失其常。吾之心，一天之心，而無欲之初，大虛同體，聖人之域，其優入之矣。寡欲之功，謂非養心之至要至要者與？雖然，君心尤爲萬化之原，而養之尤難。蓋其威命靈爽之權，本足以羅致百欲，而百計以求中者，又環相踵也。然則清心寡欲之功，豈可已乎？故曰：「君心惟在所養。」又曰：「人主當防未萌之欲。」此善發孟氏未盡之意。

表

擬輔臣奉旨撰進《雝肅殿箴》，
translation_en:
The proportion of Heavenly Principle is always greater, and the proportion of human desires is always smaller. When external things do not enter in, how could the mind be anything like desire [? or: what mind is not free of desire]? When what is internal does not stray out, what desire is not itself Heaven? In stillness it is empty, clear, and all-penetrating—this is entirely the containment of Heaven's essence. In activity it is upright, impartial, and pervasive—this is entirely the manifestation of Heaven's purity. Manifested outward, it appears as a mild countenance and a rich fullness in the back; carried to its utmost, it encompasses the universe and assists in the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth—this is entirely the circulation and universal responsiveness of Heaven's spirit and Heaven's brightness. When one reaches this point, what is limpid attains its substance, and what is lustrous does not lose its constancy. My mind is entirely the mind of Heaven; in its original state free of desire, sharing one substance with the Great Vacuity, it enters with ease into the realm of the sages. How could the effort of making desires few not be called the most essential of essentials in nourishing the mind?

Even so, the ruler's mind is all the more the source of the myriad transformations, and nourishing it is all the more difficult. For the authority of his awesome commands and numinous splendor is in itself sufficient to gather in the hundred desires, while those who use a hundred schemes to cater to his wishes surround him and follow closely upon one another's heels. Such being the case, how can the effort of purifying the mind and making desires few ever cease? Therefore it is said: "The ruler's mind depends solely on how it is nourished." And again it is said: "A ruler of men ought to guard against desires before they have sprouted." These sayings ably bring out the meaning that Mencius left unexhausted.

Memorial

An imitation of a memorial congratulating the Grand Secretaries on composing and presenting the Admonitions for the Hall of Harmonious Reverence (Yongsu dian zhen) in obedience to an imperial decree, and on the imperial command to…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
命書
御屛賀表
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批是作構思淵懿音律鏗鏘揄揚我
皇上和敬之德與輔臣箴規之意殆盡

萬曆七年某月某日具官臣某等恭遇
===
皇上命臣等撰
進
雝肅殿箴書於
御屛謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
宅中思治採芻蕘而義悉箴規
座右弘文登琬琰而道存
顧諟祇承
punctuated:
命書御屛賀表
龔廷賓
