萬曆七年某月某日，具官臣某等，恭遇皇上命臣等撰進《雝肅殿箴》，書於御屛，謹奉表稱賀者。伏以宅中思治，採芻蕘而義悉箴規；座右弘文，登琬琰而道存顧諟。祇承
translation_en:
… and Ordering It Inscribed upon the Imperial Screen: A Congratulatory Memorial.

Gong Tingbin 龔廷賓.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiong 熊: This composition is profound and admirable in conception, and resonant in rhythm and meter; it extols to the fullest both Our Sovereign's virtues of harmony and reverence and the Chief Grand Secretaries' intent of admonitory counsel.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張: Clear, elegant, and fluent; it fully captures the proper style for eulogistic presentation and is worthy of being recorded.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘: Factual in its allusions and skillful in its phrasing; showing mastery of four-six parallel prose, it may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚: Flowing, graceful, and classical in standard.

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of the Wanli 萬曆 reign [1579], Your servants, holding full official titles, so-and-so and others, having reverently encountered Your Majesty's command that Your servants compose and present the Admonition for the Hall of Harmonious Reverence (Yongsu dian zhen 雝肅殿箴), and having ordered it inscribed upon the Imperial Screen, respectfully present this memorial to offer congratulations.

We humbly submit: Dwelling at the center and pondering good governance, You gather the words of grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers so that righteous principles are fully expressed in admonitory counsel; expanding literary culture beside Your throne, You elevate precious jades of writing so that the Way is preserved through watchful contemplation of Heaven's bright mandate. Reverently receiving…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
明命深懷一得之慚忻覩
洪謨式協九圍之慶臣等誠懽誠抃稽首頓首
竊惟
天子主神人之統克慎厥脩
君心關治忽之原惟在所養
處深宮而神周八極
麗正位則日有萬幾必惟敬惟和
聖學益純于宥密斯中規中節
皇猷允迪于熈明粵虞廷衍精一之傳溫恭協
===
帝治夏后闡幾康之訓祗若勅天湯德方
新盤盂載咏武功厎定觴豆咸銘心不越
堂階運太和于寓內道不離几席表至敬
于朝端振古若玆于今爲烈自都俞之風
既邈而儆戒之道寖微獻丹扆于承明唐
箴無補續尚書于太液宋理奚資圖作敬
天終鮮躬行之實屏書無逸僅彰粉飾之
文道不虛行時應有待玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
punctuated: 明命，深懷一得之慚；忻覩洪謨，式協九圍之慶。臣等誠懽誠抃，稽首頓首。竊惟天子主神人之統，克慎厥脩；君心關治忽之原，惟在所養。處深宮而神周八極，麗正位則日有萬幾。必惟敬惟和，聖學益純于宥密；斯中規中節，皇猷允迪于熈明。粵虞廷衍精一之傳，溫恭協帝；治夏后闡幾康之訓，祗若勅天。湯德方新，盤盂載咏；武功厎定，觴豆咸銘。心不越堂階，運太和于寓內；道不離几席，表至敬于朝端。振古若玆，于今爲烈。自都俞之風既邈，而儆戒之道寖微。獻《丹扆》于承明，唐箴無補；續《尚書》于太液，宋理奚資？圖作《敬天》，終鮮躬行之實；屏書《無逸》，僅彰粉飾之文。道不虛行，時應有待。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，
translation_en:
… the illustrious command, we deeply harbor shame over our single humble insight; joyfully beholding the grand plan, it fittingly harmonizes with the celebrations of the nine regions. Your servants, truly rejoicing and truly clapping our hands in delight, bow our heads to the ground.

We humbly reflect that the Son of Heaven presides over the bond between spirits and humankind, and is able to be cautious in his self-cultivation; the ruler’s mind is the source on which order and neglect depend, and it rests solely upon how it is nourished. Dwelling in the deep palace, his spirit encompasses the eight extremes of the world; occupying the rightful throne, every day brings ten thousand affairs. Only when there is reverence and harmony does the sagely learning become ever purer in serene profundity; thus hitting the mark of standard and measure, the imperial counsels truly advance in radiant brightness.

Of old, the court of Yu extended the transmission of “refinement and single-mindedness,” and with gentle reverence harmonized with the Sovereign; in governing, the Lord of Xia expounded the instruction on “subtle springs of action and tranquility,” respectfully complying with the warnings of Heaven. When Tang’s virtue was newly renewed, basins and bowls bore chanted inscriptions; when Wu’s achievements brought firm settlement, goblets and platters were all engraved. With the mind not stepping beyond the hall and stairs, supreme harmony was circulated throughout the realm; with the Way not departing from the sitting mat and table, utmost reverence was manifested at the head of the court. From antiquity it has been thus, and in the present day it shines even more gloriously.

Since the ethos of “Oh!” and “Yes!” grew distant, the way of vigilance and admonition has gradually waned. Though the Six Admonitions of the Red Screen were presented at the Chengming Hall, those Tang admonitions were of no avail; though the Book of Documents was continued at the Taiye Pool, what aid did it give to Song governance? Painting the Diagram of Revering Heaven ultimately lacked the substance of personal practice; writing “Against Luxurious Ease” upon a screen merely displayed superficial ornament. The Way does not operate in vain; the time must await its proper moment.

This is indeed because we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
英資天縱
聖德日躋
隆敬養于
慈闈夔夔舜孝
味道腴于
講幄翼翼文心
國學
親臨四海仰崇儒之化
郊壇禮祀羣工欽享
===
帝之仁鑑古則表其章灼者八十一條勵官則
疏其姓名者數十百計無作好無作惡治
已極于蕩平若履薄若臨深功猶嚴乎警
惕洗心
密勿觀象
肅雝匪壯麗以為工惟靜深而育德
重門洞闢
念出入起居之必欽
寶障新裁欲黼黻文章之具備特宣
punctuated: 英資天縱，聖德日躋。隆敬養于慈闈，夔夔舜孝；味道腴于講幄，翼翼文心。國學親臨，四海仰崇儒之化；郊壇禮祀，羣工欽享帝之仁。鑑古則表其章灼者八十一條，勵官則疏其姓名者數十百計。無作好，無作惡，治已極于蕩平；若履薄，若臨深，功猶嚴乎警惕。洗心密勿，觀象肅雝。匪壯麗以為工，惟靜深而育德。重門洞闢，念出入起居之必欽；寶障新裁，欲黼黻文章之具備。特宣
translation_en: … possesses heroic endowments bestowed by Heaven, and sage virtue that ascends daily. Exalting reverent care in the Empress Dowager's quarters, you show the anxious awe of Shun's filial piety; savoring the richness of the Way at the Classics Mat, you display the cautious diligence of King Wen's mind. When you visit the National University in person, all within the Four Seas look up to the transforming influence of your veneration for Confucian learning; when you perform the ritual sacrifices at the suburban altars, all officials revere the benevolence of your offerings to the Lord on High. In taking antiquity as a mirror, you highlighted eighty-one illustrious cases; in encouraging officials, you recorded the names of dozens and hundreds. Having no partiality for likes and no partiality for dislikes, your governance has already reached the utmost level and impartial perfection; yet, as if treading on thin ice or standing on the brink of an abyss, your efforts remain strict in vigilance and caution. Purifying your heart in quiet diligence, you contemplate the emblems in the Hall of Solemn Harmony [Su'ong]. You do not take magnificent splendor as fine workmanship, but rather cultivate virtue through tranquility and depth. With the double gates wide open, you remain mindful that every exit, entry, movement, and rest must be reverent; with the precious screens newly fashioned, you wish for their ceremonial patterns and literary compositions to be complete. Thus you have specially proclaimed…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
溫諭下采蕪詞用作箴銘仰資啟沃謂
大君身為民表必篤敬斯可安民而
聖人心與天通非致和曷由凝
命
慎喜怒于未發常若鑑衡
審言動于斯須式昭律度
端培養惟冲和澹泊是先
保治安以危厲憂勞為戒摛詞掞藻非敢比
謨誥之陳因事納忠庶幾備韋弦之助詎
===
期葑菲不棄得借彤管于尚方何當
宵旰深惟遂飾素屏于
便殿
皇心闓懌兼收工師朦瞍之陳
聖學光華自協脩齊治平之要曰雝雝曰肅肅
壹文德之儀刑曰在廟曰在宮儼
帝命之陟降顧名思義几杖戶牖之鑒具存緣
物警心關雎麟趾之意如在
化機運之掌上
punctuated: 溫諭，下采蕪詞，用作箴銘，仰資啟沃。謂大君身為民表，必篤敬斯可安民；而聖人心與天通，非致和曷由凝命？慎喜怒于未發，常若鑑衡；審言動于斯須，式昭律度。端培養，惟冲和澹泊是先；保治安，以危厲憂勞為戒。摛詞掞藻，非敢比謨誥之陳；因事納忠，庶幾備韋弦之助。詎期葑菲不棄，得借彤管于尚方；何當宵旰深惟，遂飾素屏于便殿。皇心闓懌，兼收工師、朦瞍之陳；聖學光華，自協脩、齊、治、平之要。曰雝雝，曰肅肅，壹文德之儀刑；曰在廟，曰在宮，儼帝命之陟降。顧名思義，几杖、戶牖之鑒具存；緣物警心，《關雎》、《麟趾》之意如在。化機運之掌上，
translation_en: … gracious edict, condescending to gather our humble words to be used as admonitory inscriptions, looking to them as an aid to your enlightenment and enrichment. We reasoned that since the Great Sovereign in his own person is the model for the people, only through steadfast reverence can he bring peace to the people; and since the Sage's heart communicates with Heaven, without achieving harmony how can he consolidate the Mandate? By being cautious with joy and anger before they arise, you are ever like a mirror and a balance; by examining speech and action in every fleeting moment, you manifest the standard and the measure. To rectify your self-cultivation, tranquil harmony and quiet simplicity must come first; to preserve peace and order, peril, severity, anxiety, and toil serve as warnings. In spreading forth words and displaying literary flourishes, we would not dare compare our work to the presentation of the *Counsels* and *Announcements* (Mo Gao); yet in offering loyalty as the occasion arises, we hope perhaps to provide the assistance of a soft leather strap or a taut bowstring. How could we expect that even coarse greens and turnips would not be discarded, and that we would be permitted to borrow the red-lacquered brushes of the Directorate for Imperial Manufactories? How could our words be worthy of Your Majesty's deep reflections while dressing before dawn and eating after dusk, so as consequently to adorn the plain screens in the side halls of the palace? The Imperial mind is open and pleased, comprehensively accepting the presentations of artisans and blind musicians alike; the Sagely learning shines brightly, naturally harmonizing with the essentials of self-cultivation, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world. Called "harmonious, harmonious," called "reverent, reverent," it unifies the model of civil virtue; called "in the ancestral temple," called "in the palace," it is as solemn as the ascending and descending of the Supreme Lord's Mandate. Looking upon the name and reflecting on its meaning, the admonitions on armrests, staffs, doors, and windows are all present; using external objects to alert the mind, the spirit of the *Ospreys* (Guanju) and the *Unicorn's Hoof* (Linzhi) is as if right before us. The pivot of transformation is turned upon the palm of your hand, …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
成憲炯然目前昔
太祖揭九範于座隅格言炳炳嗣
世宗製五箴于亭右彝訓煌煌以方
今日之宏摹信于
祖功
宗德而極盛垂為奕世之懿範允宜
聖子神孫所敬承者也臣等遭逢
一德慚非補衮之才寵荷
三朝竊附諫屏之義覲
===
天顏于咫尺踴躍奚勝仰
皇極之絲綸揄揚莫罄敢不勉傾葵藿益竭涓
埃夙夜惟寅弼贊綦隆之治臣隣共濟載
賡
喜起之歌伏願
心以為師
事惟法古
養希音于淵默無須鍾虡之縣
持重器于盈成凜若神明之格則
punctuated: 成憲炯然目前。昔太祖揭《九範》于座隅，格言炳炳；嗣世宗製《五箴》于亭右，彝訓煌煌。以方今日之宏摹，信于祖功宗德而極盛；垂為奕世之懿範，允宜聖子神孫所敬承者也。臣等遭逢一德，慚非補衮之才；寵荷三朝，竊附諫屏之義。覲天顏于咫尺，踴躍奚勝；仰皇極之絲綸，揄揚莫罄。敢不勉傾葵藿，益竭涓埃；夙夜惟寅，弼贊綦隆之治；臣隣共濟，載賡《喜起》之歌。伏願心以為師，事惟法古；養希音于淵默，無須鍾虡之縣；持重器于盈成，凜若神明之格。則
translation_en:
… and the established precedents shine brightly before Your eyes. In the past, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu) displayed the Nine Models at the corner of his seat, its maxims luminous and bright; subsequently, the Epochal Ancestor (Shizong) composed the Five Admonitions to the right of his pavilion, its constant instructions resplendent and glorious. Compared with the grand design of today, it truly brings the achievements of Your ancestors and the virtue of Your forebears to the utmost flourishing; passed down as an admirable model for generation after generation, it is indeed what Your sacred sons and divine grandsons should reverently uphold.

Your servants have encountered an era of unified virtue, yet are ashamed that we lack the talent to mend the imperial robes; favored across three reigns, we humbly attach ourselves to the principle of the remonstrance screen. Beholding the Heavenly Countenance within a foot's breadth, how can we contain our jubilant excitement? Looking up to the silken words of the Imperial Perfection, we cannot exhaust our praise and extolment. How could we dare not strive to incline our hearts like sunflowers toward the sun, and further exhaust our tiny drops and grains of effort—reverent from dawn to night to assist in this supremely prosperous governance, working together as ministers and associates to once more continue the song of "Joyful Rising"?

We humbly pray that You take the mind as Your teacher and in all affairs model Yourself upon antiquity; nurture rarefied tones in deep silence, without needing bells hung upon their stands; and hold fast the weighty vessel of state in an age of fullness and accomplishment, as awed as if in the presence of the spirits. Then…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
心和氣和兩間協和以交應而民壽物壽
一人萬壽以無疆臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第參塲
策五道
===
第一問
宋獻瑞
同考試官訓導寸經批陳鑑書屛我
皇上敬脩迪哲之意惓乎至矣子能鋪張而楊厲之其篤靖獻之忱者與
同考試官教諭陳批揚榷古今而
聖上禔身顯賢實德宛然虞周交儆氣象寓箴規於揄揚可以觀忠愛矣
考試官教諭丘批敷陳整贍得獻納體
考試官教諭姚批條對詳明忠誠溢於言表
帝王所以紹鴻曆凝鼎命以隆熈洽之治
punctuated:
心和氣和，兩間協和以交應；而民壽物壽，一人萬壽以無疆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第參塲
策五道

第一問
宋獻瑞
同考試官訓導寸經批：陳鑑書屛，我皇上敬脩迪哲之意惓乎至矣。子能鋪張而楊厲之，其篤靖獻之忱者與！
同考試官教諭陳批：揚榷古今，而聖上禔身顯賢實德，宛然虞周交儆氣象。寓箴規於揄揚，可以觀忠愛矣。
考試官教諭丘批：敷陳整贍，得獻納體。
考試官教諭姚批：條對詳明，忠誠溢於言表。

帝王所以紹鴻曆、凝鼎命，以隆熈洽之治
translation_en:
… when the heart is harmonious, the vital energy is harmonious, and the realm between Heaven and Earth responds in mutual harmony; when the people enjoy longevity and all living things enjoy longevity, the One Man enjoys boundless longevity for ten thousand years. Your servants are overcome with the utmost emotion and trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty, and we reverently present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays

First Question
Song Xianrui
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Cun Jing: In setting forth the historical mirror and inscribing the screen, Our August Emperor's earnest intention to reverently cultivate himself and follow the course of wisdom is supreme. You are able to elaborate and extol it—truly one who is steadfast in the sincerity of loyal devotion!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen: Discussing antiquity and the present, the true virtue of His Sacred Majesty in cultivating his person and exalting the worthy vividly recalls the spirit of mutual admonition in the eras of Yu and Zhou. Embedding remonstrance within praise, one can see in this your loyalty and devotion.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qiu: The exposition is orderly and rich, capturing the proper style of presenting counsel to the throne.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yao: The point-by-point responses are detailed and clear, with loyalty and sincerity overflowing beyond the words.

The means by which emperors and kings continue the great dynastic calendar and consolidate the Mandate of the tripods so as to exalt aflourishing and harmonious rule…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
者無他有敬脩之實學有迪知之良圖何
者君身治之則也脩之自我而道法懸於
往代人才身之輔也用之自我而臧否匿
于羣情明君知其然於是務向學之勤對
千古于几上運知人之哲羅九州于目前
師古要矣又以其精神志意日密勿焉而
敬天以自飭辨官尚矣又以其耳目聰明
日運量焉而勤民以為訓夫是以君之身
即二帝三王之身而其臣即千載一時之
===
臣明良會而庶績凝邦其永孚于休乎知
此則我
皇上陳鑑書屏之意
昭德任賢之實與夫
敬天勤民之心不可以揚厲其萬一乎哉蓋嘗
論之虞舜古大聖人也皐陶之陳謨也首
衍慎厥身脩之旨而推及于知人安民高
宗殷中興令主也傅說之為相也首陳監
于成憲之言而迪之以旁招俊乂此大臣
punctuated: 者無他，有敬脩之實學，有迪知之良圖。何者？君身，治之則也，脩之自我，而道法懸於往代；人才，身之輔也，用之自我，而臧否匿于羣情。明君知其然，於是務向學之勤，對千古于几上；運知人之哲，羅九州于目前。師古要矣，又以其精神志意日密勿焉，而敬天以自飭；辨官尚矣，又以其耳目聰明日運量焉，而勤民以為訓。夫是以君之身即二帝三王之身，而其臣即千載一時之臣，明良會而庶績凝，邦其永孚于休乎！知此，則我皇上陳鑑書屏之意、昭德任賢之實，與夫敬天勤民之心，不可以揚厲其萬一乎哉？蓋嘗論之：虞舜，古大聖人也，皐陶之陳謨也，首衍「慎厥身脩」之旨，而推及于「知人安民」；高宗，殷中興令主也，傅說之為相也，首陳「監于成憲」之言，而迪之以「旁招俊乂」。此大臣
translation_en: …is nothing other than having the substantive learning of reverent self-cultivation and the sound strategy of enlightened discernment. Why is this so? The ruler's person is the model for governance; its cultivation rests with oneself, yet the ways and laws hang suspended in past ages. Men of talent are the auxiliaries to the ruler's person; their employment rests with oneself, yet their merits and faults lie hidden among the sentiments of the multitude. The enlightened ruler knows this is so. Therefore, he devotes himself to diligence in pursuing learning, confronting a thousand ages upon his desk; he exercises the wisdom of knowing men, gathering the Nine Provinces before his eyes. Taking antiquity as a teacher is essential, and yet with his spirit, mind, and will he labors assiduously day by day, revering Heaven to discipline himself; distinguishing officials is paramount, and yet with his ears, eyes, hearing, and sight he deliberates and measures day by day, taking diligence toward the people as his precept. Thus the ruler's person becomes the very person of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and his ministers become the ministers of a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity. When an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet and all achievements are consolidated, will the state not forever enjoy auspiciousness in full trust! Understanding this, can one not extol even one ten-thousandth of Our Sovereign's intention in displaying historical mirrors and inscribing screen-walls, his reality in manifesting virtue and employing the worthy, and his heart in revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people? Let us consider the matter: Shun of Yu was a great sage of antiquity; when Gao Yao set forth his counsels, he first elaborated the purport of "carefully cultivating his person" and extended it to "knowing men and giving peace to the people." Gaozong was a fine ruler of the Yin restoration; when Fu Yue served as his Chief Minister, he first presented the words "take the established laws as a mirror" and guided him with "summoning men of eminent talent from all sides." This is how great ministers…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
忠誠體國預危明主箴規之法所由起也
當是時舜則協于帝而咨岳牧矣高宗則
紹先王而喻股肱矣臣以是箴君君以是
受臣此陳鑒書屏之義所由肇也迨至成
周文武立極成康繼體詩書所載其言脩
己用人之道獨詳如曰自殷王中宗及高
宗及祖甲及我文王玆四人迪哲嗣王其
監于玆言師古敬德也曰繼自今我其立
政立事準人牧夫我其克灼知厥若言辨
===
官乂民也厥後孔子告君推尊文武悉舉
其脩身尊賢者以對則有古大臣箴規之
忠而不遇主聖方冊所陳徒託諸空言爾
今夫人君一日二日有萬幾至繁也三公
九卿邦伯庶長至夥也墳典丘索紀載至
浩漫也甸侯綏要荒服地里至遼邈也將
日取古聖帝哲王庸君闇主興亡之迹而
攷證焉不能也日求三事六府諸司百執
事之臣而稽詢焉亦不能也於是乎鑑以
punctuated: 忠誠體國、預危明主，箴規之法所由起也。當是時，舜則協于帝而咨岳牧矣，高宗則紹先王而喻股肱矣。臣以是箴君，君以是受臣，此陳鑒書屏之義所由肇也。迨至成周，文、武立極，成、康繼體，《詩》、《書》所載，其言脩己用人之道獨詳。如曰：「自殷王中宗，及高宗，及祖甲，及我文王，玆四人迪哲，嗣王其監于玆。」言師古敬德也。曰：「繼自今，我其立政，立事、準人、牧夫，我其克灼知厥若。」言辨官乂民也。厥後孔子告君，推尊文、武，悉舉其脩身尊賢者以對，則有古大臣箴規之忠，而不遇主聖，方冊所陳，徒託諸空言爾。今夫人君一日二日有萬幾，至繁也；三公、九卿、邦伯、庶長，至夥也；《墳》、《典》、《丘》、《索》，紀載至浩漫也；甸、侯、綏、要、荒服，地里至遼邈也。將日取古聖帝、哲王、庸君、闇主興亡之迹而攷證焉，不能也；日求三事、六府、諸司、百執事之臣而稽詢焉，亦不能也。於是乎鑑以
translation_en: … loyal and devoted to the state, forewarning an enlightened ruler of peril—was how the method of remonstrance and admonition arose. At those times, Shun was in harmony with the supreme ruler Yao and consulted the Four Peaks and Twelve Pastors, while Gaozong continued the work of the former kings and instructed his chief ministers, his "legs and arms." Ministers used these principles to admonish their rulers, and rulers used them to receive the counsel of their ministers; this is how the practice of presenting mirrors of history and inscribing folding screens began. Down to the flourishing Zhou dynasty, Kings Wen and Wu established the supreme standard, and Kings Cheng and Kang succeeded to the throne. What is recorded in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) speaks with particular thoroughness on the way of cultivating oneself and employing men. For instance, it is said: "From the Yin king Zhongzong, to Gaozong, to Zujia, and to our King Wen—these four men walked in wisdom; may the succeeding king take them as his mirror." This speaks of emulating antiquity and revering virtue. And it is said: "From now on, in establishing governance, with the managers of affairs, the administrators of law, and the pastors of the people, may I clearly know those who are順 (compliant/virtuous)." This speaks of distinguishing officials and governing the people. Thereafter, when Confucius advised his ruler, he exalted Kings Wen and Wu, citing in full their self-cultivation and honoring of the worthy in his reply. Yet though he possessed the loyal remonstrance of the great ministers of antiquity, he did not meet with a sagely ruler, and what was set forth on bamboo tablets was merely entrusted to empty words. Now, in a single day or two a ruler has ten thousand affairs of state—they are अत्यंत (most) numerous; the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, regional lords, and myriad officials are most abundant; the records of the Three Mounds (Fen), Five Canons (Dian), Eight索 (Suo), and Nine丘 (Qiu) are most vast and boundless; and the Royal, Lordly, Pacified, Allied, and Wild Domains are geographically most distant and remote. Were he daily to take the traces of rise and fall of ancient sage emperors, wise kings, mediocre rulers, and benighted lords to examine and verify them, he could not do it; and were he daily to seek out the ministers of the Three Affairs, the Six Treasuries, the various bureaus, and the hundred offices to investigate and question them, he could not do that either. Therefore, by using a mirror to…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
書之不煩神慮而百王之妍媸照于是矣
屏以紀之不勞旁察而百職之勤惰列于
是矣此古之人臣善規其君與君之善用
乎臣者率是道也是故唐有千秋金鑑張
九齡以之規玄宗也後宋丁度以龜鑑精
義進李廌以兵鑑進彭龜年以內治聖鑑
進黃度以藝祖憲鑑進其聞曲江之風而
興起者乎乃其君不盡省也天寶且播蕩
矣而竟爲獻納之虛器忠臣愛君防微之
===
意亦何裨哉唐有疏刺史名屏太宗以之
廉郡國也後宋太宗識吉州守梁昪于屏
眞宗識潁州理呂夷簡于屏高宗記從臣
所舉監司于屏孝宗揭監司帥臣郡守于
屏其聞唐宗之烈而興起者乎乃其法未
盡舉也貞觀且鮮終矣而竟爲疏列之彌
文明君夢寐求賢之思良獨難哉夫以古
爲鑑鑑形而端範斯善用鑑也以名疏屏
顧名而思實斯善用屏也洪惟我
punctuated: 書之，不煩神慮，而百王之妍媸照于是矣；屏以紀之，不勞旁察，而百職之勤惰列于是矣。此古之人臣善規其君，與君之善用乎臣者，率是道也。是故唐有《千秋金鑑》，張九齡以之規玄宗也。後宋丁度以《龜鑑精義》進，李廌以《兵鑑》進，彭龜年以《內治聖鑑》進，黃度以《藝祖憲鑑》進，其聞曲江之風而興起者乎？乃其君不盡省也。天寶且播蕩矣，而竟爲獻納之虛器，忠臣愛君防微之意，亦何裨哉！唐有疏刺史名屏，太宗以之廉郡國也。後宋太宗識吉州守梁昪于屏，眞宗識潁州理呂夷簡于屏，高宗記從臣所舉監司于屏，孝宗揭監司、帥臣、郡守于屏，其聞唐宗之烈而興起者乎？乃其法未盡舉也。貞觀且鮮終矣，而竟爲疏列之彌文，明君夢寐求賢之思，良獨難哉！夫以古爲鑑，鑑形而端範，斯善用鑑也；以名疏屏，顧名而思實，斯善用屏也。洪惟我
translation_en: … write them down, then without troubling the ruler's sacred thoughts, the virtues and flaws of a hundred kings are reflected therein; and if a folding screen is used to record them, then without exhausting effort in wide-ranging inquiry, the diligence and indolence of the hundred officials are arrayed thereon. In antiquity, when ministers excelled at admonishing their rulers, and when rulers excelled at employing their ministers, they invariably followed this way. Therefore, in the Tang there was the Golden Mirror for a Thousand Autumns (Qianqiu jinjian), with which Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 admonished Emperor Xuanzong 玄宗. Later, in the Song, Ding Du 丁度 presented the Essential Meanings of the Tortoise and Mirror (Guijian jingyi), Li Zhi 李廌 presented the Mirror of Military Affairs (Bingjian), Peng Guinian 彭龜年 presented the Sacred Mirror of Internal Governance (Neizhi shengjian), and Huang Du 黃度 presented the Constitutional Mirror of the Founding Ancestor (Yizu xianjian). Were they not inspired to rise up upon hearing of the example of the Duke of Qujiang [Zhang Jiuling]? Yet their rulers did not fully examine them. Even the Tianbao era (742–756) ended in upheaval and displacement, so the work ultimately became a mere empty vessel of presentation; of what avail, then, was a loyal minister's intention to love his sovereign and guard against incipient perils! In the Tang there was also the folding screen inscribed with the names of Prefectural Governors (cishi), with which Emperor Taizong 太宗 inspected the commanderies and principalities. Later, in the Song, Emperor Taizong noted down Liang Bian 梁昪, Prefect (shou) of Jizhou, on a screen; Emperor Zhenzong 眞宗 noted down Lü Yijian 呂夷簡, Judicial Investigator (li) of Yingzhou, on a screen; Emperor Gaozong 高宗 recorded the Regional Supervisors (jiansi) recommended by his attendant officials on a screen; and Emperor Xiaozong 孝宗 posted the names of Regional Supervisors, Regional Commanders (shuaichen), and Prefects (junshou) on a screen. Were they not inspired to rise up upon hearing of the illustrious deeds of Taizong of the Tang? Yet their methods were not carried out in full. Even the Zhenguan era (627–649) rarely maintained its perfection to the end, and in the end the practice became mere ornamental formality of listing names; how truly difficult to sustain is an enlightened ruler's waking and sleeping yearning to seek out the worthy! Now, taking antiquity as a mirror—reflecting the form so as to rectify one's conduct—this is the skillful use of a mirror; inscribing names upon a screen—looking at the name and contemplating the reality—this is the skillful use of a screen. Humbly considering Our…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝
著精誠錄首敬天之事
作昭鑒錄詳垂裕之模
成祖文皇帝有
聖學心法歷陳君道有
文華寶鑑用迪
儲皇蓋深明乎克艱厥后之訓者矣
太祖武定之後頒醒貪簡要錄于中外諸司示
以食祿恤民遇來京奏事官
===
召見賜食訪民間疾苦
成祖御極之初
頒賜敕諭于文武羣臣示以攄誠共職書中外
官姓名于
武英殿南廊以備
觀覽蓋深識乎知人安民之理者矣當時翊賛
廟謨鋪張
聖烈者則有若基若濂若安若禕輩効忠于前
有若縉若廣若榮若淮輩弼直于後猶臯
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝著《精誠錄》，首敬天之事；作《昭鑒錄》，詳垂裕之模。成祖文皇帝有《聖學心法》，歷陳君道；有《文華寶鑑》，用迪儲皇。蓋深明乎「克艱厥后」之訓者矣。太祖武定之後，頒《醒貪簡要錄》于中外諸司，示以食祿恤民；遇來京奏事官，召見賜食，訪民間疾苦。成祖御極之初，頒賜敕諭于文武羣臣，示以攄誠共職；書中外官姓名于武英殿南廊，以備觀覽。蓋深識乎「知人安民」之理者矣。當時翊賛廟謨、鋪張聖烈者，則有若基、若濂、若安、若禕輩効忠于前，有若縉、若廣、若榮、若淮輩弼直于後，猶臯
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu, the Lofty Emperor, composed the Record of Utmost Sincerity (Jingcheng lu 精誠錄), placing the matter of revering Heaven first; and he produced the Record of the Luminous Mirror (Zhaojian lu 昭鑒錄), detailing the model for bequeathing abundance to posterity. Emperor Chengzu, the Cultured Emperor, had the Mental Method of Imperial Learning (Shengxue xinfa 聖學心法), setting forth in turn the Way of the Ruler; and he had the Precious Mirror of the Hall of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua baojian 文華寶鑑), wherewith to instruct the Heir Apparent. Indeed, they deeply understood the precept of "being able to recognize the difficulties of being sovereign."

After Taizu pacified the realm by martial force, he promulgated the Concise Record for Awakening the Greedy (Xingtan jianyao lu 醒貪簡要錄) to all offices in the capital and the provinces, instructing them in drawing their salaries while showing compassion for the people; whenever officials came to the capital to present memorials, he summoned them for an audience, bestowed food upon them, and inquired after the hardships of the common people. At the beginning of Chengzu's reign, he promulgated and bestowed imperial edicts of instruction upon the civil and military officials, instructing them to pour forth their sincerity in the performance of their duties; and he had the surnames and personal names of metropolitan and provincial officials written along the southern corridor of the Hall of Martial Valor (Wuying dian 武英殿) for his inspection and perusal. Indeed, they deeply grasped the principle of "knowing men and giving peace to the people."

At that time, among those who assisted in the counsels of the ancestral temple and extolled the sage achievements of the emperors, there were men such as Liu Ji 劉基, Song Lian 宋濂,陶安 Tao An, and Wang Yi 王禕 rendering loyal service in the earlier period, and men such as Xie Jin 解縉, Hu Guang 胡廣, Yang Rong 楊榮, and Huang Huai 黃淮 giving upright aid in the later period—just like Gao Yao…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之于虞說之于殷君臣同德而授守一道
也
列聖相承至德豐功莫可殫紀恭惟
皇上稟仁聖之資撫
雍熙之運
達孝尊
親至誠法
祖
日御經筵以講學優禮大臣而
===
親政其於脩身用人之道尤孜孜焉曰
帝鑑圖說輔臣仰窺
宸衷采千古帝王事實爲之編次者法聖哲芳
規凡八十有一戒狂愚覆轍凡三十有六
按世運之隆替察治理之廢興鏡主德之
醇疵審國祚之脩短是鑑也赫赫乎與
錄昭鑒
作寶鑑之意同矣儒臣進講時時陳說所以
裨益
punctuated: 之于虞，說之于殷，君臣同德，而授守一道也。列聖相承，至德豐功，莫可殫紀。恭惟皇上稟仁聖之資，撫雍熙之運，達孝尊親，至誠法祖，日御經筵以講學，優禮大臣而親政，其於脩身、用人之道，尤孜孜焉。曰《帝鑑圖說》，輔臣仰窺宸衷，采千古帝王事實，爲之編次者。法聖哲芳規，凡八十有一；戒狂愚覆轍，凡三十有六。按世運之隆替，察治理之廢興，鏡主德之醇疵，審國祚之脩短。是鑑也，赫赫乎與錄《昭鑒》、作《寶鑑》之意同矣。儒臣進講，時時陳說，所以裨益
translation_en: … to Shun of Yu, and Fu Yue 傅說 to the Yin dynasty: sovereign and ministers were of one virtue, and the founding and maintaining of the dynasty followed a single Way. Successive Emperors inherited the throne one after another; their supreme virtue and abundant achievements are too numerous to be fully recorded. Reverently we reflect that His Majesty is endowed with benevolent and sagely qualities and presides over an era of harmonious prosperity. With far-reaching filial piety he honors his parents, and with utmost sincerity he models himself on his Imperial Ancestors. Daily he attends the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) to engage in learning, treats the Grand Ministers with generous courtesy, and personally attends to state affairs. Above all, he is tirelessly diligent in the Way of cultivating the person and employing men. As for the Illustrated Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian tushuo), it was compiled and arranged by the Grand Secretaries, who respectfully discerned the Imperial mind and gathered historical deeds of emperors and kings across the ages. Exemplary models of sages and worthies to be emulated number eighty-one in all; overturned chariots of the reckless and foolish to be guarded against number thirty-six in all. By examining the rise and decline of historical eras, observing the flourishing and decay of governance, reflecting upon the purity or flaws of a ruler's virtue, and scrutinizing the longevity or brevity of dynastic fortunes—this mirror, how illustriously it shares the very same intent as compiling the Mirror of Illumination (Zhaojian lu) and composing the Precious Mirror (Baojian)! When the Confucian courtiers advance to lecture, they expound upon it time and again, whereby it aids and benefits …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
脩省者不上侔聖哲哉曰官名
御屏輔臣仰承
德意合內外文武官僚爲之分標者左文職牧
養若而人右武職捍衛若而人據形勝之
幅員辨煩簡之職掌秩崇卑之流品稽賢
否之政績是屏也煌煌乎與
召御前
揭南廊之意同矣
深宮燕閒時時披覽所以激勵忠良者不同
===
符
祖宗哉抑此天下臣民之共聞共見也而尤未
盡也伏覩
皇上嘗
翰灑學二帝三王治天下大經大法于
文華殿又
書責難陳善四大字
頒賜講官無非求端聖學之心爾當日講畢渙
發
punctuated: 脩省者，不上侔聖哲哉？曰《官名御屏》，輔臣仰承德意，合內外文武官僚爲之分標者：左文職，牧養若而人；右武職，捍衛若而人。據形勝之幅員，辨煩簡之職掌，秩崇卑之流品，稽賢否之政績。是屏也，煌煌乎與召御前、揭南廊之意同矣。深宮燕閒，時時披覽，所以激勵忠良者，不同符祖宗哉？抑此天下臣民之共聞共見也，而尤未盡也。伏覩皇上嘗翰灑「學二帝三王治天下大經大法」于文華殿，又書「責難陳善」四大字頒賜講官，無非求端聖學之心爾。當日講畢，渙發
translation_en: … self-cultivation and introspection—does it not rival the ancient sages and wise rulers above? There is also the Imperial Screen of Official Names (Guanming Yuping), which the grand secretaries, reverently carrying out the imperial virtuous intent, compiled by classifying the civil and military officials of both the capital and the provinces: on the left are the civil officials, listing such-and-such persons charged with pasturing and nourishing the people; on the right are the military officials, listing such-and-such persons charged with defense and protection. Based on the territorial expanse and strategic topography, it distinguishes burdensome from simple duties, orders the ranks of high and low status, and examines the administrative achievements of the worthy and the unworthy. Resplendent indeed is this screen! Its intent is identical to that of summoning officials before the imperial presence and posting their names in the Southern Corridor. In the leisure of the deep palace, it is constantly perused; as a means of inspiring the loyal and good, does it not tally with the Imperial Ancestors? Yet all these are what the officials and people of the empire have jointly heard and seen, and they still do not exhaust the matter. We humbly observe that Your Majesty once inscribed with the imperial brush "Study the Great Constant Principles and Great Laws by Which the Two Emperors and Three Kings Ruled the World" in the Wenhua Hall (Hall of Literary Brilliance), and also wrote in four large characters "Urge Difficult Duties and Set Forth the Good" (ze nan chen shan) to bestow upon the Classic Colloquium officials—all of which stems solely from a mind seeking to rectify sacred learning. Once, after the daily lecture concluded, Your Majesty issued forth…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
天語授以謹天戒十二事旨哉
皇言何顥顥也夫
大君之尊如天能畏天則能體天之道爲道建
極敷猷亦如天之覆載生成各恊于正而
天下益稱聖矣
皇上甞
御製正人心勅
告諭天下臣工又
書正巳率屬四大字
===
分賜九卿無非考正百官之事爾當朝覲畢
親獎廉能諭以愛養百姓一言大哉
皇心何肫肫也夫天之大德曰生能愛民則能
以天之心爲心黜陟懲勸亦如天之五行
四時各順其職而天下益稱明矣脩身至
是視儀監爲實不徒以鑑也官人至是視
辨名爲真不特以屏也於都哉其
盛德庥烈所以登棊隆衍靈長者曷以加哉乃
執事又欲闡仲尼之指陳文武之道以補
punctuated: 天語，授以「謹天戒」十二事。旨哉！皇言何顥顥也！夫大君之尊如天，能畏天則能體天之道爲道，建極敷猷，亦如天之覆載生成，各恊于正，而天下益稱聖矣。皇上甞御製《正人心勅》，告諭天下臣工；又書「正巳率屬」四大字，分賜九卿，無非考正百官之事爾。當朝覲畢，親獎廉能，諭以「愛養百姓」一言。大哉！皇心何肫肫也！夫天之大德曰生，能愛民則能以天之心爲心，黜陟懲勸，亦如天之五行四時，各順其職，而天下益稱明矣。脩身至是，視儀監爲實，不徒以鑑也；官人至是，視辨名爲真，不特以屏也。於都哉！其盛德庥烈，所以登棊隆、衍靈長者，曷以加哉！乃執事又欲闡仲尼之指，陳文、武之道，以補
translation_en:
… imperial words, bestowing twelve injunctions on "heeding Heaven's warnings." How profound! How luminous and grand are the Emperor's words! Now, the exalted position of the Great Sovereign is like that of Heaven; if he can stand in awe of Heaven, then he can embody the Way of Heaven as his own Way. Establishing the ultimate standard and spreading forth his plans, he will also be like Heaven and Earth in sheltering, supporting, generating, and completing all things, each harmonizing in rectitude, so that the world will all the more acclaim his sageliness.

His Majesty also once personally composed the Imperial Command on Rectifying Men's Minds (Zheng renxin chi) to instruct the officials throughout the realm; and he wrote the four large characters "Rectify Oneself to Lead Subordinates" to bestow separately upon the Nine Chief Ministers—all of which is nothing other than the business of examining and rectifying the hundred officials. When the court audiences were concluded, he personally praised the incorrupt and capable, instructing them with the single phrase "cherish and nourish the common people." How great! How earnest and sincere is the Emperor's heart! Now, the great virtue of Heaven is called life; if he can love the people, then he can take the heart of Heaven as his own heart. In demoting and promoting, punishing and encouraging, he will also be like Heaven's Five Phases and four seasons, each following its proper function, so that the world will all the more acclaim his brilliance.

When self-cultivation reaches this point, inspecting one's reflection in a mirror becomes concrete reality, and not merely a matter of using a bronze mirror; when employing men in office reaches this point, distinguishing names and duties becomes genuine, and not merely a matter of recording them on a screen. Oh, how splendid! By what could such flourishing virtue and glorious achievements—whereby supreme prosperity is attained and the dynastic fortune prolonged—possibly be surpassed? Yet Your Excellency still wishes to expound the purport of Confucius (Zhongni) and set forth the Way of Kings Wen and Wu in order to supplement…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖明愚生何說之有雖然仲尼有言其繫乾象
者曰天行健其賛文德者曰純亦不已夫
人主端居穆清之上顧諟非不切也而幾
微易間存省非不力也而嗜好易投投且
間則有息而不純斯與文不相似與天不
相似矣惟
皇上密慎脩之學篤取善之誠持對越之志永
憂勤之懷慎逸欲之防嚴怠終之戒以廣
延覽以虛聽納以奮獨斷而又丕移於近
===
習不徇于讒佞不間于聲色不惑于遊畋
如天之常健如文之緝熙則不鑑而自照
不屏而恒辨天下之治可常理矣愚生芹
曝之獻如此不識可轉而聞之於
上否
第二問
王命衮
同考試官教諭張批仁本合體用内外孔孟開其
源諸儒濬其流是作闡發蘊奧末歸本于立志此有德
punctuated:
聖明，愚生何說之有？雖然，仲尼有言，其繫乾象者曰：「天行健。」其賛文德者曰：「純亦不已。」夫人主端居穆清之上，顧諟非不切也，而幾微易間；存省非不力也，而嗜好易投。投且間，則有息而不純，斯與文不相似，與天不相似矣。惟皇上密慎脩之學，篤取善之誠，持對越之志，永憂勤之懷，慎逸欲之防，嚴怠終之戒；以廣延覽，以虛聽納，以奮獨斷；而又丕移於近習，不徇于讒佞，不間于聲色，不惑于遊畋，如天之常健，如文之緝熙，則不鑑而自照，不屏而恒辨，天下之治可常理矣。愚生芹曝之獻如此，不識可轉而聞之於上否？

第二問
王命衮
同考試官教諭張批：仁本合體用内外，孔、孟開其源，諸儒濬其流。是作闡發蘊奧，末歸本于立志，此有德…
translation_en:
…His Sacred Majesty, what more could this foolish student possibly have to say? Even so, Confucius had a saying: in his appended remarks on the Image of the Qian hexagram, he said, "The movement of Heaven is full of power"; and in praising the virtue of King Wen, it is said, "Wait—his purity likewise never ceased." Now, when the ruler of men dwells upright in the serene and pure heights above, his regard for the clear mandate is not unearnest, yet subtle incipient tendencies easily create a gap; his preservation of mind and self-examination are not unrigorous, yet fond desires easily find an opening. Once they find an opening and create a gap, there are pauses and a lack of purity; thus he ceases to resemble King Wen, and ceases to resemble Heaven. May His Majesty only deepen the learning of careful self-cultivation, strengthen the sincerity of adopting what is good, uphold the resolve of standing before the spiritual presence, perpetuate the mindset of anxious diligence, guard carefully against idleness and desire, and strictly heed the warning against laxity at the end; thereby broadening his reception and observation of talent, humbling himself to listen and accept advice, and rousing his independent judgment; while furthermore not being swayed [丕移, likely a misprint for 不移] by close attendants, not yielding to slanderers and flatterers, not being distracted by music and beauty, and not being deluded by excursions and hunting—being ever vigorous like Heaven, and continuously bright like King Wen. Then without a mirror he will naturally reflect all things, without a screen wall he will constantly distinguish his officials, and the governance of the world can be permanently kept in order. Such is the humble offering of wild celery and warming sun from this foolish student; I do not know whether it may be passed on and made known to His Majesty above or not?

Second Question
By Wang Minggun 王命衮
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: Benevolence fundamentally unites substance and function, the internal and the external; Confucius and Mencius opened its source, and the various Confucian scholars dredged its stream. This essay elucidates its profound mysteries, and at the end traces the root back to establishing one's resolve. These are the words of a man of virtue…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之言可以訓多士矣
同考試官教諭蔣批論仁至孔孟如揭日中天
諸儒衍說同異均有補於仁難以淺深偏全論是作獨
能折衷歸一當是理學
考試官教諭丘批析理精微孔孟諸儒論
仁之旨闡明無餘蘊矣
考試官教諭姚批融徹精妙題旨洞然是
善言仁者
執事揭聖門求仁之指下詢承學豈謂諸
===
生居近鴻儒之鄉亦有識仁者耶顧仁之
難言也久矣是雍賜由求上賢之所不敢
承而齊楚忠清之良未足與擬者愚也何
足以知之雖然夫子曰苟志於仁矣無惡
也愚生故不敢自棄于惡則安敢自委於
無是志耶竊承服師說而亦嘗反求之此
心矣敢以臆對今夫仁也者是天地之心
而人得之以為人無古今聖愚一也反諸
身而視聽言動所以靈昭順應而不至于
punctuated:
之言，可以訓多士矣。
同考試官教諭蔣批：論仁至孔、孟，如揭日中天；諸儒衍說同異，均有補於仁，難以淺深偏全論。是作獨能折衷歸一，當是理學。
考試官教諭丘批：析理精微，孔、孟、諸儒論仁之旨，闡明無餘蘊矣。
考試官教諭姚批：融徹精妙，題旨洞然，是善言仁者。
執事揭聖門求仁之指，下詢承學，豈謂諸生居近鴻儒之鄉，亦有識仁者耶？顧仁之難言也久矣，是雍、賜、由、求上賢之所不敢承，而齊、楚忠清之良未足與擬者，愚也何足以知之？雖然，夫子曰：「苟志於仁矣，無惡也。」愚生故不敢自棄于惡，則安敢自委於無是志耶？竊承服師說，而亦嘗反求之此心矣，敢以臆對。今夫仁也者，是天地之心，而人得之以為人，無古今聖愚一也。反諸身，而視聽言動所以靈昭順應，而不至于…
translation_en:
… [words of a man] of virtue, which can serve to instruct the many scholars.

Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Jiang comments: Discussions of humaneness (ren) reached Confucius and Mencius, like holding up the sun in mid-heaven. The various Confucian scholars elaborated their explanations with similarities and differences, yet all contributed to the understanding of humaneness and can hardly be judged in terms of shallow or deep, partial or complete. This composition alone is able to weigh the views and bring them into unity; it must be a work of Learning of Principle (lixue).

Examiner and Instructor Qiu comments: The analysis of principle is subtle and refined; the purport of Confucius, Mencius, and the various Confucian scholars in discussing humaneness has been elucidated with nothing left unexpressed.

Examiner and Instructor Yao comments: Thoroughly integrated and exquisitely subtle, with the meaning of the question made completely clear—this is someone who is adept at speaking of humaneness.

Your Excellency has held up the essential aim of seeking humaneness in the school of the Sage to inquire of us junior scholars below. Could it be that because the candidates dwell near the homeland of the great Confucian masters, you think there are also those among us who understand humaneness? Yet humaneness has long been difficult to speak of! It is something that even superior worthies such as Ran Yong,端木賜 (Duanmu Ci, Zigong), Zilu (Zhong You), and Ran Qiu did not dare claim for themselves, and with which the loyal and pure worthies of Qi and Chu [Lingyin Ziwen and Chen Wenzi] were not sufficient to be compared—how then could an ignorant person like me be adequate to know it? Even so, the Master said: "If the will be set on humaneness, there will be no wickedness." Since your foolish student does not dare abandon himself to wickedness, how could he dare resign himself to lacking this will? I have privately received and adhered to the teachings of my teachers, and have also tried seeking it within this mind of mine; I therefore venture to reply with my own humble thoughts.

Now, humaneness is the mind of Heaven and Earth, which human beings obtain in order to be human; without distinction between ancient and modern, sage and fool, it is one and the same. Turning back to examine oneself, that whereby seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting are spiritually clear and harmoniously responsive, without falling into…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
昧蔽痺痿者此也徵諸人而子臣弟友所
以孝忠友信而不至於乖忤睽離者此也
推之天地之所以合德民物之所以同體
而不至間閡戕害者此也古先聖哲若堯
舜湯文之爲君禹皐伊虺之爲臣或見而
知或聞而知總會之以心體之以身未始
喋喋然言仁而仁道固未嘗不昭晰於天
下慨周道衰而道術裂繁文盛而本眞漓
夫子蓋傷之于是始揭仁以立教卽諸門
===
弟之答述魯論具已然特其求之之方爲
之之術耳至於仁之所以爲仁則固罕言
之也罕言者非祕也蓋難言之矣下逮戰
國功利薰灼人心陷溺孟子起而述孔業
焉言仁而兼言義者蓋義卽仁之毅然裁
制者耳非仁之外別有義也夫曰立達曰
愛人曰恭寬信敏惠孔子未嘗不言用也
而體卽含矣曰人心曰尊爵曰安宅孟子
未嘗不言體也而用卽貫矣先儒謂孔子
punctuated: 昧蔽痺痿者，此也；徵諸人，而子、臣、弟、友所以孝、忠、友、信而不至於乖忤睽離者，此也；推之天地之所以合德，民物之所以同體，而不至間閡戕害者，此也。古先聖哲，若堯、舜、湯、文之爲君，禹、皐、伊、虺之爲臣，或見而知，或聞而知，總會之以心，體之以身，未始喋喋然言仁，而仁道固未嘗不昭晰於天下。慨周道衰而道術裂，繁文盛而本眞漓，夫子蓋傷之，于是始揭仁以立教。卽諸門弟之答述，《魯論》具已，然特其求之之方、爲之之術耳；至於仁之所以爲仁，則固罕言之也。罕言者，非祕也，蓋難言之矣。下逮戰國，功利薰灼，人心陷溺，孟子起而述孔業焉。言仁而兼言義者，蓋義卽仁之毅然裁制者耳，非仁之外別有義也。夫曰「立達」、曰「愛人」、曰「恭、寬、信、敏、惠」，孔子未嘗不言用也，而體卽含矣；曰「人心」、曰「尊爵」、曰「安宅」，孟子未嘗不言體也，而用卽貫矣。先儒謂孔子
translation_en: …becoming darkened, obscured, numb, or paralyzed—it is this; verified in other people, that by which sons, subjects, younger brothers, and friends are filial, loyal, fraternal, and trustworthy without falling into perversity, defiance, estrangement, or separation—it is this; extended to that by which Heaven and Earth unite their virtues, and that by which the people and all things form one body without falling into obstruction, alienation, or mutual injury—it is this. The ancient sages and worthies, such as Yao, Shun, Tang, and King Wen as rulers, and Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Zhonghui as ministers, whether they knew it by seeing it or knew it by hearing of it, all comprehended it as a whole in their minds and embodied it in their persons. They never chattered endlessly about humaneness (ren), yet the Way of humaneness was indeed never anything less than bright and clear throughout the world. Alas, when the Way of Zhou declined, the Way and its methods were torn apart; as elaborate formalities flourished, original authenticity eroded. The Master grieved over this, and thereupon first held up humaneness to establish his teaching. Even the replies recorded by his various disciples are fully set forth in the Analects of Lu (Lu Lun), yet those are merely the methods for seeking it and the arts for practicing it; as for that by which humaneness is humaneness, he indeed rarely spoke of it. That he rarely spoke of it was not to keep it secret, but because it is difficult to put into words. Coming down to the Warring States period, utilitarianism and profit burned fiercely, and human minds sank and drowned; Mencius arose and transmitted the enterprise of Confucius. That in speaking of humaneness he also spoke of righteousness (yi) is because righteousness is simply the resolute regulating and judging aspect of humaneness, not that there is another righteousness outside of humaneness. Now, in speaking of "establishing others and helping others attain," of "loving others," and of "courtesy, breadth, trustworthiness, diligence, and generosity," Confucius never failed to speak of its function (yong), and yet its substance (ti) was contained therein; in speaking of "the human mind," of "the honors of nobility," and of "the peaceful abode," Mencius never failed to speak of its substance, and yet its function ran right through it. title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
多說體孟子多說用殆非也子輿氏沒此
旨益湮漢唐以降閎覽崇議之俊嵬履尊
行之彥豈不數數然哉如東觀校讎石渠
聚講非不勤也爲博而已仁則吾不知也
如揉情植節刓貞扶義非不烈也爲名而
已仁則吾不知也如綺詞麗藻逸致冲襟
非不蔚然華超然高也爲靡爲放而已仁
則吾不知也他如董子明道正誼之說韓
子原道博愛之論似矣然猶履閾而未入
===
其域囓胾而未味其旨者耶逮至有宋星
聚奎躔眞儒輩出濂有周子尋孔孟之緒
而追續之卽以無欲學聖得求仁之要矣
其言愛曰仁而根本於德非遺內也洛有
程子益衍周子之傳而推明之識仁之說
邃乎粹矣其曰仁者渾然與物同體蓋見
大也孔孟正脉其續于玆乎維時及門之
士頴厚如定夫忠信如光庭深密如與叔
警慧如立之純茂如季明自餘英哲難以
punctuated: 多說體，孟子多說用，殆非也。子輿氏沒，此旨益湮。漢唐以降，閎覽崇議之俊、嵬履尊行之彥，豈不數數然哉？如東觀校讎、石渠聚講，非不勤也，爲博而已，仁則吾不知也；如揉情植節、刓貞扶義，非不烈也，爲名而已，仁則吾不知也；如綺詞麗藻、逸致冲襟，非不蔚然華、超然高也，爲靡爲放而已，仁則吾不知也。他如董子「明道正誼」之說、韓子《原道》「博愛」之論，似矣，然猶履閾而未入其域，囓胾而未味其旨者耶？逮至有宋，星聚奎躔，眞儒輩出。濂有周子，尋孔孟之緒而追續之，卽以無欲學聖，得求仁之要矣。其言「愛曰仁」而根本於德，非遺內也。洛有程子，益衍周子之傳而推明之，《識仁》之說，邃乎粹矣！其曰「仁者渾然與物同體」，蓋見大也。孔孟正脉，其續于玆乎！維時及門之士，頴厚如定夫、忠信如光庭、深密如與叔、警慧如立之、純茂如季明，自餘英哲，難以
translation_en:
… mostly spoke of substance while Master Meng (Mencius) mostly spoke of function, they were likely mistaken. After Ziyu (Mencius) died, this essential meaning became increasingly obscured. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, were there not frequently men of talent with vast learning and lofty discussions, and men of worth with towering conduct and noble actions? For instance, collating texts in the Eastern Watchtower (Dongguan) and gathering to lecture in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiquge) were certainly not lacking in diligence, yet they were merely for breadth of learning—as for benevolence (ren), I do not know if it was there. Bending one's passions to establish integrity and carving out rectitude to uphold righteousness were certainly not lacking in fierceness, yet they were merely for reputation—as for benevolence, I do not know if it was there. Ornate diction andsplendid rhetoric, untrammeled flair and detached composure, were certainly not lacking in luxuriant華 brilliance and transcendent loftiness, yet they were merely extravagance and unbridledness—as for benevolence, I do not know if it was there. As for others, such as Master Dong's (Dong Zhongshu) doctrine of "clarifying the Way and rectifying righteousness," and Master Han's (Han Yu) discourse on "universal love" in his "Tracing the Way" (Yuan Dao), they came close; yet were they not still like someone stepping on the threshold without entering the realm, or biting into a slice of meat without savoring its flavor?

When it came down to the Song dynasty, the stars gathered in the Kui mansion, and true Confucians emerged in succession. In Lianxi there was Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi), who sought out the thread of Confucius and Mencius and carried it forward; by learning to be a sage through having no desires, he grasped the essential way of seeking benevolence. When he said that "love is called benevolence," he rooted it in virtue and did not neglect the internal. In Luoyang there were the Masters Cheng (Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi), who further expanded upon Master Zhou's transmission and elucidated it; the doctrine of "Understanding Benevolence" (Shi ren) is profound and pure indeed! Its statement that "the benevolent person seamlessly forms one body with all things" truly perceives what is great. Was not the orthodox lineage of Confucius and Mencius continued right here? At that time, among the disciples who studied at their gate—astute and generous like Dingfu (You Zuo), loyal and trustworthy like Guangting (Zhu Guangting), deep and meticulous like Yushu (Lü Dalin), alert and intelligent like Lizhi (Yin Tun [?] / Su Bing), pure and flourishing like Jiming (Liu絢)—along with the remaining brilliant and wise men, it is difficult to …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
勝道然實識仁者惟中立顯道和靖三人
者獨擅稱焉何堇堇也蓋仁猶天然孔子
之於仁也中心安之身即天矣其言仁者
譬之風雨露雷無非天之所以澤物而不
可以一端求也孟子願學孔子亦知天矣
其言仁而兼言義者蓋其時然譬之霜霰
霏雪是亦天之所以成物而非有二也後
世儒者如中立以覺言仁顯道以生意言
仁和靖以公言仁皆各就所見以立言譬
===
之譚天者即嵎夷而言天天固在是即南
交而言天天亦在是即朔方而言天天亦
未嘗不在是而要之并包八表瀰漫六合
者則非可以方所拘矣然長進雖竝許於
在涪道南獨稱于別頴何以也即尹謝沒
而其傳泯矣中立以後一傳而仲素再傳
而愿中三傳而紫陽朱子出仲素論仁雖
不少概見觀其教人每令靜中看喜怒哀
樂未發時作何氣象而愿中稱其飲人以
punctuated: 勝道。然實識仁者，惟中立、顯道、和靖三人者獨擅稱焉，何堇堇也？蓋仁猶天然。孔子之於仁也，中心安之，身即天矣。其言仁者，譬之風雨露雷，無非天之所以澤物，而不可以一端求也。孟子願學孔子，亦知天矣。其言仁而兼言義者，蓋其時然，譬之霜霰霏雪，是亦天之所以成物，而非有二也。後世儒者，如中立以覺言仁，顯道以生意言仁，和靖以公言仁，皆各就所見以立言。譬之譚天者，即嵎夷而言天，天固在是；即南交而言天，天亦在是；即朔方而言天，天亦未嘗不在是。而要之并包八表、瀰漫六合者，則非可以方所拘矣。然長進雖竝許於在涪，道南獨稱于別頴，何以也？即尹、謝沒而其傳泯矣。中立以後，一傳而仲素，再傳而愿中，三傳而紫陽朱子出。仲素論仁雖不少概見，觀其教人，每令靜中看喜怒哀樂未發時作何氣象；而愿中稱其飲人以…
translation_en: …be fully recounted. Yet among those who truly understood humaneness (ren 仁), only the three men—Zhongli 中立 (Yang Shi 楊時), Xiandao 顯道 (Xie Liangzuo 謝良佐), and Hejing 和靖 (Yin Tun 尹焞)—exclusively held that reputation. Why were there so few? This is because humaneness is like Heaven. As for Confucius in relation to humaneness, his heart-mind was at peace with it, and his very person was one with Heaven. His discussions of humaneness may be compared to wind, rain, dew, and thunder—all of which are means by which Heaven nourishes things—so it cannot be sought in any single aspect. Mencius wished to learn from Confucius, and he too knew Heaven. That he spoke of righteousness (yi 義) alongside humaneness was due to the circumstances of his time; it may be compared to frost, sleet, and driving snow, which are also means by which Heaven brings things to completion, and are not something separate. Scholars of later generations—such as Zhongli, who spoke of humaneness in terms of awareness (jue 覺); Xiandao, who spoke of humaneness in terms of vital impulse (shengyi 生意); and Hejing, who spoke of humaneness in terms of impartiality (gong 公)—all established their doctrines based on their respective insights. They may be compared to those who discuss Heaven: if one speaks of Heaven from Yuyi 嵎夷 in the east, Heaven is certainly there; if one speaks of Heaven from Nanjiao 南交 in the south, Heaven is also there; if one speaks of Heaven from Shuofang 朔方 in the north, Heaven is never not there either. Yet in sum, that which encompasses the eight reaches and pervades the six directions cannot be confined to any fixed quarter. Nevertheless, although both [Yang Shi and谢良佐/Yin Tun] were praised for their progress when [Cheng Yi 程頤 was] in Fuzhou 涪州, why was it that upon parting at Yingchuan 頴川, [Cheng Hao 程顥] remarked of [Yang Shi] alone, "My Way travels south"? Indeed, after Yin [Tun] and Xie [Liangzuo] died, their transmission died out. After Zhongli, in one transmission came Zhongsu 仲素 (Luo Congyan 羅從彥), in a second transmission came Yuanzhong 愿中 (Li Tong 李侗), and in a third transmission Master Zhu of Ziyang 紫陽朱子 (Zhu Xi 朱熹) emerged. Although Zhongsu's discourses on humaneness are rarely seen in extant records, if we look at how he taught others, he always instructed them to observe in quiescence what the disposition (qixiang 氣象) is like before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy are aroused; and Yuanzhong praised him for imbuing people with…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
和如春風發物則於仁也亦近之矣卽愿
中答朱子書首以孔孟之訓廣以人物同
得之原約以體用兼舉之本啓以靜坐默
識之功則於仁也非徒言之也朱子躬承
李氏之緒而欲衍程氏之傳懼學者徒誦
其遺言而不味其指或狥外而遺內或執
內而遺外也因爲之訓曰仁者心之德愛
之理此仁說圖所爲作也真希元氏稱其
發先儒所未發其篤信如此此於孔孟言
===
仁之指雖微有間然卽其泰山喬嶽之度
繼往開來之心殆亦勇於當仁者耶世譚
濂洛關閩由是而觀閩尤章灼長遠如此
矣乃晚近言仁者愚惑焉滔淫足性托之
乎任放以爲真而矩踰矣保奸比匪托之
乎道廣以爲容而辨殽矣耽無沉空托之
乎玄解以爲達而實墮矣揭提門戶高自
標幟托之乎立本以示杓也而曰貿貿焉
眩騖不覺矣以是求仁仁不日遠乎嗟夫
punctuated:
和，如春風發物，則於仁也亦近之矣。卽愿中答朱子書，首以孔孟之訓，廣以人物同得之原，約以體用兼舉之本，啓以靜坐默識之功，則於仁也非徒言之也。朱子躬承李氏之緒，而欲衍程氏之傳，懼學者徒誦其遺言而不味其指，或狥外而遺內，或執內而遺外也，因爲之訓曰：「仁者，心之德，愛之理。」此《仁說圖》所爲作也。真希元氏稱其發先儒所未發，其篤信如此。此於孔孟言仁之指雖微有間，然卽其泰山喬嶽之度，繼往開來之心，殆亦勇於當仁者耶！世譚濂、洛、關、閩，由是而觀，閩尤章灼長遠如此矣。
乃晚近言仁者，愚惑焉。滔淫足性，托之乎任放以爲真，而矩踰矣；保奸比匪，托之乎道廣以爲容，而辨殽矣；耽無沉空，托之乎玄解以爲達，而實墮矣；揭提門戶，高自標幟，托之乎立本以示杓也，而曰貿貿焉眩騖不覺矣。以是求仁，仁不日遠乎？嗟夫！
translation_en:
… harmony, like the spring breeze bringing things to life; thus he too came close to benevolence (ren). Looking at the letter that Yuanzhong [Li Tong 李侗] wrote in reply to Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹], he began with the teachings of Confucius and Mencius, broadened them with the origin that human beings and myriad things share in common, condensed them into the foundation that encompasses both substance and function, and inspired him with the practice of quiet-sitting and silent comprehension—so with regard to benevolence, he did not merely speak of it. Master Zhu personally inherited the line of Master Li [Li Tong] and wished to expand the transmission of the Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤]. Fearing that scholars would merely recite their surviving words without savoring their meaning—either pursuing the external while neglecting the internal, or clinging to the internal while neglecting the external—he therefore formulated the definition: "Benevolence is the virtue of the mind and the principle of love." It was for this reason that the Diagram of the Treatise on Benevolence (Renshuo tu) was composed. Zhen Xiyuan [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] praised him for revealing what earlier Confucians had never revealed, such was his devout faith in it. Although this differs slightly from the import of what Confucius and Mencius said about benevolence, yet if we consider his stature like Mount Tai and the lofty peaks, and his heart set on carrying on the past heritage and opening the way for the future, was he not also one who bravely took benevolence as his own responsibility? The world speaks of the schools of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min; viewed from this perspective, the learning of Min [Fujian] has been especially illustrious and enduring like this.
Yet as for those in recent times who speak of benevolence, I am perplexed by them. Indulging in excess to satisfy their nature, they hide behind unrestrained license, taking it to be authenticity, and so the moral standard is transgressed; harboring the wicked and associating with base men, they hide behind the breadth of the Way, taking it to be tolerance, and so moral distinctions are confused; wallowing in non-being and sinking into emptiness, they hide behind abstruse comprehension, taking it to be attainment, and so true substance is lost; hoisting factional banners and exalting their own insignia, they hide behind establishing the fundamental in order to set themselves up as the guiding standard, and thus daily [?] rush about in blind confusion without realizing it. If one seeks benevolence in this manner, does not benevolence grow more distant by the day? Alas! …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
人而不識仁者是捧土木之偶而未含神
情之靈者也爲仁而遠於人者是工鬼物
之畫而憚繪色象之顯者也又或詹詹然
惟訓釋名理而不務反躬默識猶之於人
也不思覿面考衷而徒拘拘於名氏稱謂
之辨析矣其如仁何哉夫子曰仁者人也
孟子曰仁人心也夫人而不仁則失其所
以爲心失其所以爲人也天下無無心之
人亦豈有不仁之人哉今試指其人曰是
===
無人心者也是非人也則必憤然仇怒謂
已之必爲人也旣知已之必爲人則必知
人必有心也而獨不知求仁以爲人也何
弗思之甚耶大抵天下之道言之匪艱行
之惟艱若吾閩四儒雖其所詣有淺深所
見有偏全其不畔孔孟之敎則均矣夫宛
丘之翮庚桑之壘流風猶足以被今後况
愚生生同其鄕日有感於先喆之爲者乎
實在所志耳彼玉之在璞抵擲則瓦石追
punctuated: 人而不識仁者，是捧土木之偶而未含神情之靈者也；爲仁而遠於人者，是工鬼物之畫而憚繪色象之顯者也。又或詹詹然惟訓釋名理，而不務反躬默識，猶之於人也，不思覿面考衷，而徒拘拘於名氏稱謂之辨析矣，其如仁何哉？夫子曰：「仁者，人也。」孟子曰：「仁，人心也。」夫人而不仁，則失其所以爲心，失其所以爲人也。天下無無心之人，亦豈有不仁之人哉？今試指其人曰：「是無人心者也，是非人也。」則必憤然仇怒，謂已之必爲人也。旣知已之必爲人，則必知人必有心也，而獨不知求仁以爲人也，何弗思之甚耶？大抵天下之道，言之匪艱，行之惟艱。若吾閩四儒，雖其所詣有淺深，所見有偏全，其不畔孔孟之敎則均矣。夫宛丘之翮、庚桑之壘，流風猶足以被今後，况愚生生同其鄕，日有感於先喆之爲者乎？實在所志耳。彼玉之在璞，抵擲則瓦石，追
translation_en: A human being who does not recognize humaneness is like one holding up an idol of clay and wood that lacks the vital spirit of expression and feeling; one who practices humaneness while distancing it from humanity is like an artist skilled at painting ghosts and monsters who shrinks from depicting the manifest forms of visible things. Still others chatter endlessly, merely glossing names and principles without striving for self-reflection and silent comprehension—just as, in dealing with a person, one might give no thought to meeting them face-to-face to examine their inner heart, and instead remain narrowly fixated on analyzing their names and titles. What has that to do with humaneness? The Master said, "Humaneness is to be human." Mencius said, "Humaneness is the human mind." Now, if a person is not humane, they lose that by which their mind is a mind, and lose that by which they are human. In all the world there is no person without a mind; how then could there be a person without humaneness? Suppose today you were to point at someone and say, "This person has no human mind; this is not a human being." They would surely flare up in resentful anger, insisting that they are most certainly human. Since they know that they are certainly human, they must know that a human being necessarily has a mind; yet they alone fail to know that they must seek humaneness in order to be human. How extreme is their lack of reflection! Generally speaking, with the Way in the world, speaking of it is not difficult, but practicing it is difficult. As for the four Confucian masters of our Fujian, although their attainments varied in depth and their insights varied in partiality or completeness, they were all alike in not departing from the teachings of Confucius and Mencius. Now, the plumes of Yuanqiu and the ramparts of Gengsang left lingering influences that were still sufficient to reach their contemporaries and posterity—how much more so for this foolish student, born in the very same native region and daily inspired by the deeds of those former sages! Everything truly depends on where one sets one's determination. Take jade within the uncut stone: if cast aside, it is mere tile and pebble, but if carved…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
琢則圭璋水之發源壅閼則汙泥疏濬則
川沼仁之於人亦若是已志之斯至夫何
遠哉惟執事進教之
第三問
黎時中
同考試官教諭蔣批字律二學人所鮮究子能
考據詳明品隲精當篇終尤得探本之意錄之
同考試官教諭張批是作條答字律甚悉至欲
重專官錄用專業之士誠考文正樂之不容緩者
===
考試官教諭丘批考古證今具見該贍之學
考試官教諭姚批學博詞古宜錄以式
聖人之化成天下者文也而非强作也觀
乎造化之理而已聖人之協和天下者聲
也而非人爲也得乎聲氣之元而已文明
之象顯于造化聖人效之而書契作焉中
和之氣涵於天地聖人則之而律呂制焉
是知天地者開聖人幾先之智也聖人者
成天地自然之能也制而用之謂之法推
punctuated:
琢則圭璋；水之發源，壅閼則汙泥，疏濬則川沼。仁之於人，亦若是已。志之斯至，夫何遠哉？惟執事進教之。

第三問
黎時中
同考試官教諭蔣批：字、律二學，人所鮮究。子能考據詳明，品隲精當，篇終尤得探本之意，錄之。

考試官教諭姚批：學博詞古，宜錄以式。

Benevolence in relation to man is just like this. Set your will upon it and it arrives—how could it be far off? May Your Excellency grant further instruction on this.

Third Policy Question
By Li Shizhong 黎時中

At the end of the essay, you especially grasp the meaning of tracing things back to their fundamental source. Selected for inclusion.

That by which the sages transform and perfect the world is writing, yet it is not something contrived by force; they simply observed the principles of nature's creation. That by which the sages bring harmony to the world is sound, yet it is not something made by human artifice; they simply grasped the primal origin of sound and vital energy (qi). When the emblems of civilization became manifest in nature's creation, the sages imitated them and written script was created; when the vital energy of equilibrium and harmony was contained within Heaven and Earth, the sages modeled themselves upon it and the standard pitch-pipes (lülü) were instituted.
