title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而行之謂之通神而化之使民宜之誠有
天運而人必從志一而氣自動者而可以
私智爲哉知此則王者制度考文之政
皇上法古宜今之治可得而言矣試因明問而
陳之粤自河洛效靈而圖書洩造化之祕
襄頡佐命而羲黄立制作之原奇字製於
沮誦大篆演於史籀而六書之法備焉考
文者所必稽也置緹室以候中氣截嵰竹
以定元聲而六律之音正焉審聲者所必
===
察也唐虞夏商損益不同而同律考文政
俗則一訪諸周官象胥以諭言語瞽史以
諭書名大事以漆書紀於竹簡小事以墨
書紀於布帛凡其掌故脩法而同天下之
文者何詳耶大師以掌序治政大胥以頒
樂合聲以十有二律爲之數度以十有二
聲爲之齊量凡其定律正音而和天下之
聲者何密耶周衰迹熄籍滅法湮古樂不
復作矣文獻無足徵矣孔子懼帝王之道
punctuated: 而行之謂之通，神而化之，使民宜之。誠有天運而人必從，志一而氣自動者，而可以私智爲哉？知此，則王者制度考文之政、皇上法古宜今之治，可得而言矣。試因明問而陳之。粤自河洛效靈，而圖書洩造化之祕；襄頡佐命，而羲黄立制作之原。奇字製於沮誦，大篆演於史籀，而六書之法備焉，考文者所必稽也。置緹室以候中氣，截嵰竹以定元聲，而六律之音正焉，審聲者所必察也。唐、虞、夏、商損益不同，而同律考文，政俗則一。訪諸《周官》，象胥以諭言語，瞽史以諭書名，大事以漆書紀於竹簡，小事以墨書紀於布帛，凡其掌故脩法而同天下之文者，何詳耶！大師以掌序治政，大胥以頒樂合聲，以十有二律爲之數度，以十有二聲爲之齊量，凡其定律正音而和天下之聲者，何密耶！周衰迹熄，籍滅法湮，古樂不復作矣，文獻無足徵矣。孔子懼帝王之道
translation_en:
…and carrying them out is called penetrative adaptability; making them numinous and transforming with them so that the people find them fitting. Truly, there is a heavenly movement that man must follow, and when the will is unified the vital force moves of itself—how could this be accomplished by private cleverness? Knowing this, the true king's governance of instituting measures and examining the written script, and Your Majesty's rule of modeling on antiquity while suiting the present, may now be discussed. Allow me to set this forth in response to the sagely question.

Ever since the Yellow River and the Luo River manifested their numinous efficacy, the Diagram and the Writing revealed the secrets of creation; Cangjie [transcribed 襄頡] assisted the mandate, and Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor established the origins of cultural creation. Unusual characters were devised by Jusong, the Great Seal script was elaborated by Historian Zhou (Shi Zhou), and thus the principles of the Six Categories of Script (liushu) were made complete—this is what those who examine the written script must needs investigate. Setting up the triple-walled chamber (tishi) to watch for the median qi, and cutting bamboo from MountXian [嵰竹] to fix the primal sound, the tones of the six yang pitch-pipes (liulü) were rectified—this is what those who scrutinize sounds must needs examine.

Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang differed in what they abridged and augmented, yet in unifying the pitch-pipes and examining the written script, their governance and customs were one. If we inquire into the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the Interpreter-clerks (xiangxu) made understood the spoken languages, and the Blind Historians (gushi) made understood the written character-names; great matters were recorded in lacquer writing on bamboo slips, and minor matters were recorded in ink writing on cloth and silk. In all their preserving of precedents and cultivating of institutions so as to unify the written script of the world, how detailed they were! The Grand Music Master (dashi) had charge of ordering the governance through music [? 掌序治政], and the Grand Music Assistant (daxu) distributed the musical duties and harmonized the sounds; they used the twelve pitch-pipes to establish the numerical measures, and the twelve tones to establish the equalized proportions. In all their fixing of the pitch-pipes and rectifying of the tones so as to harmonize the sounds of the world, how meticulous they were!

When the Zhou declined and the traces of the sages died out, the records were destroyed and the institutions submerged; ancient music was no longer performed, and written documents and worthy men were no longer sufficient to provide verification. Confucius feared that the Way of the Emperors and Kings…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
弗傳而禮樂之敎弗行也於是加筆削於
魯史之舊文正雅頌於殘失之詩章立百
王之軌範垂萬世之彛憲後有作者必取
衷是矣奈何秦不師古李斯變爲小篆程
邈省爲隷書而古文盡廢樂書燼於烈焰
世業散于疇人而鐘律盡亡坑焚之慘挾
偶之刑至今痛憤也漢光和中詔勒五經
于石而蔡邕書儀禮楊賜書魯詩馬日磾
書尚書堂谿典書春秋俱用古文而以八
===
分隷釋之是孔壁之古文猶可考見也晉
人尚草書唐人尚飛白宋元文人盡用晉
唐書法而碑帖之刻俱非科斗之文點畫
之多譌宜矣比者季本疑彤管非筆是未
深考周官之史職也漢建元時命樂官考
律而公孫卿治曆侍郎尊協度唐都分部
洛下閎運算俱用銅法而以太常掌之是
先王之律法猶能考求也吳楚失於輕浮
燕冀失於重濁唐宋取士拘於江左四聲
punctuated: 弗傳，而禮樂之敎弗行也。於是加筆削於魯史之舊文，正《雅》《頌》於殘失之詩章，立百王之軌範，垂萬世之彛憲，後有作者，必取衷是矣。奈何秦不師古，李斯變爲小篆，程邈省爲隷書，而古文盡廢；樂書燼於烈焰，世業散于疇人，而鐘律盡亡。坑焚之慘，挾偶之刑，至今痛憤也。漢光和中，詔勒《五經》于石，而蔡邕書《儀禮》，楊賜書《魯詩》，馬日磾書《尚書》，堂谿典書《春秋》，俱用古文，而以八分隷釋之，是孔壁之古文猶可考見也。晉人尚草書，唐人尚飛白，宋、元文人盡用晉、唐書法，而碑帖之刻俱非科斗之文，點畫之多譌，宜矣。比者季本疑彤管非筆，是未深考《周官》之史職也。漢建元時，命樂官考律，而公孫卿治曆，侍郎尊協度，唐都分部，洛下閎運算，俱用銅法，而以太常掌之，是先王之律法猶能考求也。吳、楚失於輕浮，燕、冀失於重濁，唐、宋取士拘於江左四聲，
translation_en: … would not be transmitted, and that the teachings of ritual and music would not be practiced. Thereupon he applied brush and knife to the old text of the History of Lu (Lu shi), rectified the "Odes" ("Ya") and "Hymns" ("Song") among the fragmentary and lost poetic pieces, established a model for a hundred kings, and handed down a constant standard for ten thousand generations; those who arose afterward necessarily took their standard from this. Yet how could it be that Qin did not model itself on antiquity? Li Si 李斯 changed the script into the small seal (xiaozhuan), Cheng Miao 程邈 simplified it into the clerical script (lishu), and the ancient script (guwen) was completely abolished; books on music were reduced to ashes in the fierce flames, hereditary professions were scattered among the hereditary specialists, and the bell pitch-standards were completely lost. The tragedy of burying scholars alive and burning books, and the punishments for possessing books or conversing together, arouse grief and indignation to this day. During the Guanghe reign period of the Han (178–184), an imperial decree ordered the Five Classics to be engraved on stone: Cai Yong 蔡邕 wrote out the Ceremonials and Rites (Yili), Yang Ci 楊賜 wrote out the Lu Odes (Lu shi), Ma Midi 馬日磾 wrote out the Book of Documents (Shangshu), and Tangxi Dian 堂谿典 wrote out the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). All used the ancient script and explained it in eight-tenths clerical script (bafen li); thus the ancient script from the wall of Confucius's house could still be examined and seen. Men of the Jin esteemed cursive script (caoshu), men of the Tang esteemed flying-white script (feibai), and literati of the Song and Yuan exclusively used the calligraphic methods of the Jin and Tang; since none of the engravings on steles and model-calligraphy rubbings were in tadpole characters (kedou zhi wen), it was only natural that there were many errors in dots and strokes. Recently Ji Ben 季本 doubted that the red tube (tongguan) was a writing brush; this was from not having deeply examined the scribal offices in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). During the Jianyuan reign period of the Han (140–135 BCE) [note: the reforms of Gongsun Qing et al. actually occurred in the Taichu period, 104 BCE], the music officials were ordered to examine the pitch-standards: Gongsun Qing 公孫卿 regulated the calendar, the Gentleman Attendant Zun 尊 harmonized the measures, Tang Du 唐都 divided the celestial Mansions, and Luoxia Hong 洛下閎 operated the counting rods; all used the bronze pitch-pipe method, and the Chamberlain for Ceremonials (Taichang) had charge of it, so the pitch-standard methods of the former kings could still be investigated and sought out. The speech of Wu and Chu erred in being light and floating, while that of Yan and Ji erred in being heavy and turbid; when the Tang and Song selected scholars, they were bound by the four tones of Jiangzuo (the lower Yangtze region), …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而河洛之人俱非中原之舊聲音之難辨
久矣比者李文利謂黃鐘最清是未深求
律呂之元聲也嗚呼今之時去漢愈遠矣
執事欲正楷隷之譌以復古法考律呂之
制以求元聲將何折衷哉甞觀劉原父之
筆說趙孟頫之筆經蓋深明書法之理而
悟運筆之妙者也得是人而辨論之則六
書之精蘊可得而襄頡之心法可契矣張
敔之解新書韓邦竒之輯全書蓋考究律
===
法之詳而明制作之理者也卽是書而參
考之則律呂之源委可知而音律之正變
可窮矣故吹律而知南風之不競者師曠
之聰也作訓纂而善倉頡之史篇者楊雄
之學也草茅巖穴之士安知無聰若師曠
學如楊雄者乎顧時之所用何如耳仰惟
我
聖祖稽古右文見韻書比類失倫聲音乖舛于
是
punctuated: 而河、洛之人俱非中原之舊，聲音之難辨久矣。比者李文利謂黃鐘最清，是未深求律呂之元聲也。嗚呼！今之時去漢愈遠矣。執事欲正楷、隷之譌以復古法，考律呂之制以求元聲，將何折衷哉？甞觀劉原父之《筆說》、趙孟頫之《筆經》，蓋深明書法之理而悟運筆之妙者也。得是人而辨論之，則六書之精蘊可得，而襄、頡之心法可契矣。張敔之解《新書》、韓邦竒之輯《全書》，蓋考究律法之詳而明制作之理者也。卽是書而參考之，則律呂之源委可知，而音律之正變可窮矣。故吹律而知南風之不競者，師曠之聰也；作《訓纂》而善《倉頡》之史篇者，楊雄之學也。草茅巖穴之士，安知無聰若師曠、學如楊雄者乎？顧時之所用何如耳。仰惟我聖祖稽古右文，見韻書比類失倫，聲音乖舛，于是
translation_en:
… while the people of the Yellow and Luo River regions were no longer those of the old Central Plains; thus the proper sounds and tones have long been difficult to distinguish. Recently, Li Wenli 李文利 claimed that the Yellow Bell (Huangzhong) pitch is the clearest and highest, which shows that he failed to deeply investigate the primordial sound of the twelve pitch-pipes (lülü).

Alas! Our present age is even further removed from the Han dynasty. Since Your Excellency wishes to correct the errors in regular and clerical scripts so as to restore the ancient methods, and to examine the system of the pitch-pipes so as to seek the primordial sound, by what standard shall we reach a balanced judgment? I have observed that Liu Yuanfu's (Liu Chang 劉敞) Discourse on the Brush (Bishuo) and Zhao Mengfu's 趙孟頫 Classic of the Brush (Bijing) deeply elucidate the principles of calligraphy and grasp the subtleties of wielding the brush. If we could obtain such men and discuss these matters with them, the profound essence of the Six Categories of Script (liushu) could be attained, and the mental methods of Shi Xiang 師襄 and Cang Jie 倉頡 could be matched. Zhang Yu's 張敔 explication of the New Treatise on Pitch-Pipes (Lülü xinshu) and Han Bangqi's 韓邦奇 compilation of the Complete Treatise (Yuanluo zhilü quanshu) thoroughly investigate the details of pitch-pipe regulations and clarify the principles of their creation. If we consult and cross-reference these books, the origins and developments of the pitch-pipes can be known, and the orthodox and variant forms of musical tones and pitches can be exhaustively understood.

Therefore, blowing the pitch-pipes and knowing that the southern melodies lacked vigor was due to the acute hearing of Music Master Kuang (Shi Kuang 師曠); composing the Compiled Glosses (Xunzuan) and excelling in the scribes' chapters of the Cangjie pian was due to the learning of Yang Xiong 揚雄. Among scholars living in rustic huts and mountain caves, how do we know there are none with hearing as acute as Shi Kuang's or learning like Yang Xiong's? It simply depends on how the present age employs them.

Looking up in reverence, I reflect that our Sacred Ancestor (Emperor Taizu) examined antiquity and esteemed culture. Seeing that the rhyme books arranged categories out of order and that their sounds and tones were erroneous and discrepant, he thereupon …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
命學士樂韶鳳宋濂等勒成洪武正韻其偏旁
之辨釋音韻之翻切分合增損之異宜俱
取證于毛晃而布之中外者秩秩乎中原
之正聲焉
命尚書詹同陶凱等製為
宴饗九奏樂章其始之本大初次之仰大明
終之樂清寧俱登歌于典樂而被之管絃
者渢渢乎大和之遺響焉
列聖相承至今用之迨我
===
===
皇上丕紹鴻基振揚
祖烈
宸翰奎畫之流播
聖心獨得之書法且有以妙契
皇祖之淵微而至治之薰蒸大化之融溢所謂
書同文而律和聲者誠于斯為盛矣執事
猶欲諧音律諭書名而以同文正樂之化
有望於
今日者豈以百年禮樂之期適逢其會乎愚
punctuated: 命學士樂韶鳳、宋濂等勒成《洪武正韻》，其偏旁之辨釋、音韻之翻切、分合增損之異宜，俱取證于毛晃，而布之中外者，秩秩乎中原之正聲焉。命尚書詹同、陶凱等製為《宴饗九奏樂章》，其始之《本大初》，次之《仰大明》，終之《樂清寧》，俱登歌于典樂而被之管絃者，渢渢乎大和之遺響焉。列聖相承，至今用之。迨我皇上丕紹鴻基，振揚祖烈，宸翰奎畫之流播，聖心獨得之書法，且有以妙契皇祖之淵微；而至治之薰蒸，大化之融溢，所謂「書同文」而「律和聲」者，誠于斯為盛矣！執事猶欲諧音律、諭書名，而以同文正樂之化有望於今日者，豈以「百年禮樂」之期適逢其會乎？愚
translation_en: …commanded the Academician Yue Shaofeng 樂韶鳳, Song Lian 宋濂, and others to compile the Hongwu Orthodox Rhymes (Hongwu zhengyun 洪武正韻). Its explanations and distinctions of character components, its fanqie 翻切 phonetic spellings of sounds and rhymes, and the varying appropriateness of dividing, merging, adding, or subtracting entries were all verified against the work of Mao Huang 毛晃; promulgated throughout the realm and beyond, it possesses in orderly fashion the orthodox pronunciation of the Central Plains. He also commanded the Minister Zhan Tong 詹同, Tao Kai 陶凱, and others to compose the Nine-Performance Musical Suites for State Banquets (Yanxiang jiu zou yuezhang 宴饗九奏樂章). Beginning with "Rooted in the Grand Primordium" (Ben Taichu 本大初), followed by "Looking Up to the Great Brilliance" (Yang Daming 仰大明), and concluding with "Rejoicing in Pure Tranquility" (Le Qingning 樂清寧), all were sung from the terrace by the Director of Music and set to winds and strings—resonant indeed with the lingering echoes of Supreme Harmony! Successive sacred emperors have inherited and maintained these, using them down to the present day. Now that Our Emperor has grandly succeeded to the great foundation and brilliantly exalted the achievements of his ancestors, the dissemination of his imperial brushwork and literary strokes—calligraphy uniquely attained by the sagely mind—moreover marvelously accords with the profound subtleties of the August Ancestor; meanwhile, through the permeating warmth of consummate governance and the overflowing abundance of great transformation, what are called "writing in uniform script" and "pitch-pipes harmonizing sounds" truly reach their flourishing peak right now! Yet Your Excellency still wishes to harmonize the musical pitches and issue instruction on the names of written characters, placing your hopes for the transformation of uniform script and rectified music in the present day—could it be because the time for "ritual and music to flourish after a hundred years" has justamente met its appointed juncture? In my humble…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
謂字學音律其理相通而其用相資也故
文同則音自正矣音正則律自諧矣欲同
今之文不必廢今之文也取楷書之文而
參古篆之義正者循之譌者釐之則今之
偏旁點畫皆古法也欲諧今之律不必求
之黍尺之間也密室覆緹截管實葭而黃
鐘之律定矣由是吹之而聲和候之而氣
應則音律自正而元聲可得也法由心得
待人而行今之鑄印有局也協律有官也
===
舉精於字律者而充之專其術業重其官
職海內之士不有聞風而起者乎郡縣社
學專設字律一科俾童而習焉長而用焉
勅督學憲臣歲校而高下之拔其尤者送部而
錄用焉俊秀之子不有專業而精識者乎
雖然朝廷者四方之極也君心者萬化之
原也君明樂官不明樂音心正則筆正心
和則氣和建中和之極以端制作之本者
惟在於
punctuated: 謂字學、音律，其理相通而其用相資也。故文同則音自正矣，音正則律自諧矣。欲同今之文，不必廢今之文也；取楷書之文而參古篆之義，正者循之，譌者釐之，則今之偏旁點畫皆古法也。欲諧今之律，不必求之黍尺之間也；密室覆緹，截管實葭，而黃鐘之律定矣。由是吹之而聲和，候之而氣應，則音律自正而元聲可得也。法由心得，待人而行。今之鑄印有局也，協律有官也，舉精於字律者而充之，專其術業，重其官職，海內之士不有聞風而起者乎？郡縣社學，專設字律一科，俾童而習焉，長而用焉；勅督學憲臣歲校而高下之，拔其尤者送部而錄用焉，俊秀之子不有專業而精識者乎？雖然，朝廷者，四方之極也；君心者，萬化之原也。君明樂官，不明樂音。心正則筆正，心和則氣和。建中和之極，以端制作之本者，惟在於
translation_en: … hold that the study of script and musical pitch share a common principle and mutually reinforce each other in practice. Therefore, when the script is unified, pronunciation naturally becomes correct; when pronunciation is correct, the pitches naturally harmonize. If one wishes to unify the script of today, there is no need to abolish today's script; if one takes the characters of standard script (kaishu) and consults the meanings of ancient seal script (guzhuan), following what is correct and rectifying what is erroneous, then today's radicals, dots, and strokes will all conform to ancient methods. If one wishes to harmonize the pitches of today, there is no need to seek them among millet grains and foot-measures; by hanging red silk curtains in a sealed chamber, cutting the pitch-pipes, and filling them with reed-membrane ash, the pitch of the Yellow Bell (Huangzhong) will be established. When blown from this basis, the sounds will harmonize, and when observed for seasonal pneuma (qi), the ethers will respond; thus the musical pitches will naturally be rectified and the primordial sound can be attained. Methods arise from the comprehension of the mind, yet they await capable men to be put into practice. Today there is a Service for Casting Seals (Zhuyin ju), and there are Music Directors (Xielü lang). If we recommend and appoint those well-versed in script and pitch to fill these posts, allowing them to specialize in their art and giving weight to their official positions, will not scholars throughout the empire rise up upon hearing of this trend? If in the community schools of prefectures and counties a curriculum in script and pitch is specially established so that youths practice it in childhood and apply it in adulthood; and if the Censorial Education Intendants are commanded by imperial order to examine and rank them annually, selecting the most outstanding to be sent to the Ministry for appointment, will not talented young men specialize in the study and attain refined discernment? Even so, the court is the standard for the four quarters, and the ruler's mind is the source of the myriad transformations. The ruler understands the officials of music, not the sounds of music. When the mind is upright, the brush is upright; when the mind is harmonious, the vital ether is harmonious. Establishing the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony so as to rectify the foundation of institutional creation lies solely in…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上之一心耳末學淺識不知所裁惟執事進
而教之
第四問
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批是作條答士習始末甚詳
而議論剴切詞氣古雅末段尤中肯綮宜錄以式
同考試官訓導李批教化風俗其道本相成也
此作論士習而歸重於教化是知作士之要者
考試官教諭丘批思古慨今之意委婉明切可以風矣
===
考試官教諭姚批灼見時敝而渾厚典雅佳哉
士習之日趨于敝也不獨其風會流也其
原始于世教衰而學術晦夫教化者上所
導也學術者下所明也今天下曷嘗不飭
度章號哉士曷嘗不談說賢聖脩皇王之
業哉顧其所為教為學者異何以知之蓋
教非布象魏申功令之謂也學非嫻文詞
驚空說之謂也大要在謹好尚崇道德而
感發之在誠意使上焉無的然之操姑襲
punctuated:
皇上之一心耳。末學淺識，不知所裁，惟執事進而教之。

第四問
陳文選
同考試官訓導蘇批：是作條答士習始末甚詳，而議論剴切，詞氣古雅，末段尤中肯綮，宜錄以式。
同考試官訓導李批：教化風俗，其道本相成也。此作論士習而歸重於教化，是知作士之要者。
考試官教諭丘批：思古慨今之意，委婉明切，可以風矣。
考試官教諭姚批：灼見時敝，而渾厚典雅，佳哉！

士習之日趨于敝也，不獨其風會流也，其原始于世教衰而學術晦。夫教化者，上所導也；學術者，下所明也。今天下曷嘗不飭度章號哉？士曷嘗不談說賢聖、脩皇王之業哉？顧其所為教、為學者異。何以知之？蓋教非布象魏、申功令之謂也；學非嫻文詞、驚空說之謂也。大要在謹好尚、崇道德，而感發之在誠意。使上焉無的然之操，姑襲
translation_en:
… the single mind of His Majesty alone. A junior scholar of shallow learning, I do not know how to judge these matters; I pray only that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me.

Fourth Policy Question
Chen Wenxuan 陳文選
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Su 蘇 comments: This essay answers point by point regarding the origins and development of literati customs in great detail. Its arguments are incisive and pertinent, its diction and tone are archaic and elegant, and the final paragraph hits the crucial point especially well. It should be recorded as a model.
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li 李 comments: Moral transformation through instruction and popular customs are mutually reinforcing in their principles. In discussing literati customs, this essay places ultimate emphasis on moral transformation, showing a grasp of the essentials of cultivating scholars.
Examiner Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: Its sentiments of reflecting on antiquity and lamenting the present are expressed with tactful subtlety and clear immediacy; it can serve to inspire and reform.
Examiner Instructor Yao 姚 comments: It shows keen insight into contemporary abuses while remaining substantial, generous, and classically elegant—admirable indeed!

That literati customs deteriorate day by day is not merely a matter of the drift of prevailing trends; its origin lies in the decline of moral instruction in the world and the obscuration of scholarly learning. Now, moral transformation is what those above guide; scholarly learning is what those below clarify. In the world today, when have regulations and proclamations ever failed to be strictly ordered and displayed? And when have scholars ever failed to discourse upon the worthies and sages or to cultivate the enterprises of sovereigns and kings? Yet what they actually practice as instruction and as learning is different. How do we know this? Because instruction does not mean merely posting laws on the palace gates and reiterating official regulations; learning does not mean merely mastering literary phrasing and dazzling people with empty theories. The essential point lies in being circumspect about what is favored and valued, revering morality and virtue, and inspiring people through sincerity of intention. If those above lack genuine and manifest integrity, and merely follow…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
虛文以行之下焉者知上之意不在是亦
相率承乎虛以應之欲風俗之厚士習之
善無時巳嗚呼此其弊寧獨閩哉乃執事
稟稟焉爲閩士計蓋將挽東南海濱之俗
以風天下愚生素狃于習者烏足以知此
語云新沐者必彈冠新浴者必振衣玆蓋
洗心滌慮時矣敢不掇所聞于故老者以
對粤昔唐虞交會岳牧夔龍稽首相讓雍
睦之化被于比屋三代盛時節儉正直之
===
風行于上潔白幽貞之操勵于下德義薰
蒸俗歸于厚迨夫殷士怙侈凌德蔑義用
周之治扶殷之衰故畢命曰政貴有恒辭
尚體要又曰世祿之家鮮克由禮誠欲迪
于古訓導之德義也昔人有言周之士也
貴秦之士也賤非特上貴之賤之也士亦
有自貴自賤焉今夫禮義廉耻可貴莫甚
焉媕婀蝓靡可賤莫甚焉人情孰不好貴
哉其流之趨卒不免處於賤者何上固無
punctuated:
虛文以行之，下焉者知上之意不在是，亦相率承乎虛以應之，欲風俗之厚、士習之善，無時巳。嗚呼！此其弊寧獨閩哉？乃執事稟稟焉爲閩士計，蓋將挽東南海濱之俗以風天下。愚生素狃于習者，烏足以知此？語云：「新沐者必彈冠，新浴者必振衣。」玆蓋洗心滌慮時矣，敢不掇所聞于故老者以對！
粤昔唐、虞交會，岳、牧、夔、龍稽首相讓，雍睦之化被于比屋。三代盛時，節儉正直之風行于上，潔白幽貞之操勵于下，德義薰蒸，俗歸于厚。迨夫殷士怙侈，凌德蔑義，用周之治扶殷之衰，故《畢命》曰：「政貴有恒，辭尚體要。」又曰：「世祿之家，鮮克由禮。」誠欲迪于古訓，導之德義也。昔人有言：「周之士也貴，秦之士也賤。」非特上貴之、賤之也，士亦有自貴、自賤焉。今夫禮義廉耻，可貴莫甚焉；媕婀蝓靡，可賤莫甚焉。人情孰不好貴哉？其流之趨，卒不免處於賤者，何？上固無
translation_en:
… empty formalities in carrying it out, then those below, knowing that the true intentions of their superiors do not lie therein, will likewise follow one another in responding with empty formalities; under such conditions, there will never come a time when one can expect customs to become generous and the habits of scholars to become good. Alas! Is this abuse unique to Fujian alone? Yet Your Excellency shows such reverent concern in taking counsel for the scholars of Fujian, doubtless intending to turn back the customs of this southeastern seashore so as to influence the entire realm. How could an ignorant student like myself, long accustomed to prevailing habits, be equal to knowing this? Still, as the saying goes, "He who has just washed his hair always dusts off his cap; he who has just bathed always shakes out his robes." Now is indeed the moment to cleanse the heart and purify one's thoughts; how could I dare not gather what I have heard from the elders by way of reply!

Long ago, at the juncture of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, the Four Peaks, the Twelve Pastors, Kui, and Long bowed their heads to the ground and yielded to one another, and the transforming influence of harmony and concord reached every household side by side. In the flourishing ages of the Three Dynasties, an ethos of frugality and uprightness prevailed above, while conduct of pure integrity and quiet constancy was encouraged below; steeped in virtue and righteousness, customs returned to generosity. When it came to the scholars of Yin, who relied on extravagance, spurned virtue, and disdained righteousness, the governance of Zhou was used to remedy the decline of Yin. Thus the Charge to Bi (Bi ming) says: "In government, consistency is prized; in proclamations, substance and conciseness are esteemed." And it says: "Among families of hereditary emolument, few are able to follow propriety." Truly, the desire was to guide them by ancient precepts and lead them into virtue and righteousness. People of old had a saying: "The scholars of Zhou were noble; the scholars of Qin were base." It was not merely that those above made them noble or made them base; scholars also made themselves noble or base. Now then, nothing is more worthy of esteem than propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame; nothing is more despicable than indecisive pandering and indolent extravagance. In human nature, who does not love what is noble? Why is it, then, that the drift of current tendencies ultimately cannot avoid ending up in what is base? It is because those above truly have no…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
以迪之而士鮮自立也且以閩士論之自
漢以迄于今凡幾變矣晉族遷安衣冠始
萃八姓入閩人物遞興常衮建學厥有文
章於是歐陽詹之徒出與中原士埒宋渡
而南吾道星纏諸儒林立有稱齒爲上國
者有謂海濱鄒魯者東南文物宣洩盡矣
明興文治精華人才衍庶當時元公翊運匡謨
豐功駿烈藏于盟府後先相望莫可殫述
逮至成弘間
===
國家淳龐之氣鬱而未散
累朝熙洽之澤溢而方流士相率被敎化明道
術或顯而赴響希會或微而素履考祥咸
恂恂爾雅悃實總之不詭乎道戶傳詩禮
家寶清白士甘鶉結官矢羔羊時則有若
蔡清周瑛黃鞏黃仲昭陳茂烈陳真晟諸
賢或以理學名或以氣節顯或以孝行聞
或以恬退著其大歸於樂道貞志是故有
洞晰經學咏歌一貫隨事檢心家貧或貸
punctuated: 以迪之，而士鮮自立也。且以閩士論之，自漢以迄于今，凡幾變矣。晉族遷安，衣冠始萃；八姓入閩，人物遞興。常衮建學，厥有文章；於是歐陽詹之徒出，與中原士埒。宋渡而南，吾道星纏，諸儒林立，有稱齒爲上國者，有謂海濱鄒魯者，東南文物，宣洩盡矣。明興，文治精華，人才衍庶。當時元公翊運匡謨，豐功駿烈，藏于盟府，後先相望，莫可殫述。逮至成、弘間，國家淳龐之氣鬱而未散，累朝熙洽之澤溢而方流。士相率被敎化、明道術，或顯而赴響希會，或微而素履考祥，咸恂恂爾雅、悃實，總之不詭乎道。戶傳詩禮，家寶清白，士甘鶉結，官矢羔羊。時則有若蔡清、周瑛、黃鞏、黃仲昭、陳茂烈、陳真晟諸賢，或以理學名，或以氣節顯，或以孝行聞，或以恬退著，其大歸於樂道貞志。是故有洞晰經學，咏歌一貫，隨事檢心，家貧或貸
translation_en:
…with which to guide them, and the scholars rarely stand on their own feet. Moreover, let us consider the scholars of Fujian (Min). From the Han dynasty down to the present day, how many transformations have they undergone! When the clans of the Jin dynasty migrated and settled in peace, gentry attire first gathered here; when the Eight Surnames entered Fujian, men of talent successively arose. When Chang Gun established schools, literary culture flourished; thereupon men like Ouyang Zhan emerged, rivaling the scholars of the Central Plains. When the Song court crossed to the south, our Way shone like a constellation of stars and Confucian scholars stood thick as a forest. Some praised Fujian as ranking among the premier states, while others called it the Zou and Lu of the seashore; the cultural splendor of the southeast was thus brought forth in full.

With the rise of the Ming, the essence and splendor of civil governance caused men of talent to multiply in abundance. At that time, great statesmen assisted the dynastic destiny and offered corrective counsels; their bountiful achievements and illustrious deeds are preserved in the archives of the Hall of Covenants, following one upon another in unbroken succession, more than can be fully recounted. Coming down to the Chenghua (1465–1487) and Hongzhi (1488–1505) eras, the pure and magnanimous ethos of the state remained rich and undissipated, and the harmonious and pervasive grace of successive reigns overflowed and spread far and wide. Scholars one after another received moral transformation and clarified the art of the Way. Whether prominent, answering the call of the times to meet a rare opportunity, or obscure, treading their plain path and examining signs of good fortune, all were modest, refined, and sincerely upright—in short, never deviating from the Way. Households transmitted the Odes and the Rites, families treasured pure integrity, scholars were content in patched garments like quails, and officials swore by the incorruptibility of the "Lambskin" ode. At that time there were worthies such as Cai Qing 蔡清, Zhou Ying 周瑛, Huang Gong 黃鞏, Huang Zhongzhao 黃仲昭, Chen Maolie 陳茂烈, and Chen Zhensheng 陳真晟. Some were famed for their Neo-Confucian learning of Principle, some were distinguished for their moral courage, some were renowned for their filial conduct, and some were noted for their serene retirement; their overarching aim lay in delighting in the Way and keeping their aspirations pure. Therefore, there were those who thoroughly penetrated classical learning, sang of the "one thread binding all," examined their minds in every affair, and, when their families were poor, sometimes borrowed…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
于人以自給者矣有先後抗疏落職杜門
著述力不能具筆劄辦薪米者矣有躬耕
養母懇疏辭祿短床敝席出則自執蓋者
矣有聞有司防察過嚴歸不復應舉布衣
終身者矣羣公際泰隆之會脩上世之業
履大道之經植不朽之行童而習之老而
安焉宜其風之淳俗之厚如是及乎嘉隆
以來文運益斌斌盛矣乃論者不免有過
計焉曰前輩崇雅道勵志清脩廉靖寡欲
===
矣今也得無有居服奢僭昏喪踰越務豐
殖而事淫靡者乎前輩陳胷臆闚說世務
奧衍剴切矣今也得無有緣飾纖華希徼
榮利舍肯綮而拾巵詞者乎前輩慎名檢
攄忠讜隆孝養體道脩身矣今也得無有
飾容市譽拂經背禮矯以為廉訐以為直
者乎前輩悟正學時省克視險如夷知命
樂天矣今也得無有秉心褊躁甘心脂韋
銖銖于較計營營于儇狡者乎數者有一
punctuated: 于人以自給者矣；有先後抗疏落職，杜門著述，力不能具筆劄、辦薪米者矣；有躬耕養母，懇疏辭祿，短床敝席，出則自執蓋者矣；有聞有司防察過嚴，歸不復應舉，布衣終身者矣。羣公際泰隆之會，脩上世之業，履大道之經，植不朽之行，童而習之，老而安焉，宜其風之淳、俗之厚如是！及乎嘉、隆以來，文運益斌斌盛矣，乃論者不免有過計焉。曰：前輩崇雅道，勵志清脩，廉靖寡欲矣；今也得無有居服奢僭，昏喪踰越，務豐殖而事淫靡者乎？前輩陳胷臆，闚說世務，奧衍剴切矣；今也得無有緣飾纖華，希徼榮利，舍肯綮而拾巵詞者乎？前輩慎名檢，攄忠讜，隆孝養，體道脩身矣；今也得無有飾容市譽，拂經背禮，矯以為廉，訐以為直者乎？前輩悟正學，時省克，視險如夷，知命樂天矣；今也得無有秉心褊躁，甘心脂韋，銖銖于較計，營營于儇狡者乎？數者有一于斯，…
translation_en:
…from others in order to sustain themselves; there were those who, one after another, submitted defiant memorials and were stripped of office, shutting their doors to write books while lacking the means even to procure brushes and paper or provide for firewood and rice; there were those who farmed with their own hands to support their mothers, earnestly memorializing to decline official salaries, sleeping on short beds and worn mats, and holding their own parasols when going out; and there were those who, hearing that the authorities' surveillance and inspection of examination candidates were overly severe, returned home never to sit for the examinations again, remaining commoners in coarse cloth for the rest of their lives. Those gentlemen encountered an era of supreme prosperity, cultivated the undertakings of antiquity, trod the constant path of the Great Way, and established imperishable conduct. Practicing it in youth and resting content in it in old age, how fitting it was that their ethos was so pure and their customs so generous!

Coming down to the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras and since, the flourishing of literary culture has grown ever more refined and abundant; yet commentators cannot help entertaining anxious forebodings. They say: Our predecessors revered the orthodox Way, set their minds on pure cultivation, and were incorruptible, tranquil, andof few desires; today, could there not be those who are extravagant and presumptuous in dwelling and dress, who transgress the bounds in weddings and funerals, and who devote themselves to amassing wealth and indulging in dissipation? Our predecessors laid bare their innermost thoughts and examined and discussed the affairs of the world in ways that were profound, expansive, and incisive; today, could there not be those who embellish with petty華 floridity, angle for glory and profit, and abandon the crucial points to pick up adaptable, empty words? Our predecessors were circumspect regarding their reputation and conduct, set forth loyal and forthright counsel, exalted filial care, and embodied the Way in cultivating their persons; today, could there not be those who put on false appearances to buy fame, go against the constant principles and violate ritual, affect austerity to pass as incorruptible, and expose others' secrets to pass as upright? Our predecessors comprehended orthodox learning, constantly engaged in self-examination and self-mastery, regarded perilous circumstances as level ground, understood destiny, and rejoiced in Heaven; today, could there not be those who harbor narrow and restless minds, willingly grease and soften themselves to flatter others, haggle over every ounce, and bustle about in slick cunning? If even one of these several ills…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
于斯是習壞之矣反之不可不亟也今夫
雕鏤爲器錯以五采比其用也不任黍實
寧木毋飾寧嗇毋侈忍性動心以需大受
語曰澹泊以明志寧靜以致遠是儉素當
崇也鉤棘以爲竒割裂以爲古競相記習
珍若球琅識者厭之布帛菽粟之爲文也
純然有正色冲乎有餘味語曰編之乎詩
書而不愧措之乎天地而不疑是文體當
釐也逢衣淺帶禹行舜趨始乎盜名終乎
===
亂德將安藉乎力田孝第不言躬行循德
而蹈時至則化語曰懷忠信以待舉力行
以待取是實行當脩也辨材度德膚完腹
蠹雖有合抱弗顧之矣虛名取容器小任
重實鮮中積僨轅敗犁語曰弓調然後求
勁馬服然後求良士慤然後求智是心術
當正也雖然此未可盡責之士也教化者
朝廷之急務廉恥者士人之美節上有教化
而後士人有廉恥士有廉恥而後天下有
punctuated: 于斯，是習壞之矣，反之不可不亟也。今夫雕鏤爲器，錯以五采，比其用也，不任黍實。寧木毋飾，寧嗇毋侈，忍性動心，以需大受。語曰：「澹泊以明志，寧靜以致遠。」是儉素當崇也。鉤棘以爲竒，割裂以爲古，競相記習，珍若球琅，識者厭之。布帛菽粟之爲文也，純然有正色，冲乎有餘味。語曰：「編之乎《詩》、《書》而不愧，措之乎天地而不疑。」是文體當釐也。逢衣淺帶，禹行舜趨，始乎盜名，終乎亂德，將安藉乎？力田孝第，不言躬行，循德而蹈，時至則化。語曰：「懷忠信以待舉，力行以待取。」是實行當脩也。辨材度德，膚完腹蠹，雖有合抱，弗顧之矣。虛名取容，器小任重，實鮮中積，僨轅敗犁。語曰：「弓調然後求勁，馬服然後求良，士慤然後求智。」是心術當正也。雖然，此未可盡責之士也。教化者，朝廷之急務；廉恥者，士人之美節。上有教化，而後士人有廉恥；士有廉恥，而後天下有
translation_en:
… in these respects, it means that customs have corrupted them, and reversing this cannot but be treated as urgent. Now, suppose one carves and engraves a vessel and inlays it with the five colors; when it comes to practical use, it cannot even hold a measure of millet. Better to be plain wood than ornate; better to be frugal than extravagant—enduring in one's nature and stirring one's mind so as to await great responsibilities. As the saying goes: "Through simple living one clarifies one's ambition; through tranquility one reaches afar." Thus, frugality and simplicity ought to be esteemed.

Taking crooked and thorny phrasing as marvelous, and fragmented writing as archaic, scholars compete to memorize and imitate such styles, treasuring them like fine jade—yet men of discernment despise them. Writing that is like plain cloth and silk or beans and grain is pure in its proper color and harmonious with lingering savor. As the saying goes: "Compile it alongside the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu) and there is no shame; set it forth between Heaven and Earth and there is no doubt." Thus, literary style ought to be rectified.

Wearing loose robes and narrow sashes, walking like Yu and striding like Shun—beginning by stealing a reputation and ending by confounding virtue—what use can be made of such men? Working diligently in the fields, practicing filial piety and fraternal submission, acting in person without empty words, and treading the path of virtue leads to transformation when the time comes. As the saying goes: "Cherish loyalty and trustworthiness while awaiting recommendation; strive in conduct while awaiting selection." Thus, substantive conduct ought to be cultivated.

In judging timber and measuring virtue, if the bark is intact but the core is worm-eaten, even a tree a full span in girth will not be given a second glance. Seeking favor through an empty reputation, having small capacity yet bearing a heavy charge, and lacking inner substance will overturn the carriage shafts and ruin the plow. As the saying goes: "Only after a bow is well-adjusted does one seek strength in it; only after a horse is broken in does one seek excellence in it; only after a scholar is sincere does one seek wisdom in him." Thus, the disposition of the mind ought to be made upright.

Even so, the blame for this cannot be placed entirely upon the scholars. Moral transformation through education is the urgent business of the court; a sense of integrity and shame is the fine virtue of the scholar. Only when there is moral transformation from above do scholars possess a sense of integrity and shame; only when scholars possess a sense of integrity and shame does the realm possess …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
風俗其道恒相成焉是故興起之機在士
轉移之權在上不觀之射乎設侯布鵠比
德較力期以百步則以百步中期以五十
步則五十步中下者上所率也又不觀之
市乎轉販盈縮與時貴賤一巧售則百巧
競進一素售則百素騰踊下者上所倡也
方今
聖天子作新于上求賢之
詔歲煩幾下津津乎端士習正文體為言一時
===
名公卿內外百執事咸兢兢奉
德意申飭化導甚備海澨山谷潜伏之士莫不
鼓舞更新蓋上之精神意氣周遍融液達
于罔極故感奮若是亦非獨閩也夫明德
彰敎覺朦聵而新之者
主上之惠也刋文還質應風雲而趨之者學士
之烈也有
君如此寧忍負之執事毋過慮焉
第五問
punctuated:
風俗，其道恒相成焉。是故興起之機在士，轉移之權在上。不觀之射乎？設侯布鵠，比德較力，期以百步則以百步中，期以五十步則五十步中，下者上所率也。又不觀之市乎？轉販盈縮，與時貴賤，一巧售則百巧競進，一素售則百素騰踊，下者上所倡也。方今聖天子作新于上，求賢之詔歲煩幾下，津津乎端士習、正文體為言。一時名公卿、內外百執事，咸兢兢奉德意，申飭化導甚備。海澨山谷潜伏之士，莫不鼓舞更新。蓋上之精神意氣，周遍融液，達于罔極，故感奮若是，亦非獨閩也。夫明德彰敎，覺朦聵而新之者，主上之惠也；刋文還質，應風雲而趨之者，學士之烈也。有君如此，寧忍負之？執事毋過慮焉。
第五問
translation_en:
…customs; the two principles constantly complement each other. Therefore, the impetus for rising up lies with the scholars, while the power to transform and redirect lies with those above. Do we not see this in archery? When the target and bull's-eye are set up to compare virtue and test strength, if the requirement is set at a hundred paces, they hit the mark at a hundred paces; if the requirement is set at fifty paces, they hit the mark at fifty paces—those below follow the lead of those above. And do we not see this in the marketplace? As peddling and trade expand or contract, and as prices rise or fall with the times, if a single piece of ornate craftsmanship sells well, then a hundred ornate pieces vie to come forward; if a single plain item sells well, then a hundred plain items surge in price—those below follow the example initiated by those above.

At present, the Sacred Son of Heaven fosters renewal from above. Edicts seeking worthy men are repeatedly handed down year after year, earnestly speaking of rectifying literati customs and correcting literary style. At this time, renowned grandees and ministers, along with all the officials inside and outside the capital, reverently uphold His virtuous intentions, issuing admonitions and guiding transformation with great thoroughness. Among the scholars living in seclusion along the sea coasts and in the mountain valleys, there are none who are not inspired to renew themselves. Indeed, the spirit and vitality of the ruler above permeate everywhere, reaching to the farthest bounds; that they are so moved and roused to action is not unique to Fujian alone. To clarify virtue and manifest moral teaching, awakening the blind and deaf and renewing them—this is the grace of the Sovereign above. To pare away華ornamentation and return to substance, hastening forward in response to the opportune winds and clouds—this is the meritorious enterprise of the scholars. Having a ruler such as this, how could we bear to fail Him? Your Excellency need not be overly concerned about this.

Fifth Question

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批籌海防者不激即泛是
篇陳閩廣島嶼要害具悉至論練兵擇將尤卓有成畫
同考試官教諭張批諸士談時務多疎窘鋪
叙而具經略劑量而中機宜者僅見此篇
考試官教諭丘批條畫周詳用世之學
考試官教諭姚批文章經濟俱優
夫謀臣石畫平居欽欽慮變變發若無事
然何也未變而預圖正所以變發而不懾
===
也閩固多故之地也頃海波不揚閭閻安
堵
天子之鐘鼓實式靈之然居豐者以蔀屋爲慮
審勢者以唇齒爲憂東廣之地與閩相錯
逋寇遞起竟未有大創之者此豈直廣患
閩亦患之矣古者各君其國猶相救恤以
畏簡書況今一統
明天子詎有漠然眡鄰竟秦越哉屢奉
明旨會勦特于南澳設重鎮以連兩省之聲援
punctuated:
龔廷賓
同考試官教諭熊批：「籌海防者，不激即泛。是篇陳閩、廣島嶼要害具悉，至論練兵擇將，尤卓有成畫。」
同考試官教諭張批：「諸士談時務多疎窘，鋪叙而具經略，劑量而中機宜者，僅見此篇。」
考試官教諭丘批：「條畫周詳，用世之學。」
考試官教諭姚批：「文章、經濟俱優。」
夫謀臣石畫，平居欽欽慮變，變發若無事然，何也？未變而預圖，正所以變發而不懾也。閩固多故之地也，頃海波不揚，閭閻安堵，天子之鐘鼓實式靈之。然居豐者以蔀屋爲慮，審勢者以唇齒爲憂。東廣之地與閩相錯，逋寇遞起，竟未有大創之者。此豈直廣患？閩亦患之矣。古者各君其國，猶相救恤，以畏簡書；況今一統明天子，詎有漠然眡鄰竟秦越哉？屢奉明旨會勦，特于南澳設重鎮，以連兩省之聲援。
translation_en:
Gong Tingbin 龔廷賓
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiong 熊 comments: "Those who plan for coastal defense are either overly drastic or overly vague. This essay sets forth the strategic points of the islands of Fujian and Guangdong in full detail, and when it comes to discussing training troops and selecting generals, it possesses an especially outstanding and well-formed plan."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: "When the various scholars discuss current affairs, they are mostly sketchy and constrained; only in this essay do we see an account that lays things out while possessing strategic vision, and weighs matters while hitting upon the right course of action."
Examiner and Instructor Qiu 丘 comments: "Its itemized plans are comprehensive and detailed—learning of practical use to the world."
Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: "Both its literary composition and its statecraft are superior."
Now, as for the rock-solid plans of counseling ministers: in ordinary times they are anxiously concerned about crises, yet when a crisis breaks out they act as though nothing were happening. Why is this? Planning ahead before a crisis occurs is precisely why one is unafraid when a crisis does break out. Fujian is inherently a land of many troubles. Recently the sea waves have not risen, and the common people in their neighborhoods have lived in peace and security; the bells and drums of the Son of Heaven have truly lent their numinous efficacy to this. Yet one who dwells in abundance takes the shaded hovels [referring to the hexagram Feng 豐 in the Book of Changes] as a concern, and one who examines the strategic situation takes the interdependence of lips and teeth as a worry. The territory of eastern Guangdong interlocks with Fujian; fugitive pirates arise there in succession, and in the end no one has dealt them a heavy blow. How could this be merely a calamity for Guangdong? Fujian also suffers from it. In antiquity, when each ruler governed his own state, they still rescued and aided one another out of awe for the bamboo dispatches [of the king]; how much more so today under an enlightened Son of Heaven of a unified realm—how could we indifferently look upon our neighbor's territory as though we were distant Qin and Yue? Repeatedly we have received explicit imperial decrees for joint suppression, and a major garrison has been specially established at Nan'ao 南澳 in order to link the mutual support of the two provinces. …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫寇辟則鹿也閩人掎之廣人角之相與
踣之有何不克第詳廣海島嶼甚多故逋
逃如搏景緩則鵰搶急則告撫廣亦明知
其詐而姑羈維之幸無大縱非直我閩之
師勢難越擊已也且自嘉隆來首難無慮
數十皆連艘數百橫行廣海而犯閩烽火
者一焉夫入犯之衝首南澳次銅山次浯
嶼次南日小埕烽火今寨遊舟師鱗次櫛
比非復曩時之比扼其上游則閩海內地
===
可無慮矣至于外島可略而言在漳曰南
澳在泉曰彭湖在興曰湄洲在福曰海壇
夫南澳有重鎮矣海壇有遊兵矣湄洲在
目睫之間亦無所伏姦矣脫有侵軼而竊
據者其彭湖乎夫彭湖遠在海外去泉二
千餘里其山迂迴有三十六小嶼羅列如
排衙然內澳可容千艘又周遭平山為障
止一隘口進不得方舟令賊得先據所謂
一人守險千人不能過者也矧山外多礁
punctuated: 夫寇辟則鹿也，閩人掎之，廣人角之，相與踣之，有何不克？第詳廣海島嶼甚多，故逋逃如搏景，緩則鵰搶，急則告撫。廣亦明知其詐而姑羈維之，幸無大縱，非直我閩之師勢難越擊已也。且自嘉、隆來，首難無慮數十，皆連艘數百，橫行廣海，而犯閩烽火者一焉。夫入犯之衝，首南澳，次銅山，次浯嶼，次南日、小埕、烽火。今寨遊舟師鱗次櫛比，非復曩時之比；扼其上游，則閩海內地可無慮矣。至于外島，可略而言：在漳曰南澳，在泉曰彭湖，在興曰湄洲，在福曰海壇。夫南澳有重鎮矣，海壇有遊兵矣，湄洲在目睫之間，亦無所伏姦矣；脫有侵軼而竊據者，其彭湖乎？夫彭湖遠在海外，去泉二千餘里，其山迂迴，有三十六小嶼，羅列如排衙然。內澳可容千艘，又周遭平山為障，止一隘口，進不得方舟，令賊得先據，所謂「一人守險，千人不能過」者也。矧山外多礁，
translation_en: Now, pirates may be compared to a deer: if the men of Fujian seize it by the hind legs and the men of Guangdong take it by the horns, bringing it down together, how could they fail to prevail? Yet if one examines the waters of Guangdong closely, there are very many islands and islets, so that hunting down fugitives there is like clutching at shadows: when pressure relaxes, they swoop down and plunder like hawks; when hard-pressed, they sue for pacification. Guangdong, too, clearly knows their deceit, yet for the time being keeps them on a loose rein, counting itself fortunate if they do not break out on a large scale—it is not merely that our Fujian forces find it difficult by the nature of the situation to cross over and strike them. Moreover, since the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras, the ringleaders who have risen in revolt number no fewer than several dozen; all of them linked hundreds of vessels together to rampage across the seas of Guangdong, whereas only a fraction ever raided the Fenghuo signaling sector in Fujian. Now, among the strategic avenues of incursion, the first is Nan'ao, next is Tongshan, next is Wuyu, and next are Nanri, Xiaocheng, and Fenghuo. Today the naval forces of the stockades and roving squadrons are arrayed as closely as fish scales and comb teeth, no longer comparable to bygone days; by holding the upper reaches against them, the coastal interior of Fujian may be free from worry. As for the outer islands, one may speak of them in brief: in Zhangzhou there is Nan'ao, in Quanzhou there is Penghu (the Pescadores), in Xinghua there is Meizhou, and in Fuzhou there is Haitan. Now, Nan'ao already has a major garrison command, Haitan has roving troops, and Meizhou lies right before our eyes and eyelashes, leaving nowhere for villains to lurk; if by chance invaders should spill over and stealthily occupy a base, would it not be Penghu? Now, Penghu lies far out overseas, more than two thousand li from Quanzhou; its hills wind roundabout, with thirty-six small islets arrayed like officials lined up at court. Its inner bay can hold a thousand vessels, and all around flat hills serve as a screen, leaving only a single narrow entrance through which ships cannot advance abreast; should the pirates manage to occupy it first, it would be a case of what is called "one man holding a pass, whom a thousand men cannot get past." How much more so when outside the hills there are many reefs, …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
風汛不常吾之戰艦難久泊矣而曰可以
攻者否也往居民恃險為不軌乃徙而虛
其地今不可以民實之明矣若分兵以守
則兵分者於法為弱遠輸者於法為貧且
絕島孤懸混茫萬頃脫輸不及而援後時
是委軍以予敵也而曰可以守者否也亦
嘗測其水勢沈舟則不盡其深輸石則難
扞其急而曰可以塞者亦非也夫地利我
與賊共者也塞不可守不可攻又不可則
===
將委之乎惟謹脩內治而已法曰佚能勞
之飽能饑之賊之所資者糧食所急者硝
磺也惟峻接濟之防而敦陳整旅以需其
至則賊既失其所恃而海上軍事又絕不
相聞雖舳艫軋芴詎能為久頓謀哉以我
之逸待賊之勞以我之飽待賊之饑稍逼
內地則或給接濟以掩禽或假漁商而襲
擊此營平致敵之術也法有不以兵勝而
以計困者此之謂也於戲接濟勾引患非
punctuated:
風汛不常，吾之戰艦難久泊矣，而曰可以攻者，否也。往居民恃險為不軌，乃徙而虛其地，今不可以民實之，明矣。若分兵以守，則兵分者於法為弱，遠輸者於法為貧；且絕島孤懸，混茫萬頃，脫輸不及而援後時，是委軍以予敵也，而曰可以守者，否也。亦嘗測其水勢，沈舟則不盡其深，輸石則難扞其急，而曰可以塞者，亦非也。夫地利，我與賊共者也。塞不可，守不可，攻又不可，則將委之乎？惟謹脩內治而已。法曰：「佚能勞之，飽能饑之。」賊之所資者糧食，所急者硝磺也。惟峻接濟之防，而敦陳整旅以需其至，則賊既失其所恃，而海上軍事又絕不相聞，雖舳艫軋芴，詎能為久頓謀哉？以我之逸，待賊之勞；以我之飽，待賊之饑。稍逼內地，則或給接濟以掩禽，或假漁商而襲擊，此營平致敵之術也。法有不以兵勝而以計困者，此之謂也。
於戲！接濟、勾引，患非
translation_en:
…and the winds and tides are unpredictable, making it difficult for our warships to anchor there for long. Thus, to say that it can be attacked is wrong. In the past, the inhabitants relied on its natural barriers to engage in lawlessness, so they were relocated and the land was left vacant; it is clear that we cannot populate it with civilians today. If we divide our troops to garrison it, according to the rules of military art, dividing forces leads to weakness, and transporting supplies over long distances leads to impoverishment. Moreover, it is an isolated island suspended alone amidst ten thousand頃 of boundless sea; should supplies fail to arrive in time and reinforcements come too late, that would be abandoning our army to the enemy. Thus, to say that it can be defended is also wrong. Its water conditions have also been sounded: sinking boats will not fill its depth, and dumping stones can hardly stem its swift currents. Thus, to say that it can be blocked up is wrong as well. Now, geographical advantage is something shared by both ourselves and the pirates. If it cannot be blocked, cannot be defended, and cannot be attacked either, shall we then simply abandon it to them? We should only attend carefully to our internal governance. The military classic says: "If the enemy is at ease, be able to exhaust him; if he is well-fed, be able to starve him." What the pirates rely upon is grain, and what they urgently need is saltpeter and sulfur. Only by strictly enforcing the defenses against illicit supplying, while arraying our formations and readying our troops to await their coming, will the pirates lose what they depend upon and be completely cut off from intelligence of our naval affairs. Even if their vessels are crowded tightly together, how could they plan for a prolonged stay? With our ease, we await the pirates' exhaustion; with our abundance, we await the pirates' hunger. When they draw slightly closer to the mainland, we can either feign providing supplies in order to ambush and capture them, or disguise our men as fishermen and merchants to launch a surprise attack—this was the Marquis of Yingping's (Zhao Chongguo 趙充國) art of drawing in the enemy. When the rules of war speak of winning not by force of arms but by cornering the enemy through stratagem, this is what is meant.

Alas! The evils of illicit supplying and collusive luring have existed for no…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
一日矣漳民航海商夷其本業也自
先朝過禁遂致勾倭釀成禍府邇者假充餉之
名寓弭盜之術請開海禁意誠善矣然亦
以東南夷不爲中國患故云不謂日本之
狡黠也窮宼無聊又安知不出於勾引計
乎大抵閩廣地勢雖稍稍殊而通夷市海
同骫法嗜利亦同廣禁而閩弛則閩爲逋
藪閩禁而廣弛則廣爲逋藪安南私泊于
閩蔡佛保流毒於廣其已事可鑒已夫蚊
===
虻啙膚手不期而摶其痛一也同舟而遇
風波雖夷貉之子同心而共濟者其患一
也謂宜齊禁周防協和并力何憂乎姦氓
何畏乎逋宼哉執事曰治盜之筴非勦則
撫愚謂此非兩事也不勦而撫則其就撫
也不固不散而聚則其養禍也滋深故議
勦議撫當先議兵閩兵有水有陸水獨用
土著以土人習水非吳越人可望也陸則
土客兼用土有五璧客有六璧幾相半矣
punctuated:
一日矣。漳民航海商夷，其本業也。自先朝過禁，遂致勾倭，釀成禍府。邇者假充餉之名，寓弭盜之術，請開海禁，意誠善矣；然亦以東南夷不爲中國患故云，不謂日本之狡黠也。窮宼無聊，又安知不出於勾引計乎？大抵閩、廣地勢雖稍稍殊，而通夷市海同，骫法嗜利亦同。廣禁而閩弛，則閩爲逋藪；閩禁而廣弛，則廣爲逋藪。安南私泊于閩，蔡佛保流毒於廣，其已事可鑒已。夫蚊虻啙膚，手不期而摶，其痛一也；同舟而遇風波，雖夷貉之子，同心而共濟者，其患一也。謂宜齊禁周防，協和并力，何憂乎姦氓？何畏乎逋宼哉？

執事曰：「治盜之筴，非勦則撫。」愚謂此非兩事也。不勦而撫，則其就撫也不固；不散而聚，則其養禍也滋深。故議勦議撫，當先議兵。閩兵有水有陸：水獨用土著，以土人習水，非吳、越人可望也；陸則土、客兼用，土有五璧，客有六璧，幾相半矣。
translation_en:
… a single day. For the people of Zhangzhou (漳), sailing the seas to trade with foreign peoples is their primary livelihood. Ever since the previous reigns imposed overly strict maritime prohibitions, it led them to collude with the Japanese pirates (Wo 倭), brewing a hotbed of disaster. Recently, under the pretext of replenishing military provisions while embodying a strategy to quell piracy, officials petitioned to lift the maritime prohibitions. The intention was truly good; yet this was proposed only because the foreigners of the Southeast were not then a menace to China—it did not reckon with the cunning craftiness of Japan. When desperate bandits have nothing left to rely on, how do we know they will not resort to schemes of collusion and enticement? On the whole, although the terrain of Fujian (Min 閩) and Guangdong (Guang 廣) differs slightly, their intercourse with foreigners and maritime trading are the same, and their bending of the law and greed for profit are also the same. If Guangdong enforces prohibitions while Fujian relaxes them, then Fujian becomes a haven for fugitives; if Fujian enforces prohibitions while Guangdong relaxes them, then Guangdong becomes a haven for fugitives. Annam (安南) privately anchoring in Fujian, and Cai Fobao (蔡佛保) spreading his poison across Guangdong—these past events serve as a clear warning. Now, when mosquitoes and gadflies bite the skin, the hands strike at them without prior coordination, because the pain is one and the same; when men in the same boat encounter wind and waves, even if they are the sons of Yi and Mo tribes, they unite their hearts to cross together, because the peril is one and the same. I say that the provinces ought to unify their prohibitions, make defense comprehensive, and cooperate with combined strength—what worry then would there be over traitorous commoners, and what fear of fugitive bandits?

You, sir, ask: “As for the strategy of dealing with bandits, if it is not extermination, then it is pacification.” In my humble view, these are not two separate matters. If one pacifies them without first striking them down, their submission to pacification will not be firm; if they are allowed to remain gathered rather than dispersed, the disaster thereby nurtured will grow ever deeper. Therefore, in deliberating over extermination or pacification, one must first deliberate over the troops. The troops of Fujian include both naval and land forces. The navy exclusively employs native locals, because the locals are accustomed to the water in a way that men from Wu (吳) and Yue (越) cannot hope to match. On land, both local troops and guest troops are used together; the local troops have five camps [?] (bi 璧) and the guest troops have six camps [?], making them nearly half and half. …

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
若謂客兵必當去則前此閩人壺漿迎之
者誰也若謂土兵必可用則異時興難嘯
呼者又誰也創往禍者曰沿海勾引之姦
多有詐稱應募者籍之爲兵得無虞其漏
師爲變者乎似非過計也審時務者又曰
此屬易與爲亂則孰若部之爲兵而令就
約束乎亦一策也然而終未探其本也以
愚私臆兵不必土客顧練之何如爾今之
浙兵非復昔日素練之舊矣且浙非無事
===
區也卒然軍興奈兵不可借何故練土者
遠畫募客者權宜也然以未試之土著而
遽去聲敵之客兵萬一有警土著不支誰
尸其咎哉孫子曰將者國之輔也輔周則
國强陸宣公亦云用兵之道在乎將得其
人得其人則狙詐咸作使不得其人則狙
詐咸作敵有一淮陰市人皆精卒矣有一
忠簡盜賊皆義旅矣今土著所以不可恃
者多緣將之非人故練之無法耳今誠嚴
punctuated: 若謂客兵必當去，則前此閩人壺漿迎之者誰也？若謂土兵必可用，則異時興難嘯呼者又誰也？創往禍者曰：「沿海勾引之姦，多有詐稱應募者，籍之爲兵，得無虞其漏師爲變者乎？」似非過計也。審時務者又曰：「此屬易與爲亂，則孰若部之爲兵，而令就約束乎？」亦一策也。然而終未探其本也。以愚私臆，兵不必土客，顧練之何如爾。今之浙兵，非復昔日素練之舊矣，且浙非無事區也，卒然軍興，奈兵不可借何？故練土者遠畫，募客者權宜也。然以未試之土著，而遽去聲敵之客兵，萬一有警，土著不支，誰尸其咎哉？《孫子》曰：「將者，國之輔也；輔周則國强。」陸宣公亦云：「用兵之道，在乎將得其人。得其人，則狙詐咸作使；不得其人，則狙詐咸作敵。」有一淮陰，市人皆精卒矣；有一忠簡，盜賊皆義旅矣。今土著所以不可恃者，多緣將之非人，故練之無法耳。今誠嚴
translation_en: If one says that guest troops must be dismissed, then who was it that the people of Min previously welcomed with jugs of drink? If one says that local troops can certainly be employed, then who was it that at another time stirred up trouble and shouted in mutiny? Those chastened by past disasters say: "Among the treacherous elements along the coast who collude with enemies, many falsely claim to respond to recruitment; if we register them as soldiers, how can we not worry that they might leak military secrets and stage a mutiny?" This does not seem to be an excessive concern. Yet those who assess current affairs say: "Since this sort is easily drawn into rebellion, what is better than organizing them into troops and making them submit to discipline?" This too is one policy. Yet in the end, neither probes the root of the matter. In my humble opinion, troops need not be distinguished as local or guest; it simply depends on how they are trained. Today's Zhejiang troops are no longer the well-trained veterans of days past; moreover, Zhejiang is not a region free of trouble—if military emergencies suddenly arise there, what will we do when their troops cannot be borrowed? Therefore, training local troops is a long-term plan, while recruiting guest troops is a temporary expedient. Yet if we rely on untested local natives and abruptly dismiss the guest troops whose reputation overawes the enemy, should an alarm arise in one case out of ten thousand and the local natives fail to hold out, who will bear the blame? Master Sun (Sunzi) said: "The general is the bulwark of the state; if the bulwark is complete, the state is strong." Duke Xuan of Lu (Lu Zhi 陸贄) also said: "The way of employing troops lies in obtaining the right men as generals. When one obtains the right men, even the cunning and deceitful can all be put to use; when one fails to obtain the right men, the cunning and deceitful all become enemies." With a single Marquis of Huaiyin (Han Xin 韓信), men from the marketplace all became elite soldiers; with a single Duke Zhongjian (Zong Ze 宗澤), bandits and thieves all became righteous brigades. Today, the reason local natives cannot be relied upon is mostly because the generals are not the right men, and thus there is no method in their training. If today we truly make strict…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
督責之令精綜覈之鏡視各部將果曉暢
軍事者優遇之否則懲之果和輯士心者
久任之否則亟去之果守約遵令實心訓
練者卽謗書盈篋必傾心誠信之而剥衆
夤緣者卽操三尺法之庶幾將率而下人
人畏威懷德平時旣有投石超距之風臨
敵試有衝鋒陷陣之績則土亦何謝於客
然後漸次汰客方爲萬全此尚需以歲月
非今日事也於戲擊陸寇易擊海寇難撲
===
初發之寇易撲久玩之寇難收一方之寇
易收兩省之寇難迂疎之見特談兵之常
爾乃若隨機制勝神明不窮自有
廟算在
punctuated: 督責之令，精綜覈之鏡，視各部將，果曉暢軍事者，優遇之；否則懲之。果和輯士心者，久任之；否則亟去之。果守約遵令、實心訓練者，卽謗書盈篋，必傾心誠信之；而剥衆夤緣者，卽操三尺法之。庶幾將率而下，人人畏威懷德。平時旣有投石超距之風，臨敵試有衝鋒陷陣之績，則土亦何謝於客？然後漸次汰客，方爲萬全。此尚需以歲月，非今日事也。於戲！擊陸寇易，擊海寇難；撲初發之寇易，撲久玩之寇難；收一方之寇易，收兩省之寇難。迂疎之見，特談兵之常爾。乃若隨機制勝，神明不窮，自有廟算在。
translation_en:
…orders of supervision and accountability, and sharpen the mirror of comprehensive verification. Observe the commanders of each unit: if they are truly well-versed in military affairs, treat them generously; otherwise, punish them. If they truly harmonize and win the hearts of the soldiers, keep them long in their posts; otherwise, swiftly remove them. If they truly abide by regulations, obey orders, and train their troops with genuine dedication, then even if baskets are filled with slanderous letters against them, trust them whole-heartedly; whereas those who fleece their men and curry favor for advancement should be dealt with according to the three-foot statutes of the law. In this way, from the commanders on down, everyone will stand in awe of authority and cherish virtue. When in peacetime they already display the spirit of hurling stones and leaping over barriers, and when facing the enemy they prove to have the merit of charging the vanguard and breaking the lines, how then would the local troops be any inferior to the guest troops? Only after this should the guest troops be gradually pared away—that alone is the completely safe course. Yet this still requires the passage of months and years; it is not something that can be done today.

Alas! Striking land bandits is easy, while striking sea bandits is difficult; stamping out newly arisen bandits is easy, while stamping out bandits who have long grown insolent is difficult; rounding up the bandits of a single region is easy, while rounding up the bandits of two provinces is difficult. These pedantic andremote views of mine are merely the commonplaces of military discussion. As for adapting to circumstances to achieve victory with inexhaustible and godlike subtlety, that rests with the plans of the Imperial Court.

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
萬曆己卯秋福建舉鄉試事
既竣有司錄諸士之文以
獻龍雲不佞從諸執事後乃敢
申於多士曰爾多士亦知所
以預是舉者乎亦知所以無
負主司責期之厚矣乎夫多
===
士之所進文也所明經學也
所論者古今時事也異日徵
之用則措之天下國家也
國朝陋前代詞賦之制專以經
術取士士必通經然後庸以
施于政固以業經學成可致
用也故皆養之學校而一之
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

萬曆己卯秋，福建舉鄉試。事既竣，有司錄諸士之文以獻。龍雲不佞，從諸執事後，乃敢申於多士曰：爾多士亦知所以預是舉者乎？亦知所以無負主司責期之厚矣乎？夫多士之所進，文也；所明，經學也；所論者，古今時事也；異日徵之用，則措之天下國家也。國朝陋前代詞賦之制，專以經術取士。士必通經，然後庸以施于政，固以業經學成，可致用也。故皆養之學校，而一之…
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the jimao year of the Wanli era (1579), Fujian held its Provincial Examination. Once the proceedings were concluded, the authorities compiled the essays of the scholars to present to the throne. Unworthy though I, Long Yun 龍雲, am, having followed behind the various officiating functionaries, I venture to set forth these words to the many scholars: Do you scholars truly understand why you have been selected in this examination? Do you truly understand how not to fail the generous expectations and responsibilities placed upon you by the examiners? Now, what you scholars have presented is literary composition; what you have elucidated is classical learning; what you have discussed are ancient, modern, and contemporary affairs; and when one day this is tested in practical employment, it will be applied to the realm and the state. Our dynasty disdained the system of poetic compositions used in former eras and selects scholars exclusively through mastery of the Classics. A scholar must thoroughly understand the Classics before he is employed in governance, surely because once one's study of the Classics is accomplished, it can be put to practical use. Therefore, all are nurtured in schools and unified…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
於科目龍雲嘗伏覩
聖祖諭侍臣有曰人才必養之於
未用之先用之於旣成之後
譬之稼豫耕則有穫又以明
道德通世務爲文之要深怪
險僻雕刻浮藻爲文之病
聖謨丕顯二百餘年來道化日新
===
我
皇上嗣服卽申飭學政以端示向
往達之天下莫不改易觀聽
矧八閩固夙稱海濱鄒魯乎
蓋自常衮興學之後宋諸大
儒輩出閩之士知所向方舊
矣今
punctuated: 於科目。龍雲嘗伏覩聖祖諭侍臣有曰：「人才必養之於未用之先，用之於旣成之後。譬之稼，豫耕則有穫。」又以明道德、通世務爲文之要，深怪險僻、雕刻、浮藻爲文之病。聖謨丕顯，二百餘年來道化日新。我皇上嗣服，卽申飭學政以端示向往，達之天下，莫不改易觀聽，矧八閩固夙稱「海濱鄒魯」乎？蓋自常衮興學之後，宋諸大儒輩出，閩之士知所向方舊矣。今
translation_en:
…through the examination categories. I, Long Yun 龍雲, once humbly read where the Sacred Progenitor (Emperor Taizu) instructed his attending ministers, saying: "Men of talent must be nurtured before they are employed, and employed after their education is complete. It is like farming: if one plows in advance, there will be a harvest." He also held that clarifying morality and understanding worldly affairs are the essentials of writing, while deeply deploring obscure eccentricity, over-elaborate carving, and superficial floridity as the maladies of writing. The sacred counsels have shone brightly, and for over two hundred years moral transformation has been renewed day by day.

When Our Sovereign Emperor succeeded to the throne, he immediately reiterated instructions on educational administration so as to set forth the proper direction to follow. Reached by this throughout the realm, there was no one whose outlook and hearing were not transformed—how much more so in the Eight Prefectures of Fujian (Bamin 八閩), long acclaimed as the "Zou and Lu on the Seashore" (Haibin Zou Lu 海濱鄒魯)! Indeed, ever since Chang Gun 常衮 promoted education in the Tang, and great Confucian scholars emerged in succession during the Song, the literati of Fujian have long known the proper direction to pursue. Now…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
文教洋溢章縫之徒徧于寰區
凡髫齔之童幼而習之家塾
者無異于郷學國學學于郷
學國學者卽以試有司對
明廷居官任職無所不可諸士
誠私淑先賢陶成于
運隆化洽之日也可不知所自
===
乎顧
上籲俊尊
帝孜孜焉思得真才實德以共治
理龍雲不能不有大懼焉蓋
天下日事末學趨於華靡久
矣今所望者乃在篤行躬脩
之士龍雲非敢謂
punctuated: 文教洋溢，章縫之徒徧于寰區。凡髫齔之童，幼而習之家塾者，無異于郷學、國學；學于郷學、國學者，卽以試有司，對明廷，居官任職，無所不可。諸士誠私淑先賢，陶成于運隆化洽之日也，可不知所自乎？顧上籲俊尊帝，孜孜焉思得真才實德以共治理，龍雲不能不有大懼焉。蓋天下日事末學，趨於華靡久矣，今所望者，乃在篤行躬脩之士。龍雲非敢謂
translation_en: …civilizing education overflows, and scholars in ritual caps and robes are found throughout the realm. Even young children with tufted hair and losing their milk teeth, learning from youth in family schools, study what is no different from that in the local schools and the Directorate of Education; and those who study in the local schools and the Directorate of Education are thereby ready to be examined by the authorities, to reply before the enlightened court, and to hold office and fulfill official duties—there is nothing for which they are unsuited. You scholars have truly modeled yourselves privately after the former worthies and been molded to maturity in an age of flourishing fortune and pervasive transformation; how could you fail to know whence this comes? Yet when the Sovereign above summons men of eminence to honor the Supreme Ruler, tirelessly seeking to obtain men of true talent and solid virtue with whom to share in governance and order, I, Long Yun 龍雲, cannot but feel great trepidation. For the world has daily busied itself with superficial learning and tended toward florid extravagance for a long time; what is hoped for today lies rather in scholars of earnest conduct and personal cultivation. I, Long Yun, would not dare to say that…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
國家培養未至多士心術盡或
頗也間有負
作人至意竄端匿跡獲厠於其
間則是進末學而崇華靡主
司任之也
明旨申飭之謂何徒使人以科目
不能得人為多士誚是非主
===
司所望于爾多士也龍雲聞
之山之高而雲霧興焉水之
深而蛟龍產焉君子道德之
厚而文章著焉多士皆占一
經而據理敷詞至談時務讜
論嘉猷疊出主司操量衡而
程槩之謂終身所建立足信
punctuated: 國家培養未至，多士心術盡或頗也。間有負作人至意，竄端匿跡，獲厠於其間，則是進末學而崇華靡，主司任之也。明旨申飭之謂何？徒使人以科目不能得人為多士誚，是非主司所望于爾多士也。龍雲聞之，山之高而雲霧興焉，水之深而蛟龍產焉，君子道德之厚而文章著焉。多士皆占一經而據理敷詞，至談時務，讜論嘉猷疊出，主司操量衡而程槩之，謂終身所建立足信
translation_en:
… the dynasty’s nurturing has not yet sufficed, or that the dispositions of heart among the many scholars are all perchance skewed. Yet if occasionally there are those who betray the supreme intent of cultivating talent, concealing their true nature and hiding their tracks to gain a place among the successful candidates, then this amounts to advancing superficial learning and exalting华華靡 (flowery extravagance)—and the responsibility for it falls upon the chief examiners! What then becomes of the explicit imperial decrees repeatedly enjoining caution? It would merely cause people to fault the many scholars by saying that the examination system fails to obtain true men of talent. This is not what the chief examiners hope for from you, the many scholars.

Longyun has heard it said: where the mountain is high, clouds and mists arise; where the water is deep, flood-dragons are bred; where the gentleman’s moral virtue is profound, his literary compositions shine forth. You scholars each specialize in one of the Classics and set forth your words grounded in principle; when it comes to discussing current affairs, forthright arguments and fine counsels emerge one after another. The chief examiners hold the scales and measures to evaluate and weigh them, believing that what you will establish throughout your entire lives can be trusted…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
於此也寧意猶有不然者乎
今夫刻鏤土木以為果餌飾
之丹青而文以金繒雜沓賓
筵見者莫不悅之求其實不
可嚐也辨白黑者瞭然于目
而別矣有瞽師焉其言白黑
若得其情至授以質則懵然
===
也彼徒勦浮論夷考其行無
一與所言相當者何異瞽師
言白黑乎殆于果餌之飾可
悅而不可食者類也夫士學
古之學至錄於上之人乃不
以所學為世用奚以文為今
多士以計偕應試南宮行且
punctuated: 於此也。寧意猶有不然者乎？今夫刻鏤土木以為果餌，飾之丹青，而文以金繒，雜沓賓筵，見者莫不悅之，求其實，不可嚐也。辨白黑者瞭然于目而別矣；有瞽師焉，其言白黑若得其情，至授以質，則懵然也。彼徒勦浮論，夷考其行，無一與所言相當者，何異瞽師言白黑乎？殆于果餌之飾，可悅而不可食者類也。夫士學古之學，至錄於上之人，乃不以所學為世用，奚以文為？今多士以計偕應試南宮，行且
translation_en: …in this. Could one ever suspect that it might turn out otherwise? Now suppose someone carves clay and wood to make fruits and pastries, painting them in red and green and adorning them with gold and silk, and sets them out in profusion at a banquet for guests; everyone who sees them is delighted, yet if one seeks their substance, they cannot be tasted. Those who distinguish black from white see the difference clearly with their eyes; yet suppose there is a blind music-master who speaks of black and white as though he grasps their true nature, but when handed the actual objects, is utterly bewildered. As for those who merely plagiarize superficial theories, when one calmly examines their conduct and finds that not a single thing corresponds to what they have said, how do they differ from a blind music-master speaking of black and white? They are virtually of the same kind as those ornamental fruits and pastries that are pleasing to look at yet inedible. When a scholar studies the learning of antiquity, to the point of being selected and recorded by his superiors, and yet fails to put what he has learned to practical use in the world, what good is literary composition? Now the many gentlemen are traveling with the provincial tribute accounts to sit for the examination at the Ministry of Rites (Nangong), and soon will…

title: 萬曆七年福建鄉試錄
text:
奉
廷對第進士顧主司未敢以是
爲厚幸獨惟遭時自見宜知
所以振厲而祓滌維新庶他
日效於實用天下國家有攸
賴也則是錄號爲得人矣語
曰馬服知驥劔斫知鋼主司
===
將藉是以稱塞多士勗乎哉
河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣
儒學敎諭丘龍雲謹序
punctuated:
奉廷對，第進士。顧主司未敢以是爲厚幸，獨惟遭時自見，宜知所以振厲而祓滌維新，庶他日效於實用，天下國家有攸賴也，則是錄號爲得人矣。語曰：「馬服知驥，劔斫知鋼。」主司將藉是以稱塞，多士勗乎哉！
河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣儒學敎諭丘龍雲謹序。
translation_en:
…receive the Palace Examination, and qualify as metropolitan graduates (jinshi). Yet the examiners dare not regard this alone as great good fortune; rather, having met with the right times to manifest themselves, the candidates ought to know how to rouse their spirits, cleanse themselves, and make themselves anew, so that in the future they may prove effective in practical application and the empire and the state may have something to rely upon—only then will this record truly be acclaimed as having obtained the right men. As the saying goes: "By hitching a horse to a carriage one knows a thoroughbred; by hacking with a sword one knows fine steel." The examiners will rely on this to fulfill their responsibility. May the many scholars exert themselves!

Respectfully written as a postface by Qiu Longyun 丘龍雲, Instructor of the Confucian School of Luoshan County in Xinyang Department, Runing Prefecture, Henan.
